Our framework applies to a broad class of conformal iterated function systems indexed by lattice points, including those associated with the Hurwitz continued fraction, and transfers positive-density combinatorial patterns to digit sets while preserving the maximal Hausdorff dimension. As applications, we obtain fractal counterparts of the multidimensional and polynomial Szemer\'edi theorems, as well as their relativized versions yielding a counterpart of the multidimensional Green--Tao theorem.

arxiv:2610.37125.title: Enumeration of zero-sum subsequences: A proof of Bialostocki-Lotspeich conjecture
arxiv:2610.37125.summary: Let $C_n$ be a cyclic group of order $n\ge 2$, and let $S=g_1\cdot\ldots\cdot g_{\ell}$ be a sequence over $C_n$, with repetitions allowed. We denote by $\mathsf N_0^n(S)$ the number of subsets $I\subseteq[1,\ell]$ with $|I|=n$ and $\sum_{i\in I}g_i=0$. A conjecture proposed by Bialostocki and Lotspeich in 1992 states that $$\mathsf N_0^n(S)\ge \binom{\lfloor |S|/2\rfloor}{n}+ \binom{\lceil |S|/2\rceil}{n}.$$ Several partial results toward this conjecture are known.

arxiv:2610.37136.title: On additive bases of finite abelian groups
arxiv:2610.37136.summary: Let $G$ be a finite abelian group, let $p$ be the smallest prime divisor of $|G|$, and let $c_0(G)$ be the least integer $t$ such that every regular sequence over $G$ of length at least $t$ is an additive basis. Additive bases have been extensively studied in additive combinatorics, and the exact value of $c_0(G)$ has been determined for many groups of rank at least three and some groups of rank two (in which case groups of the form $C_p\oplus C_{pn}$ turn out to be exceptional). In this paper, we continue the study of $c_0(G)$ and obtain the following results.

arxiv:2610.37163.title: Maximal geometric quotients of flag varieties
arxiv:2610.37163.summary: We introduce the notion of maximal geometric quotient, namely a geometric quotient of a polarized pair under a torus action which has a birational contraction to any other GIT quotient. For the action of the maximal torus on a complete flag variety, we show that a maximal geometric quotient exists and it is a Mori dream space, and its Cox ring is isomorphic to the Cox ring of the flag variety. We discuss birational properties of the maximal geometric quotients, their relations with the Chow quotients and explain how to construct them for maximal torus actions on flag varieties.
arxiv:2610.37163.authors: Lorenzo Barban, Michele Bianco, Luis E. Sol\'a Conde

arxiv:2610.37167.title: Notes on efficient dominating sets and efficient open dominating sets in circulant graphs
arxiv:2610.37167.summary: Let $D$ be a proper subset of $\mathbb{Z}_n$ such that $|D|$ divides $n$ and is relatively prime to $\frac{n}{|D|}$. We first establish a necessary and sufficient condition for $D$ to be an efficient dominating set of some circulant graph $\Cay(\mathbb{Z}_n,S)$. Moreover, for an inverse-closed subset $S$ of $\mathbb{Z}_n\setminus\{0\}$ such that $|S|+1$ divides $n$ and is relatively prime to $\frac{n}{|S|+1}$, we give a necessary and sufficient condition for the existence of efficient dominating sets in $\Cay(\mathbb{Z}_n,S)$.

arxiv:2610.37173.title: Optimal path decompositions of sparse random graphs
arxiv:2610.37173.summary: Let $\operatorname{odd}(G)$ be the number of odd-degree vertices of a graph $G$. We prove that, if $p=o(1)$ and $np/\log n\to\infty$, then with probability tending to one the random graph $G(n,p)$ has an edge decomposition into exactly $\operatorname{odd}(G)/2$ paths. This confirms a conjecture of Glock, K\"uhn and Osthus from 2016.

arxiv:2610.37184.title: Representations of shifted quantum affine algebras and cluster algebras II: Non simply-laced types and cluster expansions
arxiv:2610.37184.summary: We extend our previous results on cluster structures in the Grothendieck rings of categories $\mathcal{O}^{\mathrm{sh}}$ for shifted quantum affine algebras to the non-simply laced types. We also show that, for all types, the formal power series expressions of the cluster monomials in terms of classes of positive prefundamental representations can be regarded as limits of cluster expansions, thus establishing their positivity.
arxiv:2610.37184.authors: Christof Geiss, David Hernandez, Bernard Leclerc

arxiv:2610.37207.title: A nilpotent version of the first Kac conjecture
arxiv:2610.37207.summary: We derive a formula for the nilpotent Kac polynomial and define an explicit generalized Kac-Moody Lie algebra (by generators and relations) and conjecture that its graded dimensions recover the constant terms of the nilpotent Kac polynomial. We outline empirical evidence supporting the conjecture and prove it for two special classes of quivers: quivers without oriented cycles except loops and quivers with "negative enough" Euler form.

arxiv:2610.37208.title: Counting and Sampling Git Graphs
arxiv:2610.37208.summary: Version Control Systems, like Git and Mercurial, represent the history of a project as a Directed Acyclic Graph, capturing divergences and merges throughout development. A widely adopted workflow, the feature branch workflow, imposes a particularly simple structure: a single main branch and features branches evolving in parallel without interfering with one another. This work presents an enumerative study of these Git graphs.

arxiv:2610.37246.title: Non-convergence in heterogeneous Hegselmann-Krause dynamics: The bounded influence model
arxiv:2610.37246.summary: In a recent preprint, we found counterexamples to a number of auxiliary conjectures in a 2012 paper of Mirtabatabaei and Bullo, concerning convergence in two fundamental models of heterogeneous Hegselmann-Krause dynamics, the synchronized bounded confidence (SBC) and synchronized bounded influence (SBI) models. Building on our work, Etesami and Touri presented an example of an opinion vector which doesn't converge under SBC dynamics, resolving the main conjecture from the 2012 paper in that case. Here we complete this project by presenting an example of an opinion vector which doesn't converge under SBI dynamics.
arxiv:2610.37246.authors: Peter Hegarty, Damiano Ognissanti, Edvin Wedin

arxiv:2610.37273.title: Effective Gromov-Witten computations for GKM spaces and a semisimple application
arxiv:2610.37273.summary: We report a major update to our original software GKMtools and record multiple improvements in the computation of Gromov--Witten invariants of GKM spaces. This includes a refined divisor equation that reduces the complexity from exponential to linear in the number of marked points, three tricks to accelerate the computation of curve class relations in the GKM graph, and an implementation of Mihalcea's algorithm for homogeneous varieties using the equivariant quantum Chevalley formula. As an application, we prove that the small quantum cohomology of the type-$E$ generalized Grassmannians $E_7/P_2,E_7/P_4,E_7/P_5,E_8/P_6$ is generically semisimple.

arxiv:2610.37291.title: Non-split groups of Lie type and iSchur algebras with unequal parameters
arxiv:2610.37291.summary: We present a geometric framework for realizing quantum Schur algebras with unequal parameters, via constructible sheaves on flag varieties arising from non-split groups of Lie type. In the special cases of general unitary groups and minus-type orthogonal groups, this framework yields the iSchur algebras with unequal parameters, which are closely related to the quasi-split iquantum groups of type AIII. Such a geometric realization enables the construction of canonical bases, integral forms, and monoidal categorification for these unequal-parameter iSchur algebras and the corresponding iquantum groups.
arxiv:2610.37291.authors: Li Luo, Rui Song, Yang Yang

arxiv:2610.37315.title: The maximum size of intersecting $k$-graphs with covering number $k$
arxiv:2610.37315.summary: Let $m(k)$ be the maximum size of an intersecting $k$-graph with covering number $k$. In the present paper, it is proved that for all $k>e^{32}$, \[ m(k)\ge k^k\exp\bigl(-50\sqrt{k\log k}\bigr). \] Together with Zakharov's upper bound \cite{Z}, this implies $m(k)=k^k\exp\bigl(-k^{1/2+o(1)}\bigr)$.
arxiv:2610.37315.authors: Peter Frankl, Jian Wang, Yaoran Yang, Yutong Zhang

arxiv:2610.37317.title: Localization of weighted Goldman volume on $\mathrm{SL}(3,\R)$-Hitchin Component
arxiv:2610.37317.summary: We compute Goldman volume on the moduli space of convex real projective structures on a closed oriented surface of genus at least two, with exponential weight defined by the shifted Blaschke area. For every positive parameter, the integral converges and is a finite sum of inverse powers of that parameter. Its coefficients are intersection numbers involving the bundle of regular cubic differentials on the moduli stack of stable curves.

arxiv:2610.37351.title: Toric Varieties from Multiple Zeta Values
arxiv:2610.37351.summary: The linear relations among fixed weight multiple zeta values (MZVs) are a well-studied subject in number theory. Elements of putative linear bases for this fixed-weight space are, however, not algebraically independent; they satisfy non-linear relations. We study these relations by approximating them through motivic MZVs, formal MZVs and numerical computations.
arxiv:2610.37351.authors: Annika Burmester, Steven Charlton, Abhiram Kidambi, Felix Lotter, Rosa Prei{\ss}

arxiv:2610.37372.title: Stationary Coexistence in Stochastic Gause Systems with General Trophic Responses
arxiv:2610.37372.summary: We study stationary coexistence in stochastic Gause predator-prey systems with independent multiplicative environmental noise and trophic responses depending on both population densities. A weighted population balance cancels the trophic interaction and yields moments of order greater than one without imposing predator self-regulation. These estimates give a direct occupation-measure proof of a sufficient coexistence criterion based on prey establishment and predator invasion of the prey-only stationary environment.
arxiv:2610.37372.authors: Andr\'es S\'anchez, Leon A. Valencia, Jorge M. Ramirez Osorio

arxiv:2610.37392.title: The K-property of equilibrium states for systems with non-uniform structure
arxiv:2610.37392.summary: In this paper, we develop a general criterion for the K-property of equilibrium states within the Climenhaga-Thompson framework. Under suitable pressure-gap and non-uniform expansiveness assumptions, we show that the unique equilibrium state has the K-property, provided that the good collection of orbit segments satisfies an appropriate non-uniform specification property, as well as an appropriate non-uniform distortion control property for the potential function. These results do not require any additional lambda-decomposition structure and apply to a wide range of systems, including those with non-trivial central directions, such as the frame flow over closed rank-one manifolds with…

arxiv:2610.37395.title: Code uniqueness of 4-cell connected disjoint clusters in spatial chromatic model
arxiv:2610.37395.summary: The spatial chromatic model (SCM) is a novel entity-oriented spatial data model proposed in recent years. Spatial tessellations formed by SCM have been applied in preliminary analyses of spatial point pattern recognition,spatial topology, and Voronoi diagram generation. Unlike previous spatial tessellation models, a key feature of SCM is that each subspace (cell) possesses a chromatic code, which serves as the foundation for various theoretical analyses and applications of SCM.

arxiv:2610.37396.title: Finite group actions on the non-minimal nilpotent orbit closures in type A
arxiv:2610.37396.summary: We study quotients of the closures of the nilpotent orbits of type A by finite groups of inner automorphisms. Assuming the nilpotent orbit is not minimal, we show that the Q-factorial terminalizations of quotients of nilpotent orbit closures are precisely the quotients of the symplectic resolutions of the orbit closures. This identifies the Mori fan of each Q-factorial terminalization of the quotient with the Mori fan of a symplectic resolution of the orbit closure.
arxiv:2610.37396.authors: Gwyn Bellamy, Misha Feigin, Pavel Shlykov

arxiv:2610.37399.title: Representation and abelianization growth, particularly along expanding sequences
arxiv:2610.37399.summary: We study two obstructions to a finite group $G$ having a generating $d$-tuple whose Cayley graph has spectral gap at least $\epsilon$. Lubotzky and Weiss proved that such a gap forces $\mathrm{ab}_k(G)$, the largest order of the abelianization of a subgroup of index at most $k$, to be $\exp(O_\epsilon(dk))$, while de la Harpe, Robertson and Valette proved that it forces $\mathrm{rep}_k(G)$, the number of irreducible complex representations of degree at most $k$, to be $\exp(O_\epsilon(dk^2))$. We show that the first bound implies the second, and in fact implies it with $k^2$ replaced by $k\log k$.

arxiv:2610.37401.title: A semigroup approach for rough partial differential equations with jumps
arxiv:2610.37401.summary: We establish an infinite-dimensional sewing lemma for discontinuous paths on a scale of Banach spaces. This allows us to construct Young and rough convolutions with jumps. Based on this we analyze the local and global well-posedness of semilinear parabolic rough partial differential equations (PDEs) with jumps in mixed space-time regularity spaces.
arxiv:2610.37401.authors: Alexandra Blessing Neam\c{t}u, Hongjun Gao, Haoyuan Li

arxiv:2610.37408.title: High powers of grids in random geometric graphs and thresholds for wide spanning structures
arxiv:2610.37408.summary: Using results of Leighton and Shor and of Shor and Yukich, we present a connection between $d$-dimensional bandwidth and (sharp) thresholds in $d$-dimensional random geometric graphs: namely, that the sharp threshold for a given graph property in random geometric graphs is determined by its $d$-dimensional bandwidth, and vice versa, whenever the $d$-dimensional bandwidth of this property grows sufficiently fast (at least polylogarithmically) with the order of the graphs. This connection provides a number of corollaries, such as new information about the sharp thresholds for containing different spanning subgraphs in $1$-dimensional random geometric graphs, as well as asymptotically tight…

arxiv:2610.37417.title: Nonexistence of Hadamard difference sets in groups of order $4p^2$ with $p\equiv 3 \pmod 4$, $p\ge 7$
arxiv:2610.37417.summary: We show that the Frobenius group $\langle x,y,z\mid x^p=y^p=z^4=1,\ xy=yx,\ zxz^{-1}=y,\ zyz^{-1}=x^{-1}\rangle$ of order $4p^2$ contains no $(4p^2,2p^2-p,p^2-p)$ difference set if $p\equiv 3\pmod 4$ is a prime with $p \geq 7$. Together with results of McFarland, Iiams and Liebler this shows that no group of order $4p^2$ with $p \equiv 3 \pmod 4$ and $p \geq 7$ contains a Hadamard difference set.

arxiv:2610.37421.title: Equidistant Affine Subspaces: Explicit Bounds, Codimension-Two Reduction, and Transverse Products
arxiv:2610.37421.summary: Let $\mathcal{N}(k,n)$ be the largest size of a family of affine $k$-planes in $\R^n$ at pairwise separation distance one. We develop a unified treatment of upper bounds, dimension reduction, and product constructions. Orthogonal-projection coordinates give a rank-stratified distance identity; a Veronese lifting converts its polynomial consequences into simultaneous total isotropy.

arxiv:2610.37423.title: Sharp Bounds for Toral Eigenfunctions and Threefold Additive Energy on Circles
arxiv:2610.37423.summary: For the lattice circle $P_n=\{z\in\mathbb{Z}^2:|z|^2=n\}$, we prove that the threefold additive energy $J_3(P_n)\le C|P_n|^3$, with an absolute constant $C$. This establishes the optimal bound suggested by Krishnapur--Kurlberg--Wigman and Bombieri--Bourgain. We also prove a uniform weak $L^6$ bound for $L^2$-normalized eigenfunctions on the square torus, and hence uniform $L^p$ bounds for every $1\le p<6$.

arxiv:2610.37439.title: Measure of Maximal Entropy for Geodesic Flows on Noncompact Manifolds of Nonpositive Curvature
arxiv:2610.37439.summary: We establish the variational characterization of the measure of maximal entropy on noncompact manifolds of nonpositive sectional curvature. Assuming that the deck transformation group contains an axial isometry with a rank-one axis and has a finite critical exponent, we prove that the supremum of the entropies of invariant probabilities equals the critical exponent and is attained if and only if the Bowen-Margulis-Sullivan (BMS) measure is finite. In that case, the measure of maximal entropy is unique and equals the normalized BMS measure.

arxiv:2610.37460.title: Rank reduction in orthosymplectic types
arxiv:2610.37460.summary: This note establishes a rank reduction for RLL-realization of quantum affine supergroups of orthosymplectic type. In the rational limit, this provides a more conceptual proof of the analogous result for orthosymplectic superYangians from arXiv:2311.18818. We also determine the exact scalar prefactor appearing in the evaluation of the universal $R$-matrix, refining the main result of arXiv:2408.16720.

arxiv:2610.37463.title: Local Law and Eigenvector Delocalization for Random Lifts
arxiv:2610.37463.summary: We establish a quantitative local law for random $N$-lifts of a fixed finite connected simple graph with minimum degree at least three. Away from the singular energies of the universal-cover spectrum, we obtain high-probability entrywise Green's function estimates down to spectral scales $(\log N)^C/N$, uniformly in the bulk and near regular edges and cusps. As a consequence, we establish complete eigenvector delocalization: every normalized eigenvector $u$ whose eigenvalue stays a small but fixed positive distance away from the singular energies satisfies $\|u\|_\infty\leq(\log N)^C/\sqrt{N}$ with high probability.

arxiv:2610.37468.title: Multicritical pseudo-Siegel bounds and the optimality of the Brjuno condition for all neutral polynomials
arxiv:2610.37468.summary: We establish uniform multicritical pseudo-Siegel bounds for polynomials of Zakeri type, where all free critical points are on the boundary of an invariant Siegel disk of bounded type. This generalizes the unicritical result~\cite{DL:wZ}. As an application, we show the optimality of the Brjuno condition under the Zakeri restriction: as the rotation number becomes non-Brjuno, the Siegel disk evolves into the Cremer Hedgehog.
arxiv:2610.37468.authors: Dzmitry Dudko, Yusheng Luo, Runze Zhang

arxiv:2610.37477.title: The Assouad Dimension of Graphs: An Affirmative Answer to Fraser's Question
arxiv:2610.37477.summary: This article primarily investigates the Assouad dimension of graphs of continuous functions. Initially, the Assouad spectrum of the graph of a H\"older and count-H\"older continuous function has been derived. It has been shown that the Assouad dimension of the graph of a continuous function $f:[a,b]\to \mathbb{R}$ with the count-H\"older condition is at least \( 1 + \sup \left\{ \overline{\dim}_{\mathrm{B}}L_f(y) : y \in \mathscr{R}_f[a,b]\right\} \) where $\overline{\dim}_{\mathrm{B}}$ denotes the upper box dimension, $L_f(y)$ is the level set of $f$ at level $y$, and $\mathscr{R}_f[a,b]$ is the range of $f$ on $[a,b]$.
arxiv:2610.37477.authors: Binyan Yu, Bilel Selmi, Jia Liu, Yongshun Liang

arxiv:2610.37479.title: Minimal acceleration and the topology of premonotonic cocycles
arxiv:2610.37479.summary: In his global theory of one-frequency Schr\"odinger operators~\cite{Av15}, Avila asked whether the acceleration of a real-analytic $\SL(2,\R)$ cocycle over an irrational circle rotation is bounded below by the absolute value of its topological degree and whether equality in nonzero degree characterizes premonotonicity. We answer this question affirmatively for every irrational frequency, without arithmetic restrictions. Here premonotonicity means that some iterate becomes strictly monotonic in the base variable after a periodic change of coordinates~\cite{AK15}.

arxiv:2610.37497.title: Bounds for B-coloring planar and outerplanar graphs
arxiv:2610.37497.summary: A proper coloring of the edges of a graph is one in which every $K_{1,2}$ is totally multicolored. A B-coloring is a coloring of the edges of $G$ in which every $K_{1,2}$ and every $K_{2,2}$ is totally multicolored. In this paper, we improve two results by the authors and Gy\'arf\'as.
arxiv:2610.37497.authors: Ryan R. Martin, Mikl\'os Ruszink\'o, G\'abor N. S\'ark\"ozy

arxiv:2610.37512.title: Coprime matchings of divisor sets
arxiv:2610.37512.summary: For a positive integer $n$, let $D(n)$ be its set of positive divisors and put $N:=\tau(n)=|D(n)|$. We characterize the arithmetic progressions $\mathcal P$ of length $N$ that admit a bijection with $D(n)$ pairing relatively prime integers. Such a coprime matching exists if and only if, for every prime $p\mid n$, at most $N/(\nu_p(n)+1)$ terms of $\mathcal P$ are divisible by $p$, where $\nu_p(n)$ is the exponent of $p$ in $n$.

arxiv:2610.37532.title: Relative distality and incidence bounds in positive characteristic
arxiv:2610.37532.summary: We prove Szemer\'edi-Trotter-type incidence bounds for algebraic relations in any field $F$ admitting a valuation with finite residue field. This includes $\mathbb F_q(t)$, $\mathbb F_q((t))$, and all finitely generated extensions of finite fields. Bays and Martin show that any algebraic $K_{d,s}$-free relation $E\subseteq F^k\times F^\ell$ admits a power-saving in the classical Zarankiewicz bound of K\H{o}v\'ari, S\'os, and Tur\'an.

arxiv:2610.37539.title: The packing and covering number of trees are local
arxiv:2610.37539.summary: For a graph, its $r$-packing number is the size of the largest $r$-separated set and its $r$-covering number is the size of the smallest $r$-net. We show that the $r$-covering number and $r$-packing number are continuous in the fringe topology on locally finite trees. This recovers convergence results by Meir and Moon for e.g. uniform binary trees, uniform plane trees, uniform Poly\'a trees and random recursive trees, and proves new results for many other tree models, such as size-conditioned Bienaym\'e trees, simply generated trees, $m$-ary search trees, the minimum spanning tree of the complete graph and preferential attachment trees.
arxiv:2610.37539.authors: Caelan Atamanchuk, Simon Briend, Serte Donderwinkel, Elaine Herrera

arxiv:2610.37551.title: Systolic pants decompositions with polynomial growth
arxiv:2610.37551.summary: We investigate improved bounds on the kissing number of a hyperbolic surface under the assumption that the systole set contains pants decompositions with volume growth constraints. Namely, when the dual graph of the pants decomposition has polynomial volume growth, we obtain a power-savings improvement for the upper bound on the kissing number in terms of systolic length. We also construct super-exponentially many (in $g$) pants decompositions with exponential volume growth for which our techniques still imply stronger upper bounds for kissing numbers.
arxiv:2610.37551.authors: Tarik Aougab, Jonah Gaster, Nicholas Miller

arxiv:2610.37573.title: Escape of mass for finite-area hyperbolic surfaces
arxiv:2610.37573.summary: Let $M$ be a noncompact finite-area hyperbolic surface. We give a lower bound for the $L^2$ norm of eigenfunctions and Eisenstein series in a compact part of the surface. This extends a result of Soundararajan [arXiv:0901.4060] to the nonarithmetic setting.
arxiv:2610.37573.authors: Alex Cohen, Zhenhao Li, Zhongkai Tao

arxiv:2610.37578.title: A cubic chromatic bound for capped graphs
arxiv:2610.37578.summary: An ordered graph is capped if, for any four vertices $a<b<c<d$, the edges $ac$ and $bd$ imply the edge $ad$. We prove that every nonempty capped graph $G$ satisfies $\chi(G)\leq\min\{3^{\omega(G)-1},18\omega(G)^3\}$, where $\chi(G)$ and $\omega(G)$ are its chromatic number and clique number. This proves a conjecture of Davies, Krawczyk, McCarty and Walczak.

arxiv:2610.37595.title: On Khovanov local equivalence groups
arxiv:2610.37595.summary: Inspired by work in Seiberg--Witten and Heegaard Floer homology, Dunfield, Sch\"utz, and the author constructed an abelian "local equivalence group" built from pairs of chain complexes, and a homomorphism from the smooth concordance group to this group that uses the odd Khovanov complex and the Bar-Natan deformation of the even Khovanov complex. Lewark independently gave a related local equivalence group and concordance invariant, using only the Bar-Natan deformation. In this paper, we construct $(\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z})^\infty$ subgroups of Lewark's local equivalence group and the kernel of the map from our local equivalence group to Lewark's, as well as $\mathbb{Z}^\infty$ direct summands…

arxiv:2610.37600.title: Polynomial automorphisms of C^2 with the same equilibrium measure
arxiv:2610.37600.summary: We review the following question: when do two polynomial automorphisms of C^2 have the same maximal entropy measure? While the answer has been known for some time when both automorphisms are compositions of H\'enon maps, the general case is more delicate. In this (mostly expository) note we explain how recent results in random dynamics give an almost complete solution to the question, and point out a number of related open problems.

arxiv:2610.37608.title: On $\mathbb{P}^1$-bundles on $\mathbb{P}^3$ that are small modifications of a Fano fourfold
arxiv:2610.37608.summary: We find necessary conditions for the projectivization of a rank two vector bundle $\mathcal{E}$ on $\mathbb{P}^3_{\mathbb{C}}$ to be related to a smooth Fano 4-fold by a small $\mathbb{Q}$-factorial modification (SQM). Furthermore, we fully describe the birational geometry of $\mathbb{P}_{\mathbb{P}^3}(\mathcal{E})$ when $\mathcal{E}$ is stable, with $c_1=-1$, $c_2=2$. In this case, we prove that there exists a flip from $X^+$ to $\mathbb{P}_{\mathbb{P}^3}(\mathcal{E})$, where $X^+$ is smooth and Fano.

arxiv:2610.37616.title: Generic tensor products are not maximal
arxiv:2610.37616.summary: We construct tensor products of uniform matroids which are strictly freer than their generic linear tensor products. In particular, the generic tensor product of two copies of $U_{7,9}$ is not maximal. More generally, for every $a,b\ge2$, this holds for $U_{7,a+7}$ and $U_{7,b+7}$.

arxiv:2610.37628.title: Localization, cobordism, and twisted $\chi_y$-genera of $\overline{\mathcal{M}}_{0,n}$
arxiv:2610.37628.summary: We use the method of equivariant localization to obtain a recursion for the cobordism-valued one-point psi-class intersections on $\overline{\mathcal{M}}_{0,n}$, and hence the cobordism classes $[\overline{\mathcal{M}}_{0,n}]$. Restricting to the hyperbolic formal group law, we recover the Poincar\'{e} polynomials of $\overline{\mathcal{M}}_{0,n}$ as a special case, and obtain new formulas for Hirzebruch $\chi_y$-genera of $\overline{\mathcal{M}}_{0,n}$ twisted by tautological line bundles.

arxiv:2610.37650.title: Hodge--Riemann relations for nef bundles
arxiv:2610.37650.summary: We introduce the $(m,p,q)$-Lefschetz property for $(1,1)$-type endomorphisms of Hodge--Lefschetz modules, providing a framework for studying nef $(1,1)$-classes and characteristic classes of nef vector bundles on compact K\"ahler manifolds. Under a Hall--Rado type condition on nef twisted vector bundles, we prove Hodge--Riemann relations for products of top Chern classes and, in suitable bidegrees, for products of derived Schur classes. For products of nef $(1,1)$-classes, we show furthermore that the Hall--Rado type condition is equivalent to simultaneous Hodge--Riemann relations.

arxiv:2610.37677.title: Explicit matrix hitting points for noncommutative algebraic branching programs
arxiv:2610.37677.summary: We give a deterministic polynomial-resource black-box identity test for noncommutative algebraic branching programs (ABPs), using ordinary matrix evaluations of the output polynomial. Given an alphabet of size $m\ge1$ and an ABP vertex bound $S\ge1$, we construct one fixed tuple of integer matrices of order $R=(m+2)d(d+1)/2$, where $d=(m+2)S$, with entry bit length $O(d\log(d+1))$. Every nonzero polynomial computed by an ABP with at most $S$ vertices has a nonzero evaluation at this tuple.

arxiv:2610.37694.title: Invariance in half-space last passage percolation and directed polymers
arxiv:2610.37694.summary: We prove various invariance properties for half-space geometric and exponential last passage percolation and the half-space log-gamma polymer, analogous to the full-space invariances proved by Dauvergne. We use the RSK and geometric RSK correspondences to establish a conditional distributional identity between the half-space models and the corresponding full-space models, which allows us to directly transfer the invariance results in the full space to the half space.

arxiv:2610.37711.title: The View-Obstruction Problem for Spheres in Dimensions Six and Seven
arxiv:2610.37711.summary: Place closed Euclidean balls of radius r at the points of (1/2, 1/2, ..., 1/2) + Z^n. The view-obstruction problem for spheres asks for the least r such that every ray from the origin into the open positive orthant meets a ball. Equivalently, it asks for D_n = sup_v min_{t in R} sum_i ||t v_i - 1/2||{Z}^2 over positive integer vectors v, where ||x||{Z} denotes the distance from x to the nearest integer.

arxiv:2610.37718.title: A short proof of the universality of the fundamental shadow links
arxiv:2610.37718.summary: We give a constructive three-dimensional proof of Costantino and Thurston's universality theorem for fundamental shadow links. More precisely, every compact connected oriented three-manifold with empty or toroidal boundary can be obtained by integral Dehn filling along a subset of the boundary components of a fundamental shadow link exterior.

arxiv:2610.37721.title: Local-to-Global Theorems Based on Cones with Applications to Graph Coloring
arxiv:2610.37721.summary: Local-to-Global theorems are a cornerstone of many of recent developments in theoretical computer science from coding theory and PCPs all the way to analyzing mixing time of Markov chains. Building on trickledown theorems on simplicial complexes, several techniques have been established to obtain tighter local-to-global theorems to analyze the spectral gap of the Glauber dynamics, namely matrix trickledown, ${\mathcal C}$-Lorentzian polynomials and more recently Bochner type inequalities. In this paper, we adopt non-local local-to-global/Bochner type inequalities on "cones", corresponding to the local neighborhood of a given vertex, to show that the Glauber dynamics mixes in polynomial time…

arxiv:2610.37724.title: Moment Polyptychs and the Equivariant Quantisation of Hypertoric Varieties
arxiv:2610.37724.summary: We study the equivariant geometric quantisation of a non-compact hypertoric variety of complex dimension $2n$ using symplectic cutting. When the defining arrangement is cooriented so that its base region is non-empty and bounded, fibre rotation has proper moment map and produces compact K\"ahler orbifold cuts carrying the residual torus action. We introduce the moment polyptych of such a cut, a polytopal complex assembled from truncated arrangement regions, and show that its vertices and local lattice data determine the fixed points, tangent weights, and finite orbifold groups required for equivariant orbifold Riemann-Roch localisation.

arxiv:2610.37730.title: Nonlinear springs with orbits in radicals: a solvability criterion
arxiv:2610.37730.summary: An odd polynomial oscillator has a periodic orbit given by a quadrature. When the zeros of the energy polynomial are all simple or all of even multiplicity, that quadrature is elementary exactly when the polynomial is a perfect square, and the time is a sum of inverse tangents. Recovering the displacement inverts that relation, algebraic when their coefficients are commensurate, making a closed form a Galois question.

arxiv:2610.37745.title: Defining 2-group symmetries on lattices and extracting their anomalies
arxiv:2610.37745.summary: Ordinary $0$-form symmetries $G$ can mix with $1$-form symmetries $\Pi_2$ to form a $2$-group $\mathcal{G}$. We give a concrete lattice definition for a class of finite $2$-group symmetries in terms of local relations among symmetry operators. These relations identify the Postnikov class $[\rho]\in H^3(BG,\Pi_2)$ that characterizes the mixing.

arxiv:2610.37777.title: Maximal Curves with Few Automorphisms
arxiv:2610.37777.summary: We consider the problem of constructing maximal curves with few automorphisms over finite fields. Our main ingredient is the determination of the \(\operatorname{PGL}_2\!\left(\overline{\mathbb F}_p\right)\)-stabilizer of the roots of the Chebyshev polynomials, apart from two exceptional cases already treated in the literature. We prove that, in all other cases, the only nontrivial M\"obius symmetry is the sign involution.

arxiv:2610.37813.title: Characteristic identities for orthogonal quantum matrices: examples
arxiv:2610.37813.summary: In this note, we illustrate our recent results regarding structure theory of orthogonal Quantum Matrix algebras \cite{OP-BMW,OP-reciprocal,OP-ortho} using the simplest nontrivial example: the RTT-algebra associated with the canonical orthogonal R-matrix of type $O(3)$ (see, e.g., \cite{FRT}). By introducing a suitable linear order on the set of generators, we obtain a set of quadratic relations defining the algebra. Next, we investigate relations among its higher-degree polynomials.

arxiv:2610.37827.title: Homotopy types and torsion in homology of generalized chessboard complexes
arxiv:2610.37827.summary: Multiple chessboard complexes are deleted joins of skeleta of a simplex. We classify their homotopy types for at most three rows and extend this classification to arbitrary column capacities, with the $2$-torus as the only exception to a wedge of spheres. We determine explicit homotopy decompositions for two families with four and five rows and use a common capacity redistribution map to construct infinite families with $2$- and $3$-torsion in integral homology.

arxiv:2610.37848.title: Ternary analogs of dendriform algebras and quadri-algebras
arxiv:2610.37848.summary: We construct ternary analogs of dendriform algebras and quadri-algebras, generalizing the well-known binary case. These new structures are defined in terms of nonsymmetric operads. We construct these new operads using ternary operations defined in terms of ternary Rota-Baxter operators.
arxiv:2610.37848.authors: Yu Hin (Gary),  Au, Murray R. Bremner

arxiv:2610.37850.title: Spectrahedral relaxations and tightenings of rigidly convex sets
arxiv:2610.37850.summary: We construct a natural spectrahedral relaxation of a rigidly convex set (rcs) that depends only on the cubic part and on the degree of the defining real zero polynomial. For quadratic polynomials, we prove exactness and for a product of linear polynomials, we show that a higher order version of our relaxation is exact. We also establish a way of tightening the relaxation by moving the origin inside the rcs, and that the rcs is recovered by sweeping the origin over its interior.

arxiv:2610.37866.title: Finite-Sample Optimal Conformal Prediction Sets under Covariate Shift
arxiv:2610.37866.summary: We study conformal prediction under covariate shift with a known covariate density ratio, seeking prediction sets with minimum expected length under the target distribution. For every calibration sample size, we prove that the rule combining the inverse conditional-density score with randomized weighted conformal calibration minimizes this expected length among all rules valid over the full weighted-exchangeability class. We approximate the oracle using quantile and kernel histograms, including forest-weighted estimators, and select estimators and tuning parameters by resampling to estimate calibrated target length.

arxiv:2610.37885.title: Complete $RO$-Graded Tambara Structure of $H\underline{\mathbb Z}$ for cyclic groups
arxiv:2610.37885.summary: We compute the $RO$-graded Tambara functor of $H\underline{\mathbb{Z}}$ for every finite cyclic group. We introduce a valuation language for homotopy groups: for prime-power cyclic group equivariant, classes are represented by compatible vertex arrays or by edge arrays. In these coordinates we compute products, restrictions, transfers, Weyl actions, and norms.

arxiv:2610.37920.title: High-chromatic tournament parts without a complete pair of cyclic triangles
arxiv:2610.37920.summary: Nguyen, Scott, and Seymour conjectured that any two disjoint subtournaments of sufficiently large chromatic number contain cyclic triangles, one in each subtournament, with all edges between them oriented in the same direction. We disprove this conjecture by constructing, for every positive integer $d$, a tournament $T$ with a vertex partition $(X,Y)$ such that $\chi(T[X]),\chi(T[Y])\ge d$, but no cyclic triangle in either part is complete to a cyclic triangle in the other. Our construction combines a graph of large girth and large chromatic number with a variant of Kneser graphs defined in terms of binary functions.
arxiv:2610.37920.authors: Guantao Chen, Hein van der Holst, Shengze Wang

arxiv:2610.37931.title: Generalised hyperbolic polynomials: combinatorial interpretation and real-rootedness
arxiv:2610.37931.summary: For $p,q$ natural numbers, define $\Delta^{\langle p,q \rangle}:=x^{p-1}\frac{\partial}{\partial y} + y^{q-1}\frac{\partial}{\partial x}$, and consider the sequence of polynomials $\biggl((\Delta^{\langle p,q \rangle})^n \cdot x\biggr)_{n\geq 0}$; we call these the generalised hyperbolic polynomials. In this paper, we provide a simple combinatorial interpretation for these polynomials. As special cases, we obtain combinatorial interpretations for the coefficients of the analogs of sinh and cosh corresponding to the curve $x^p- p y^q/q=1$; on setting $p=q=3$, we obtain Conrad and Flajolet's tree interpretation for the coefficients of the Dixonian elliptic functions (2006) as a special case.

arxiv:2610.37940.title: Enumeration Complexity of Permutation Classes
arxiv:2610.37940.summary: We study classes of permutations that are defined by avoidance of forbidden patterns. For each fixed finite set $B$ of forbidden patterns, we study the \emph{avoider enumeration problem}: given an integer $n$, output all $B$-avoiding permutations of length $n$. Avoider enumeration is output-polynomial for every fixed $B$.

arxiv:2610.37944.title: Symmetric List Objects
arxiv:2610.37944.summary: Cons-lists are fundamental to functional programming, and are well-understood as initial algebras, and as a concrete construction of free monoids. In category theory, such list objects can be axiomatised internal to any monoidal category, with nil and cons maps, and a recursion mechanism. When strengthened to support parametrised recursion, they can be shown to give the free monoid construction.
arxiv:2610.37944.authors: Fiona Blackett, Vikraman Choudhury, Rin Liu

arxiv:2610.37956.title: Torsion Theories in a non-pointed Context II: iterated torsion theories
arxiv:2610.37956.summary: Generalizing a known result in the context of homological categories, we show that, in a regular protomodular category $\mathcal{C}$ equipped with a posetal, monocoreflective subcategory whose coreflector inverts monomorphisms, every torsion theory, in a non-pointed sense, satisfying suitable properties gives rise to a torsion theory in the category $\operatorname{Arr}(\mathcal{C})$ of arrows in $\mathcal{C}$. Moreover, we show that the induced torsion theory in $\operatorname{Arr}(\mathcal{C})$ satisfies the same good properties of the original one in $\mathcal{C}$, allowing to iterate the process. Examples of this situation can be found in protomodular varieties of universal algebras with…

arxiv:2610.37961.title: On the cohomological dimension of Henselian valued fields
arxiv:2610.37961.summary: Let $(K,v)$ be a Henselian valued field of rank one and of mixed characteristic $(0,p)$, with value group $\Gamma$ dense in $\mathbb{R}$ and residue field $k$. We compute all the graded pieces of the filtration induced by $v$ on the Milnor $\mathrm{K}$-theory modulo $p$ of $K$, in terms of the exterior powers of the $\mathbb{F}_p$-vector space $\Gamma/p\Gamma$ and of the modules of differential forms of $k$. This extends to the non-discrete setting a classical theorem of Kato concerning complete discretely valued fields.
arxiv:2610.37961.authors: Diego Izquierdo, Giancarlo Lucchini Arteche, Gonzalo Manzano Flores

arxiv:2610.37969.title: Diagrams for Roots and Quiver Representations in the context of the Gabriel-Kac Theorem
arxiv:2610.37969.summary: Using the data of the Dynkin diagrams, we build graphical calculi for representing the positive roots of Kac-Moody algebras and the representations of quivers. Once developed, we use these to analyze the asymptotic size of the root and representation spaces, and discuss how this relates to the Gabriel-Kac theorem, the correspondence between these two structures. We give a refinement of this correspondence in terms of the trichotomy of growth rates for Kac-Moody algebras depending on if they are of finite, affine, or indefinite type, which is done in terms of what we call ``tree like" representations.

arxiv:2610.37990.title: Symmetry-resolved periods in a cyclic-dominance automaton: separating intrinsic from lattice-induced periodicity
arxiv:2610.37990.summary: Periodic attractors of spatially extended systems possess not one period but a hierarchy of periods, one for each level of observation and symmetry quotient, and this hierarchy separates how a pattern evolves from how it fits the finite domain. For a synchronous threshold model of cyclic dominance on an $L\times L$ torus, equivalent to the three-color cyclic cellular automaton of Fisch, Gravner and Griffeath, we measure for every attractor a \emph{tuple} of periods: that of the populations ($\Tpop$), of the full configuration ($\Tst$), and of the configuration up to color rotations ($\Tcol$), lattice symmetries ($\Tgeo$) and the full space--color group ($\TG$). Equivariance implies exact…
arxiv:2610.37990.authors: Francisco J. Mu\~noz, Juan Carlos Nu\~no

arxiv:2610.37996.title: Calabi-Yau Hyperbolicity
arxiv:2610.37996.summary: The goal of this paper is to introduce a new notion of hyperbolicity for compact complex manifolds with trivial canonical bundle, called \textit{Calabi--Yau hyperbolicity}. We investigate its fundamental properties and establish a characterization in terms of the fundamental group. In particular, we show that no compact K\"ahler Calabi--Yau manifold is Calabi--Yau hyperbolic, highlighting the genuinely non-K\"ahler nature of this notion.

arxiv:2610.38023.title: Pointed Hurwitz--Brill--Noether theory
arxiv:2610.38023.summary: We study the geometry of Hurwitz--Brill--Noether spaces with vanishing conditions at a totally ramified point. Degeneration to a curve with an elliptic tail simplifies the combinatorics of Larson, Larson--Larson--Vogt, and Aggarwal, giving inductive proofs of Aggarwal's results in the one-point setting, and yields an efficient recursion for the algebraic Euler characteristics. Finally, when the expected dimension is negative, we give a numerical criterion ensuring the universal Hurwitz--Brill--Noether locus admits a component of expected relative dimension, generically finite over its image in the Hurwitz space, analogous to the existing results of Pflueger and Teixidor i Bigas for…

arxiv:2610.38066.title: Loop Space Models and Integral Homology of Connected Quandles
arxiv:2610.38066.summary: We construct a marked integral delooping of a connected quandle's covering monoid, realizing its rack space as a homotopy fiber. For finite connected quandles at primes $p$ not dividing a point-stabilizer order, we determine the local $A_\infty$ type and the ordinary rack cohomology shuffle algebra over fields of characteristic $p$. We compute integral quandle homology in all positive degrees for finite connected regular cyclic Alexander quandles and the tetrahedral quandle.

arxiv:2610.38071.title: A curve of genus $2$ over $\mathbb{C}(t)$ and hexads of bitangents to a smooth quartic
arxiv:2610.38071.summary: In this paper we study the Abel-Jacobi map of a genus 2 curve over $\mathbb{C}(t)$ arising from a double cover of $\mathbb{P}^2(\mathbb{C})$ branched along six lines. We utilize the so-called Mumford representations to conduct the calculations. As an application, we give an alternative proof of classical results on quartics and bitangents.

arxiv:2610.38099.title: Strong stable sets and asymptotic fineness
arxiv:2610.38099.summary: We investigate the strong stable sets of the geodesic flow on hyperbolic surfaces and their relation to the injectivity radius. We prove that the strong stable set of a vector does not coincide with its stable horocycle if and only if the injectivity radius along the associated geodesic ray is not bounded away from zero and the ray does not diverge through a cusp. In that case, the strong stable set is an uncountable union of stable horocycles.

arxiv:2610.38108.title: Safety of layered control systems via control barrier morphisms
arxiv:2610.38108.summary: Layered control architectures provide a powerful paradigm for synthesizing controllers for complex systems. Yet, translating guarantees at each layer to system-level guarantees is challenging due to the interactions between layers. To address this problem, this paper presents a categorical perspective on layered control architectures.
arxiv:2610.38108.authors: Aaron D. Ames, Joe Moeller, Massimiliano de Sa, Paulo Tabuada

arxiv:2610.38115.title: Geometric properties of the analytic Emerton-Gee stack
arxiv:2610.38115.summary: The analytic Emerton-Gee stack is a rigid analytic moduli stack of $(\varphi,\Gamma)$-modules over the Robba ring, and is expected to play a fundamental role in the categorical $p$-adic local Langlands correspondence for locally analytic representations. In this paper, we establish the fundamental geometric properties of the analytic Emerton-Gee stack: it is a rigid analytic Artin stack, normal, a local complete intersection, and equidimensional of the expected dimension. As an application, our normality result removes the reducedness hypothesis in the paper of Le, Strauch, and Wang, thereby yielding an unconditional proof of the conjecture on the global sections of the analytic Emerton-Gee…

arxiv:2610.38137.title: The Miyaoka-Yau inequality and the delta invariant for Fano varieties II -soliton case-
arxiv:2610.38137.summary: Inspired by recent work of Inoue and Hallam-Lahdili, we prove an equivariant Miyaoka-Yau inequality with a correction term for smooth Fano manifolds admitting K\"ahler-Ricci solitons. It recovers the usual Miyaoka-Yau inequality in the K\"ahler-Einstein case. Our proof uses weighted equivariant Bogomolov-Gieseker and Langer inequalities for torsion-free sheaves, together with a weighted slope estimate for the canonical extension sheaf.

arxiv:2610.38139.title: Non-associative Hopf Algebra on Dyck Paths Arising from the Shuffle-insertion Product
arxiv:2610.38139.summary: In this paper, we define a shuffle-insertion product and a cut-box coproduct on the vector space spanned by Dyck paths, where the product is commutative but non-associative. We prove that the product and coproduct are compatible, making the space a non-associative bialgebra. This bialgebra is connected and bigraded by path degree and peak number, and hence is a non-associative Hopf algebra.
arxiv:2610.38139.authors: Nantel Bergeron, Yuchen Guo, Huilan Li

arxiv:2610.38143.title: Comparison categories: the normal form and the regularity of comparison data
arxiv:2610.38143.summary: There are many types of equivalence relations in mathematics, each one enjoying its own defnition, but many of them can also be defined by transformations of morphisms: Green's relations, orbit relations, conjugacy, equality of orbit closures, equivalence of Cauchy sequences, stable isomorphism. We unify them through the comparison category of a comparison datum, read at levels $-1,0,1,2,\dots$ (comparisons in both directions, connected components, homotopy groups). Its normal form is a full subcategory of a Grothendieck construction $\int_VH$ cut out by a map $s$; the classical relations are traced back to it by restriction along $s$, enrichment by a cost (limit relations) and filtered…

arxiv:2610.38161.title: Asymptotic distributions of the Betti and Hodge numbers of $\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}$
arxiv:2610.38161.summary: We study the asymptotic distributions of the Betti and Hodge numbers of the moduli spaces $\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}$ of stable pointed curves and the all-light Hassett spaces $\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,0|n}$, for fixed genus $g\ge1$ as the number of markings tends to infinity. We prove central limit theorems for the full Betti distributions, whose variances grow linearly in $n$ with leading coefficients independent of the genus. For the normalized even Betti numbers, we establish refined local limit theorems with estimates uniform in degree.

arxiv:2610.38163.title: Test ideals can be computed by boundaries
arxiv:2610.38163.summary: Let $R$ be a normal $F$-finite ring of characteristic $p>0$. We show that one effective $\mathbb{Q}$-divisor $\Delta$, with $K_R+\Delta$ $\mathbb{Q}$-Cartier of index prime to $p$, computes the big test ideal. This answers a question of Schwede and Smith.
arxiv:2610.38163.authors: Rahul Ajit, with Appendix joint with Daniel Apsley

arxiv:2610.38184.title: Geometry of $m$-direct-sum morphisms
arxiv:2610.38184.summary: Let $V$ be a complex vector space of dimension $mk$ ($m\ge2$). A morphism from a positive-dimensional projective variety $f\colon X\to\mathrm{Gr}(k,V)$ is $m$-direct-sum if $V=U_{x_1}\oplus\cdots\oplus U_{x_m}$ for every $m$ pairwise distinct points $x_1,\dots,x_m$ on $X$, where $U_x\subset V$ is the subspace represented by $f(x)$. We show that $X$ is necessarily a smooth rational curve.
arxiv:2610.38184.authors: Duo Li, Yanjie Li, Francesco Russo

arxiv:2610.38187.title: Special cycles and Picard groups of Baily--Borel compactifications
arxiv:2610.38187.summary: In this paper, we answer two basic questions concerning algebraic cycles on orthogonal Shimura varieties attached to lattices. First, we prove that Kudla's special cycles and Heegner cycles have the same rational span in every codimension. This fills a gap in the codimension-one argument of \cite[Remark 2.4]{BLMM17}, pointed out by Bruinier--Zuffetti \cite{BZ26}.

arxiv:2610.38237.title: Inflection sets of permutations
arxiv:2610.38237.summary: In 2020, Brualdi and Dahl introduced the discrete derivative $\sigma'(i)=\sigma(i+1)-\sigma(i)$ of a permutation $\sigma\in\Sym_n$. In this paper, we focus on the second derivative of a permutation, $\sigma''(i)=\sigma(i+1)+\sigma(i-1)-2\sigma(i)$, and the inflections it determines. We show that for even $n$, the only distinct permutations with the same second derivative are the identity and its reverse, while for odd $n$, the second derivative is not injective even after excluding them.
arxiv:2610.38237.authors: Gordon Rojas Kirby, Mariana Smit Vega Garcia

arxiv:2610.38287.title: A Characterization of Functions on the Integer Lattice That Are L-Extendable through Local Convex Extensions
arxiv:2610.38287.summary: L-extendable functions on the integer lattice are functions that admit a $\frac12$UJ-convex relaxation; that is, values can be assigned to the additional half-integral points, while keeping the original values at integer points, so that the resulting function is $\frac12$UJ-convex. Various examples of L-extendable functions and their applications are known. A general characterization of L-extendability for functions on the integer lattice, however, remains open.
arxiv:2610.38287.authors: Ken Yokoyama, Yuni Iwamasa, Kei Kimura

arxiv:2610.38298.title: Stability conditions on Calabi-Yau threefolds of type K
arxiv:2610.38298.summary: A Calabi-Yau threefold of type K is a free quotient $X=(S\times E)/G$ of the product of a K3 surface and an elliptic curve. We construct a family of geometric Bridgeland stability conditions on $X$ by using Liu's product construction on $S\times E$ and then inducing along the Galois covering. The family has dimension $2h^{1,1}(X)$, and is disjoint from the $\widetilde{\GL}_2^+(\R)$-orbit of Li's stability conditions.

arxiv:2610.38323.title: Determination of weight enumerators of binary extremal self-dual codes of length 60
arxiv:2610.38323.summary: We construct three binary extremal self-dual codes of length $60$ with weight enumerators for which no binary extremal self-dual codes of length $60$ were previously known to exist. This completes the determination of the weight enumerators that occur for binary extremal self-dual codes of length $60$.

arxiv:2610.38328.title: Sizes of cross-intersecting families
arxiv:2610.38328.summary: The size of cross-intersecting families ${\cal F}_1, \dots, {\cal F}_d$ is usually measured by the sum or the product of the sizes $|{\cal F}_i|$. These two natural size functions have different extremal structures, and different techniques have been developed for them. We introduce the cross-degree of a size function and show that the potential extremal structures of maximum cross-intersecting families are the same for all size functions of finite cross-degree, including the sum and the product.

arxiv:2610.38330.title: Sharp Bounds on Torsional Rigidity of Metric Graphs with Signed Delta-Vertex Strengths
arxiv:2610.38330.summary: We study torsional rigidity on finite compact connected metric graphs with real \(\delta\)-vertex strengths in the regime of strictly positive torsion. For a fixed total length \(L>0\), let \(I_+\) be the sum of the positive strengths and \(I_-\) the sum of the magnitudes of the negative strengths, with \(I_+>I_-\). We determine the sharp infimum and the exact threshold for a finite universal supremum.

arxiv:2610.38368.title: Crescent configurations in three dimensions
arxiv:2610.38368.summary: A crescent configuration of $n$ points in $\mathbb R^d$ is a set in general position whose distinct pairwise distances have multiplicities $1,\ldots,n-1$. We construct such a configuration in $\mathbb R^3$ for every $n\geq3$, giving a uniform bound of three for the minimum dimension. The proof uses equally spaced parameters on a short circular helix and Rolle's theorem.

arxiv:2610.38371.title: An analogue of $\Gamma$-function for irreducible cuspidal representations of the group $\mathrm{GL}(2)$ over a two-dimensional local field
arxiv:2610.38371.summary: Let $\mathbf F$ be a non-archimedian local field of odd residue characteristic, ${\mathcal O}={\mathbf F}[\![t]\!]\subset{\mathcal K}={\mathbf F}(\!(t)\!)$. We consider the subgroup $\widehat{\mathrm{GL}}(2,{\mathcal O})={\mathcal K}^\times\cdot{\mathrm{GL}}(2,{\mathcal O})\subset{\mathrm{GL}}(2,{\mathcal K})$, and the normalizer ${\mathrm{GL}}'(2,{\mathcal O})\subset{\mathrm GL}(2,{\mathcal K})$ of an Iwahori subgroup $I\subset{\mathrm{GL}}(2,{\mathcal K})$. We calculate the $\Gamma$-functions for irreducible special representations of $\widehat{\mathrm{GL}}(2,{\mathcal O})$ and ${\mathrm{GL}}'(2,{\mathcal O})$.

arxiv:2610.38373.title: A logarithmic error term for subset sums of zero-sum-free sets
arxiv:2610.38373.summary: For a positive integer $k$, let $f(k)$ be the minimum number of distinct nonempty subset sums of a zero-sum-free $k$-element set, where the minimum is taken over all finite abelian groups. We prove $f(k)\ge \frac{k^2}{2}-13k\log(k+1)-116k$. Together with the classical upper bound, this gives $f(k)=k^2/2+O(k\log k)$, with the optimal leading coefficient.

arxiv:2610.38374.title: A five-species counterexample to the Hofbauer--Kon--Saito conjecture on qualitative permanence
arxiv:2610.38374.summary: Hofbauer, Kon and Saito (J. Math. Biol. 2008) showed that a Lotka-Volterra interaction matrix $A$ with negative diagonal can be qualitatively permanent only if (C1) every cycle of length $\ge 2$ of $A$ is nonpositive and (C2) every negative cycle contains exactly one negative entry.

arxiv:2610.38376.title: Projective compactifications of hypersurface complements
arxiv:2610.38376.summary: Let $U$ be a smooth affine variety of the form $U=\mathrm{P}^n\setminus H$, where $H\subset\mathrm{P}^n$ is a smooth connected hypersurface. We prove that every smooth projective compactification of the complex manifold $U$, by adding a smooth connected divisor, is isomorphic to $\mathrm{P}^n$. The proof uses the rational Reeb index of the normal circle bundle and positive $S^1$-equivariant symplectic homology.

arxiv:2610.38386.title: Moments of Magic Squares: Line-Sum Conditions, a Permutation Threshold, and Random Energies
arxiv:2610.38386.summary: Every semi-magic square of order $n$ satisfies the axial moment identities $\sum_{i,j}s_{ij}j^m=\sum_{i,j}s_{ij}i^m=M(n)\sum_jj^m$ for all $m\ge1$, where $M(n)=n(n^2+1)/2$. For real matrices the converse requires $1\le m\le n-1$, whereas for arrangements of $\{1,\dots,n^2\}$ fewer moments suffice once $n\ge14$. We define the permutation threshold $k^*(n)$ as the least $k$ such that every arrangement satisfying these identities for $1\le m\le k$ is semi-magic.

arxiv:2610.38401.title: Robustness of Magic and the Directed Geometry of State Conversion
arxiv:2610.38401.summary: In this work, we introduce a state-space distance calibrated by stabilizer states based on the dual structure of the robustness of magic (RoM), and show that RoM is exactly represented as the distance to the free-state set. We then extend this geometry to state conversion by defining the directed conversion deficiency $C_{\mathcal F}$ as the distance between a target state and the set of states freely reachable from a given input state. The quantity $C_{\mathcal F}$ characterizes free convertibility and is related to the minimum stabilizer quasiprobability weight required to represent the conversion residual through the relation $1+2C_{\mathcal F}$.

arxiv:2610.38412.title: Nice Partitions of Signed-Graphic Arrangements Are Inductive Factorizations
arxiv:2610.38412.summary: Nice partitions of hyperplane arrangements give tensor factorizations of Orlik-Solomon algebras as graded vector spaces. In general, a hyperplane arrangement admitting a nice partition need not be free. In this paper, we consider signed-graphic arrangements, the subarrangements of type-$B$ Weyl arrangements, over fields of characteristic different from $2$.
arxiv:2610.38412.authors: Weikang Liang, Suijie Wang, Yue Zhou

arxiv:2610.38414.title: The Borisov--Nuer conjecture and root decompositions in even unimodular Lorentzian lattices
arxiv:2610.38414.summary: We prove that every vector of $\mathrm{II}_{8n+1,1}$, with $n\ge1$, is a sum of two roots if and only if $n=1$ or $2$. This settles the Borisov--Nuer conjecture and implies the existence of Ulrich line bundles for every very ample polarization on a complex unnodal Enriques surface. For vectors of negative norm, we express the number of root decompositions as a Fourier coefficient of a vector-valued theta series, reducing existence to positivity.

arxiv:2610.38427.title: On the Witt liftability of quasi-F-split Calabi--Yau varieties
arxiv:2610.38427.summary: We prove that a quasi-$F$-split strict Calabi--Yau variety $X$ of dimension $d$ over an algebraically closed field $k$ of odd characteristic $p$ admits a smooth projective lifting over $W(k)$ if $p\geq d-1$, or if $p=d-2$ and $H^0(X,T_X)=0$. We also prove $W_3(k)$-liftability in odd characteristic.

arxiv:2610.38430.title: Tur\'an number of three disjoint cliques of arbitrary sizes
arxiv:2610.38430.summary: The Tur\'an number $\rm ex(n,H)$ of a given graph $H$ is the maximum number of edges in an $n$-vertex $H$-free graph. In this paper, for all $p\ge q\ge r\ge 2$ and $n\geq p+q+r$, we determine the exact value of $\rm ex(n,K_p\cup K_q\cup K_r)$ and describe all extremal graphs.
arxiv:2610.38430.authors: Alexandr Kostochka, Dadong Peng, Zimu Xiang, Liang Zhang

arxiv:2610.38435.title: Nevanlinna Theory on Berkovich Curves
arxiv:2610.38435.summary: We develop a value distribution theory for finite analytic morphisms between proper connected quasi-smooth Berkovich curves over a complete algebraically closed non-Archimedean field. The central tool is a multi-tail Dirichlet Green function on finite truncations of a generalized skeleton, which makes non-Archimedean potential theory on skeleta compatible with global Nevanlinna asymptotics. Using it, we prove the first main theorem as an exact identity relating the characteristic, counting, and proximity functions.

arxiv:2610.38447.title: Davenport constants with growing binary rank
arxiv:2610.38447.summary: We study the correction to the standard lower bound $D^*$ for Davenport constants of finite abelian groups with a growing elementary two-component. For every fixed nontrivial abelian $p$-group $H$ of odd order, we prove $D(H\oplus C_2^r)=D^*(H\oplus C_2^r)+(D(H)-1)\log_2 r+O_H(1)$, with a uniform version for varying $H$. For $C_3\oplus C_2^r$, we determine exact values on explicit infinite intervals of ranks.

arxiv:2610.38456.title: Sheaves on quoric manifolds
arxiv:2610.38456.summary: Quoric manifolds are quaternionic analogues of quasitoric manifolds introduced by Hopkinson. Given a quoric manifold over a simple polytope, we study the stratification induced by the faces of the polytope. We then show that the equivariant derived category of constructible sheaves with respect to the face stratification is equivalent to the derived category of constructible DG-modules over a DG-algebra defined on the orbit space.

arxiv:2610.38460.title: Tensor products of 2-representations
arxiv:2610.38460.summary: In this paper we define comonoidal structures on additive $\Bbbk$-linear $2$-categories which guarantee the existence of a monoidal structure on the corresponding $2$-categories of $2$-representations.

arxiv:2610.38469.title: Hilbert functions of filtered graphical zonotopal algebras
arxiv:2610.38469.summary: The external zonotopal algebra of a graph is generated by nilpotent vertex elements $X_v$ and determines the graphical matroid after deleting loops. Replacing these generators by $f(X_v)$, for a power series $f(u)$, and filtering by word length gives a family of filtered algebras. We extend filtered graph reconstruction from simple graphs to loopless multigraphs without isolated vertices when the linear and quadratic coefficients of $f$ are nonzero.
arxiv:2610.38469.authors: Boris Shapiro, Ilya Smirnov, Arkady Vaintrob

arxiv:2610.38472.title: EKR Results for Cuspidal Representations of $\mathrm{GL}_2(q)$
arxiv:2610.38472.summary: Let $\mathcal{S}_\chi$ be a cuspidal representation of $\mathrm{GL}_2(q)$. A subset $S \subseteq \mathrm{GL}_2(q)$ is \emph{$t$-intersecting} if $\dim_{\mathbb{C}}\{v \in \mathcal{S}_\chi: g_1v = g_2v\} \geqslant t$ for any $g_1, g_2 \in S$. In this paper, we determine $\max{|S|}$ where $S$ is $t$-intersecting.

arxiv:2610.38474.title: On the motivic approach to the Abhyankar rectifiability problem and concrete rectifications
arxiv:2610.38474.summary: We study closed embeddings of the complex affine line into affine three-space. We prove that, for every such embedding, the complete-intersection normal map identifies the $\mathbb{A}^1$-fundamental sheaf of its complement with $\mathbf{K}_2^{\mathrm{MW}}$. The proof compares torsors under arbitrary strongly $\mathbb{A}^1$-invariant group sheaves.
arxiv:2610.38474.authors: A. S. Frolov, I. S. Dorofeev

arxiv:2610.38498.title: On the Supersingular reduction of Cubic fourfolds with Complex Multiplication
arxiv:2610.38498.summary: If $X$ is a K3 surface with complex multiplication by a CM field $E$, Kazuhiro Ito proved that the height of the reduction of $X$ in characteristic $p>0$, and its Artin invariant if it is supersingular, can be computed from the decomposition of $p$ in $E$. We present analogous results for cubic fourfolds by using the main theorem of complex multiplication for cubic fourfold, proved by Rikuto Ito.

arxiv:2610.38515.title: The asymptotics of off-diagonal book Ramsey numbers
arxiv:2610.38515.summary: Let $B_n$ be the book graph consisting of $n$ triangles sharing a common edge. We prove upper bounds for $r(B_{\lceil\alpha n\rceil},B_n)$ that asymptotically match the known lower bounds in the remaining range $1/6<\alpha<1/4$. Combined with the known results for the other ranges of $\alpha$, this completely determines the asymptotics of the Ramsey number $r(B_{\lceil\alpha n\rceil},B_n)$ for every fixed $0<\alpha\le1$: \[ r(B_{\lceil\alpha n\rceil},B_n)=(c(\alpha)+o(1))n, \qquad c(\alpha)= \begin{cases} 2, & 0<\alpha\le1/6,\\[1mm] \displaystyle\frac{3}{1+2p_\alpha^2}, & 1/6<\alpha\le\alpha_0,\\[3mm] (1+\sqrt\alpha)^2, & \alpha_0<\alpha\le1, \end{cases} \] where…
arxiv:2610.38515.authors: Lulu Dai, Chunchao Fan, Qizhong Lin

arxiv:2610.38525.title: Dimension-free exponential entropy quotients over $\mathbb{F}_2$
arxiv:2610.38525.summary: Let $X$ be a random vector in $\mathbb{F}_2^m$, and let $X'$ be an independent copy. We prove that, for every $\varepsilon>0$, there is a subspace $G$ with $\dim G\le 2^{320(1+\varepsilon)/\varepsilon}H(X)$ such that $H(q_GX)\le(1+\varepsilon)(H(q_GX+q_GX')-H(q_GX))$. In particular, the quotient entropy is at most $(1+\varepsilon)(H(X+X')-H(X))$.

arxiv:2610.38539.title: Minimizing the spectral radius of unicyclic graphs with fixed order and dissociation number
arxiv:2610.38539.summary: A dissociation set of a graph G is a vertex subset S contained in V(G) such that the induced subgraph G[S] has maximum degree at most 1, and the dissociation number of G is the cardinality of a maximum dissociation set denoted by {\Phi}(G). In this paper, we first derive a sharp lower bound on the dissociation number for all unicyclic graphs. Furthermore, we also study the graphs with minimum spectral radius among all unicyclic graphs with given order and dissociation number and explicitly identify all extremal graphs for \(n-4 \le \Phi(G) \le n-1\).
arxiv:2610.38539.authors: Yu Zhou, Yuanyuan Chen, Dan Li, Dandan Fan

arxiv:2610.38550.title: Equivalence of freeness and higher order freeness of hyperplane arrangements
arxiv:2610.38550.summary: Using vector bundle theory, we prove that an essential hyperplane arrangement in an $\ell$-dimensional vector space over a field of characteristic zero is free if and only if its module of logarithmic derivations of order $p$ is free for some $1\le p\le\ell-1$. The same statement holds for multiarrangements.

arxiv:2610.38552.title: Directed isoperimetry and infinitely fast robbers
arxiv:2610.38552.summary: We study the fast version of the cops and robber game on finite digraphs with unit-speed cops and an unbounded-speed robber. We prove a lower bound for the cop number of every strongly connected digraph in terms of its order, maximum out-degree, and out-vertex expansion, extending Mehrabian's isoperimetric lower bound to digraphs, where connected components are replaced by forward reachable sets. For strongly connected abelian Cayley digraphs of fixed out-degree, we show that the ratio of the cop number to the number of vertices is comparable to each of out-vertex expansion, vertex expansion of the underlying undirected graph, minimum nontrivial character displacement, the square root of…

arxiv:2610.38560.title: Large tight components and Dirac thresholds for tight Hamilton cycles
arxiv:2610.38560.summary: For every odd integer $r\ge1$, let $q_r=1-2^{-r}\binom r{(r-1)/2}$. We show that, for every odd $r\ge3$ and sufficiently large $n$, every $n$-vertex $r$-uniform hypergraph with at least $q_r\binom nr$ edges contains a tight component with at least $(1/2-o(1))\binom nr$ edges. This confirms a conjecture posed by Lang and Sanhueza-Matamala in 2024.
arxiv:2610.38560.authors: Hao Lin, Guanghui Wang, Jiande Zhang, Wenling Zhou

arxiv:2610.38574.title: The exact digirth and out-degree bounds for $C(k,k)$-subdivision and out-forest in digraphs
arxiv:2610.38574.summary: For each integer $k\ge2$, let $C(k,k)$ denote the oriented cycle formed by two internally vertex-disjoint directed paths of length $k$ with the same initial and terminal vertices. Picasarri-Arrieta and Rambaud ({\small European J. Combin., 2024}) asked for the smallest integer $g_k$ such that every digraph with minimum out-degree at least two and digirth at least $g_k$ contains a subdivision of $C(k,k)$.
arxiv:2610.38574.authors: Bin Chen, Jianfeng Hou, Xinmin Hou, Siyue Liu, Xinjie Wang, Xinyu Zhou

arxiv:2610.38586.title: Estimating the number of nodes and paths in a DAG by following a random path
arxiv:2610.38586.summary: We investigate a simple method to compute an unbiased estimate of the number of nodes of a directed acyclic graph (DAG) by following a random directed path. This method is due to Leonard Pitt from 1987, and it generalizes a method of D. E.

arxiv:2610.38599.title: Graphon Colourings and Limits of Graph Partitions
arxiv:2610.38599.summary: We develop a framework for pure and mixed graphon colourings and use it to study the limiting behaviour of graph partition parameters under cut convergence. Pure colourings correspond to measurable partitions, while mixed colourings assign a probability distribution on the colour set to each point. We develop the representation, equivalence and convergence theory, and show that every mixed graphon colouring has an equivalent pure representative, possibly on a different probability space.
arxiv:2610.38599.authors: Svante Janson, Tiffany Y. Y. Lo, Colin McDiarmid, Anda Skeja, Fiona Skerman

arxiv:2610.38655.title: Regularity of Symbolic Powers of Polymatroidal Ideals and Supermodular Prime Intersections
arxiv:2610.38655.summary: Let $S=\mathbb{K}[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$ be a polynomial ring over a field $\mathbb{K}$. For a polymatroidal ideal $I\subseteq S$ generated in degree $d$, we prove $$\omega(I^{(s)})=\operatorname{reg} I^{(s)}=\operatorname{reg} I^s=sd\qquad(s\ge1),$$ where symbolic powers use all associated primes and $\omega$ denotes the largest degree of a minimal generator. Thus every symbolic power has a degree resolution.

arxiv:2610.38658.title: Larger Crossing Families
arxiv:2610.38658.summary: We give the first explicit constant for crossing families of linear size by showing that every set of $n$ points in general position in the plane contains a crossing family of size approximately $\frac{n}{79}$. We further identify some conditions where there are even larger crossing families. The first such condition forbids the existence of a large different pattern, namely non-convex 4-clusters: We show that every point set contains either a large non-convex 4-cluster or a large crossing family.

arxiv:2610.38664.title: Upper Bounds for CSP Non-redundancy via Locally Decodable Codes
arxiv:2610.38664.summary: In the study of constraint satisfaction problems (CSPs), the non-redundancy of a relation measures the maximum number of clauses in a CSP instance which can be logically independent. In the last few years, CSP non-redundancy has found a number of applications including in query complexity, sparsification, kernelization and streaming. In this paper, we present a novel technique for upper-bounding the non-redundancy of some relations using locally decodable codes (LDCs) and locally correctable codes (LCCs).
arxiv:2610.38664.authors: Joshua Brakensiek, David Conlon, Venkatesan Guruswami, Xiaoyu He, Jiaxi Nie, Maya Sankar, Hung-Hsun Hans Yu

arxiv:2610.38669.title: The equal norm Grassmannian: topology and applications to frame fields
arxiv:2610.38669.summary: Given an orientable rank-$d$ vector bundle over a $d$-manifold, the Euler class is the unique obstruction to finding a nowhere-zero section. An equal norm Parseval frame is a certain collection of sections, one of whose properties is that the lengths of each vector at each point are equal. This makes the Euler class an obvious obstruction to finding such a frame.
arxiv:2610.38669.authors: Samuel A. Ballas, Ferhat Karabatman, Tom Needham, Clayton Shonkwiler

arxiv:2610.38670.title: Simple Cuts, Simple Landscapes: Global Synchronization and Rank-Width-One Matrices
arxiv:2610.38670.summary: We study how the structure of the coupling matrix $\boldsymbol A$ shapes the energy landscape $E_{\boldsymbol A}(\boldsymbol\theta)=-\frac12\sum_{i,j}A_{ij}\cos(\theta_i-\theta_j)$ of the Kuramoto model. We prove that, for an entrywise nonnegative coupling matrix $\boldsymbol A$ with connected support, if $\boldsymbol A$ has rank-width one over $\mathbb R$, then the landscape is "simple", i.e., every local minimum is synchronized. The rank-width bound is sharp, and the result has many interesting implications for global synchronization.

arxiv:2610.38674.title: Projected Brion's theorem
arxiv:2610.38674.summary: We present an analogue of Brion's theorem for the projected integer-point transform. Brion's theorem writes the integer-point transform of a rational polyhedron $P$ as the sum of the rational functions associated to its vertex cones. The pushforward $\pi_*$ along a lattice projection $\pi$ turns the transform of $P$ into the generating function of the numbers of lattice points in the fibres of $\pi$.

arxiv:2610.38698.title: Models of n-dimensional categories as $n\to\infty$
arxiv:2610.38698.summary: We verify that saturated complicial sets model the right limit of the $\infty$-categories of $(\infty,n)$-categories, whereas the canonical comparison with the left limit is not an equivalence. By contrast the category of strict $\omega$-categories is equivalent to both the right and left limits of the categories of strict $n$-categories.
arxiv:2610.38698.authors: Viktoriya Ozornova, Martina Rovelli, Tashi Walde

arxiv:2610.38703.title: Vietoris-Rips complexes of affine Coxeter groups
arxiv:2610.38703.summary: We prove that all affine Coxeter groups admit contractible Vietoris-Rips complexes. More precisely, for any affine Coxeter group $W_a$ there exists a finite generating set $A$ such that $\mathcal{VR}_t(W_a;A)$ is contractible for all $t\ge 1$. We prove this as a special case of a more general result about certain groups.
arxiv:2610.38703.authors: Riley Decker, Matthew C. B. Zaremsky

arxiv:2610.38710.title: Spontaneous Spirals in Spatial Systems
arxiv:2610.38710.summary: Several chemical and biological systems produce spontaneous spirals in their dynamical behavior, such as the Belousov-Zhabotinsky reaction in chemistry and the slime mold Dictyostelium in biology. In a previous study, such spiral wave formation was accurately replicated with a computational spatial system known as the Ideal Storage Cellular Automaton Model (ISCAM). Here, a more detailed investigation is presented of the ability of this model to generate spontaneous spirals depending on its parameter values.

arxiv:2610.38727.title: Existence of weak Landau-Ginzburg models for weighted complete intersections
arxiv:2610.38727.summary: We prove that every smooth well formed Fano or Calabi-Yau weighted complete intersection admits a nef-partition. As an application, we establish the existence of weak Landau-Ginzburg models for all such Fano weighted complete intersections.

arxiv:2610.38736.title: Transverse rational curves and the homogeneity of contact Fano manifolds
arxiv:2610.38736.summary: We prove that every smooth complex projective contact Fano manifold is homogeneous under its connected contact automorphism group. The argument extends and simplifies the incidence method of our earlier proof of the LeBrun--Salamon conjecture. After the classical reductions, balanced transverse rational maps through every point yield tangent sections extending across the nodal boundary.
arxiv:2610.38736.authors: Zhengyu Hu, Kefeng Liu, Xueyuan Wan

arxiv:2610.38751.title: Examples of rigid Twistor D-modules
arxiv:2610.38751.summary: The well-established theory of D-modules gives a framework to study linear differential equations from the perspective of algebraic geometry. A significant advancement in this theory has been the introduction of Twistor D-modules by Claude Sabbah and Takuro Mochizuki: These objects expose inherent, but hidden information of the underlying differential equations in an elegant way. We explain the foundational concepts of Twistor D-modules and give concrete examples of these objects.

arxiv:2610.38760.title: On a Conjecture of Fiedorowicz
arxiv:2610.38760.summary: Fiedorowicz conjectured that every finite simply connected CW complex is homotopy equivalent to the classifying space of a finite monoid. We prove this conjecture. Our main construction takes a finite monoid M and a map from a finite connected CW complex into the classifying space of M, and produces a new finite monoid whose classifying space is homotopy equivalent to the mapping cone of the given map.

arxiv:2610.38791.title: Discretisation in algebraic $K$-theory of independent ample groupoids and their Steinberg algebras
arxiv:2610.38791.summary: An independent ample groupoid $G$ comes equipped with a discrete groupoid $G_d$ and a proper \'etale correspondence $\Omega:G_d\to G$. Discretisation with respect to a homological invariant $\mathcal{H}$ holds when $\mathcal{H}(\Omega)$ is an equivalence. We show for example that discretisation with respect to the $K$-theory spectrum $\mathbb{K} \mathfrak{B}_G$ of the permutative category of bisections always holds, establish excision and continuity for this invariant, and use all this and explicit resolutions by independent groupoids to compute it for several families of ample groupoids.

arxiv:2610.38812.title: Dimensions of Fano schemes of lines on hypersurfaces
arxiv:2610.38812.summary: Let $X\subset\mathbb{P}^n_\mathbb{C}$ be a smooth hypersurface of degree $d\ge2$, with $n\ge3$. We prove that an $m$-dimensional integral projective family of lines sweeping a variety of dimension $y$ satisfies $m\le\max\{2y-d-1,n-3\}$. This proves the de Jong-Debarre conjecture for $d\le n$ and the Beheshti-Starr bound for lines on smooth hypersurfaces for $d\ge n+1$.

arxiv:2610.38819.title: Primitive flag-transitive generalized quadrangles
arxiv:2610.38819.summary: Let $\mathcal{Q}$ be a finite thick generalized quadrangle of order $(s,t)$ with a flag-transitive automorphism group $G$. A well-known conjecture of Kantor from the early 1990s asserts that up to duality, $\mathcal{Q}$ is either of classical type, or it is one of two sporadic examples of order $(3,5)$ or $(15,17)$. Although this fundamental problem in finite geometry remains open, it has been resolved in some special cases.
arxiv:2610.38819.authors: Timothy C. Burness, Tao Feng, Jianbing Lu

arxiv:2610.38837.title: Intrinsic Non-Reductive Geometric Invariant Theory and Moduli Spaces of Principal Bundles with Non-Reductive Structure Groups
arxiv:2610.38837.summary: We prove the existence of moduli spaces for algebraic stacks with a weak action of $\Theta = [\mathbb{A}^1/\mathbb{G}_m]$ (including stacks of filtered objects and unstable $\Theta$-strata) for which the center admits a good moduli space and the retraction to the center has flat, finitely presented relative inertia, providing a stack-intrinsic generalization of the existence of non-reductive Geometric Invariant Theory quotients. As an application, we construct quasi-projective coarse moduli spaces of principal bundles over a smooth projective curve with non-reductive structure groups, including moduli spaces of Ramanathan unstable principal bundles of fixed Harder--Narasimhan type.
