arxiv:2610.38845.title: The geometry of Floquet states
arxiv:2610.38845.summary: This paper studies the moduli space of "good" periodic Hamiltonians, i.e., periodic Hamiltonians with nondegenerate Floquet spectrum. The corresponding Floquet states determine a geometric model for the moduli space of such Hamiltonians. The model is expressed in terms of configuration spaces, flag manifolds, and principal bundles.
arxiv:2610.38845.authors: Vladimir Y. Cherynak, John R. Klein

arxiv:2610.38849.title: Extended weak order in all rank three Coxeter groups
arxiv:2610.38849.summary: We prove that extended weak order is a lattice for all rank 3 Coxeter groups. This was previously known in finite and affine types, and in the universal Coxeter group of rank 3. All other cases are new to this paper.
arxiv:2610.38849.authors: Grant Barkley, Colin Defant, Patricia Hersh, Jon McCammond, Thomas McConville, David E Speyer

arxiv:2610.38859.title: On strongly FP-injective accessibility and weakly FP-projective periodicity
arxiv:2610.38859.summary: Accessibility results are established for (Cartan-Eilenberg) strongly FP-injective complexes, by first proving the accessibility of Strongly FP-injective modules and then utilizing the pseudopullback theorem. We also prove that every acyclic complex of weakly FP-projective modules has weakly FP-projective cycles over left $<\aleph_m$-coherent rings for a non-negative integer $m$. This is achieved by introducing the cotorsion pairs $\bigl(\mathcal{C}\aleph_mP\text{-}proj,\mathcal{C}\aleph_mP\text{-}inj\bigr)$, cogenerated by all $\aleph_m$-presentable weakly FP-projective modules, and proving that acyclic complexes of modules from the class $\mathcal{C}\aleph_mP\text{-}proj$ have weakly…

arxiv:2610.38864.title: All-even sets in $\mathbb{R}^2$ and $\mathbb{R}^3$
arxiv:2610.38864.summary: Call a finite nonempty point set $S\subset\mathbb{R}^d$ all-even if for every direction $\ell \in \mathbb{P}(\mathbb{R}^d)$, the number of hyperplanes perpendicular to $\ell$ that intersect $S$ is even. In 2026, Francisco Santos presented a question of Juan Benigno Seoane-Sep\'ulveda on the existence of all-even sets in dimensions $3$ and higher, together with examples of such sets in dimension $2$. Call a set $S\in\mathbb{R}^d$ line-all-even if for every direction $\ell \in \mathbb{P}(\mathbb{R}^d)$ the number of lines parallel to $\ell$ that intersect $S$ is even.

arxiv:2610.38866.title: Early warning of critical transitions: Distinguishing supercritical and subcritical bifurcations from noisy observations
arxiv:2610.38866.summary: Early-warning methods can indicate that a system is approaching a loss of stability, but they do not usually reveal whether the approaching bifurcation is supercritical or subcritical. We investigate whether this distinction can be made from noisy pre-transition observations. For this investigation, we extend a regression-based stability method by including the leading cubic nonlinear term, whose sign is used to predict the bifurcation type.
arxiv:2610.38866.authors: Paul A. Sanders, Christian Kuehn, Bastian Hilder, Robbin Bastiaansen

arxiv:2610.38875.title: The bigraded Frobenius series of the wreath product superspace coinvariant rings
arxiv:2610.38875.summary: We determine the bigraded Frobenius series of the superspace coinvariant ring $R^{(1,1)}_{\mathbb{Z}_r\wr\mathfrak{S}_n}$ for the wreath products $\mathbb{Z}_r\wr\mathfrak{S}_n$, which is the quotient of the ring $\mathbb{C}[x_1,\ldots,x_n]\otimes\bigwedge[\theta_1,\ldots,\theta_n]$ of polynomial-valued differential forms by the ideal generated by diagonal $\mathbb{Z}_r\wr\mathfrak{S}_n$-invariants with vanishing constant term. The bigraded multiplicity of each irreducible character is a sum over standard Young $r$-tableaux of an expression determined by the flag major index and flag descent number. This refines the Frobenius series graded by fermionic degree found by Bhattacharya--Rhoades…
arxiv:2610.38875.authors: Sutanay Bhattacharya, Sylvie Corteel, Yuhan Jiang, John Lentfer, Brendon Rhoades

arxiv:2610.38900.title: Sharp dimension bounds for right-angled hyperbolic polytopes
arxiv:2610.38900.summary: We determine the largest dimensions in which right-angled hyperbolic polytopes of finite volume can exist. The dimension is at most eight in general, and at most four when all vertices lie at infinity. Both bounds are attained, improving the previously known upper bounds of twelve and six.

arxiv:2610.38912.title: Finite-size ignition laws near a vanishing branching deficit on near-regular simple graphs
arxiv:2610.38912.summary: We study heterogeneous bootstrap percolation on uniform simple graphs with prescribed degrees of mean $d\to\infty$ and deviations at most $C\sqrt d$. Thresholds are independently one with probability $(1-c/d)/d$ and two otherwise; seeds form an independent uniform set of prescribed size $a$. Let $T_a$ be the terminal number of active vertices and $b$ be one minus the mean number of threshold-one descendants of a reached vertex.

arxiv:2610.38919.title: A Gasch\"utz Lemma for linear algebraic groups with applications to the Riemann-Hilbert correspondence
arxiv:2610.38919.summary: The classical Gasch\"utz Lemma states that for a surjective morphism $G\to H$ of finite groups, generators $h_1,\ldots,h_d$ of $H$ can be lifted to generators $g_1,\ldots,g_d$ of $G$, provided that $G$ can be generated by $d$ elements. We prove an analog of this statement for linear algebraic groups. This has applications to the algebraic-geometric theory of linear differential equations: We show that every regular singular differential embedding problem over the rational function field has a regular singular solution.

arxiv:2610.38927.title: $L$-Space Knots in $\mathfrak{sl}_{n}$-like Knot Floer Homology
arxiv:2610.38927.summary: It has been of particular interest in recent years to relate categorifications of quantum knot invariants like the Jones polynomial to Floer-theoretic invariants like knot Floer homology using spectral sequences. In pursuit of Rasmussen's conjecture, Dowlin constructed a family of invariants with properties like those of Khovanov and Rozansky's $\mathfrak{sl}_n$-homology theories. In this paper, we explore these invariants for $L$-space knots and thin knots.

arxiv:2610.38941.title: Anchored isoperimetry in percolation
arxiv:2610.38941.summary: We show that, for any infinite transitive graph $G$, the infinite cluster after supercritical percolation almost surely inherits the anchored isoperimetry of $G$. Moreover, the probability of violating the corresponding isoperimetric inequality decays exponentially in the isoperimetric profile of the host graph. This was previously known only for nonamenable transitive graphs, $\mathbb{Z}^d$, and very recently for transitive graphs of polynomial growth.
arxiv:2610.38941.authors: Sahar Diskin, Lyuben Lichev, Ritvik Ramanan Radhakrishnan, Benny Sudakov, Laury Verhoeven

arxiv:2610.38949.title: The Oriented Freudenthal Suspension Theorem
arxiv:2610.38949.summary: The Freudenthal Suspension Theorem states that the connectivity of the unit map $X\rightarrow\Omega\Sigma X$ of the suspension-loop adjunction for a pointed space $X$ is twice the connectivity of $X$ itself. We extend this theorem to $X$ being a pointed $(\infty,\infty)$-category, i.e. an oriented space in the sense of Gepner--Heine.

arxiv:2610.38952.title: PBW theorem for affine super Yangian
arxiv:2610.38952.summary: We prove a Poincar\'e--Birkhoff--Witt theorem for the distinguished affine super Yangian $Y=Y_{1/2,1/2}(\widehat{\mathfrak{sl}}(m|n))$, where $m,n\geq2$ and $m\neq n$. With respect to the current filtration, there is a canonical isomorphism \[ \operatorname{gr}_F Y\cong U\!\left(\operatorname{uce}\!\left( \mathfrak{sl}(m|n)\otimes\mathbb C[z^{\pm1},u] \right)\right), \] where $\operatorname{uce}$ denotes the universal central extension. For any totally ordered classical basis homogeneous in parity and current degree, ordered supermonomials in arbitrary fixed filtered lifts form a vector-space basis of $Y$, with odd exponents restricted to zero or one.

arxiv:2610.38963.title: Amitsur groups of Imprimitive Fano Threefolds
arxiv:2610.38963.summary: We classify possible Amitsur groups of smooth imprimitive Fano threefolds defined over $\cc$ that admit a faithful action of a finite group.

arxiv:2610.38971.title: Regular closedness off the real axis for root closures of bounded-height integer polynomials
arxiv:2610.38971.summary: For each integer $h\ge1$, let $Z_h$ be the closure in the complex plane of the roots of nonzero integer polynomials whose coefficients have absolute value at most $h$, with no degree restriction. We prove that $Z_h$ is regular closed off the real axis: every non-real point of $Z_h$ is a limit of interior points. The root-closure identification of Espigul\'e and Juher, for which we include a self-contained proof, shows that the same closure arises from monic polynomials and that outside the closed unit disc it is the connectedness locus of $h+1$ equally spaced collinear similarities.

arxiv:2610.38972.title: Spectral Structures on Vector Bundles
arxiv:2610.38972.summary: We develop an intrinsic theory of spectral structures on holomorphic vector bundles over compact Riemann surfaces, generalising eigenspace decompositions without eigenvalues. Their geometric realisations are presentations of vector bundles as pushforwards of line bundles along finite branched covers. We construct their analytic moduli stack locally of finite presentation and identify it with the relative Picard stack of the universal family of finite covers.

arxiv:2610.38979.title: Non-concordant 2-links in simply-connected 4-manifolds
arxiv:2610.38979.summary: We construct an infinite family of smooth 2-component links of 2-spheres $\Sigma_k\subset S^2\times S^2$ whose respective components are smoothly concordant but which are pairwise not topologically concordant in any topological $\mathbb{Z}$-homology cobordism. In particular, the $\Sigma_k$ are pairwise non-concordant in $(S^2\times S^2)\times[0,1]$.

arxiv:2610.38995.title: Networks with Memory and Isospectral Reduction
arxiv:2610.38995.summary: Restricting the linear dynamics of a graph to selected vertices generally introduces memory, because interactions can pass through hidden vertices before returning. The resulting rational memory kernels give isospectral reduction a dynamical interpretation and identify latent graph symmetries with symmetries of the observed evolution.

arxiv:2610.38996.title: Graftings and cograftings for species
arxiv:2610.38996.summary: We introduce graftings and cograftings for vector species, modelled on the elementary operations of adjoining and deleting a root in a rooted forest. We relate these maps to operads, up and down operators, and obtain nontrivial balanced pairs, admitting pair of creation/annihilation operators with commuting relations. We establish universal properties for the species of rooted forests.

arxiv:2610.39010.title: Positivity of the Mirabolic Quantum Groups
arxiv:2610.39010.summary: In this paper, we construct the canonical basis for the modified mirabolic quantum $\mathfrak{sl}_n$. We then study the associated $\dot{U}_v(\mathfrak{sl}_n)$-module and $\dot{U}_v(\mathfrak{sl}_n)$-comodule structures and prove the positivity of this basis with respect to these two structures.
arxiv:2610.39010.authors: Zhaobing Fan, Haitao Ma, Zhicheng Zhang

arxiv:2610.39021.title: Hook monomial immanants are Kazhdan-Lusztig positive
arxiv:2610.39021.summary: Stembridge conjectured that every monomial immanant is non-negative on totally non-negative matrices, and Haiman proposed a stronger statement which at $q=1$ says that every monomial immanant is a non-negative integer combination of the Kazhdan-Lusztig immanants of Rhoades and Skandera. We prove this for every hook shape $(a,1^{n-a})$ and every $n$. More precisely, each of the per-vertex functions obtained by splitting Stembridge's formula for hook characters is Kazhdan-Lusztig positive.

arxiv:2610.39032.title: A proof of the Murty--Simon conjecture on diameter-$2$-critical graphs
arxiv:2610.39032.summary: The Murty-Simon conjecture states that every $n$-vertex diameter-$2$-critical graph has at most $\lfloor n^2/4 \rfloor$ edges, with equality only for the balanced complete bipartite graph. Using regularity methods, F\"uredi proved this for all sufficiently large $n$ (specifically, $n$ greater than a tower of $2$'s of height roughly $10^{14}$). We present a proof of the Murty-Simon conjecture that works for all $n$.

arxiv:2610.39033.title: Large deviations for random walks generated by countable groups: a unified approach
arxiv:2610.39033.summary: We present a unified treatment of various large deviation principles in the context of random walks induced by actions of countable groups. The fundamental notion undergirding the global perspective is that of weakly almost additive random walks, inspired by earlier works on the metric geometry of group actions as well as by recent developments in the theory of nonadditive thermodynamic formalism. We treat large deviations of the renormalized vector-valued distance function from the origin for groups acting simultaneously, by isometries and in a weakly almost additive fashion, on an arbitrary number of metric spaces.

arxiv:2610.39035.title: Comparing metric completions of triangulated categories with Verdier quotients
arxiv:2610.39035.summary: Neeman's metric on a triangulated category assigns lengths to morphisms and allows us to construct triangulated metric completions of the category. We prove that the metric completion of a triangulated category with respect to a constant metric is always a subcategory of the Verdier quotient by the thick subcategory generated by cones of zero-length morphisms, and we provide a sufficient criterion for equality. To that end, we define continuous functors between completions which induce triangulated functors between completions.

arxiv:2610.39061.title: Bases for the Top-Degree Garsia-Haiman Module
arxiv:2610.39061.summary: We introduce two new monomial bases for the top $t$-degree component of the Garsia-Haiman module $V_\mu$ for every partition $\mu$. Both bases are indexed by column-strict standard fillings of shape $\mu$; the first has exponents governed by entrywise refinements of Haglund's combinatorial statistics for the modified Macdonald polynomials $\widetilde{H}_\mu(X;q,t)$. The second basis has exponents governed by an insertion algorithm of Bhattacharya-Ratheesh-Viswanath, and gives a basis realization of the ``fermionic formula" of the $m_{1^n}$-coefficient of the $q$-Whittaker polynomial.

arxiv:2610.39077.title: A lattice path model for Schubert and forest polynomials: positivity and combinatorial interpretations
arxiv:2610.39077.summary: In this paper, we give combinatorial interpretations of (i) the Graham-positive coefficients in the expansion of double Schur polynomials in the double fundamental quasisymmetric basis and (ii) the coefficients in the expansion of Grothendieck polynomials in the grove basis. To obtain these interpretations, we construct a common lattice path model for Schubert, Grothendieck, and double Schubert polynomials and their respective quasisymmetric counterparts: forest, grove, and double forest polynomials. The first interpretation answers a question of Bergeron, Gagnon, Nadeau, Spink, and Tewari asking for an explicit combinatorial interpretation of the coefficients.

arxiv:2610.39078.title: Borsuk number in four dimensions is at most seven
arxiv:2610.39078.summary: We prove that every bounded set of diameter one in four-dimensional Euclidean space can be covered by seven balls of diameter strictly smaller than $0.9999$. In particular, the Borsuk number satisfies $b_4\le7$. The proof combines geometric arguments based on contact points of the circumball with an exact finite computation.
arxiv:2610.39078.authors: Andrii Arman, Andriy Bondarenko, Andriy Prymak, Danylo Radchenko

arxiv:2610.39085.title: Weighted Tur\'an densities for hypergraphs
arxiv:2610.39085.summary: Bondy and Tuza generalized the Tur\'an problem for graphs to weighted graphs. Subsequently, F\"uredi and K\"undgen gave a solution in the case of cliques. We consider the weighted Tur\'an problem on hypergraphs and prove the first tight asymptotic result for 3-uniform hypergraphs.
arxiv:2610.39085.authors: David James, Bernard Lidick\'y, Dhruv Mubayi

arxiv:2610.39092.title: Finding solutions with the Borsuk-Ulam theorem
arxiv:2610.39092.summary: Many existence theorems in combinatorics and geometry reduce to the Borsuk-Ulam theorem or its generalizations. We study how these existence arguments can be turned into effective numerical methods when a simple example with a single known solution is available. The idea is to deform this example into the given problem and follow its solution during the deformation.

arxiv:2610.39102.title: Logarithmic transformations on the six-sphere
arxiv:2610.39102.summary: We show that there are infinitely many choices of the multiplicities in the logarithmic transformation step of the Alp\"oge--Claude construction which produce a complex threefold diffeomorphic to the six-sphere. Moreover, distinct choices of the multiplicities yield biholomorphically inequivalent complex structures.

arxiv:2610.39103.title: The inverse problem for Julia limiting directions in the Eremenko--Lyubich class
arxiv:2610.39103.summary: We study the inverse problem for Julia limiting directions in the Eremenko-Lyubich class $\mathcal B$, which is the class of transcendental entire functions with a bounded set of singular values, and its meromorphic generalization $\mathcal B_{mer}$. Every nonempty compact subset of the circle can be the set of Julia limiting directions of an entire $f\in\mathcal B$. For finite unions of nondegenerate closed arcs, the corresponding $f\in\mathcal B$, even with every finite order at or above an explicit bound determined by the arc lengths, can be attained.
arxiv:2610.39103.authors: Jiaxing Huang, Jun Wang, Xiao Yao

arxiv:2610.39107.title: Minimally-coupled Quasilinear Symmetric Hyperbolic Systems, Naturally
arxiv:2610.39107.summary: We consider symmetric hyperbolicity and well-posedness in the context of natural equations, which are closed subobjects of jet bundles over natural bundles. We show how non-natural equations can be "naturalized", and we discuss how a precise version of "minimal coupling" offers a (provably unique, up to isomorphism) method for constructing natural equations from certain equations defined on a single manifold. We discuss how to define symmetrizers, hyperbolizations, and constraints for minimally coupled natural equations, and we show how these can be used to recover standard existence and uniqueness results, relative to any choice of background structure (a metric, for minimally coupled…

arxiv:2610.39113.title: Frequency-induced Tipping: Resonance-Driven Tipping in a Threshold Predator-Prey System
arxiv:2610.39113.summary: Tipping points refer to abrupt, substantial, and often irreversible transitions in dynamic systems that can be triggered by minor perturbations. Existing tipping mechanisms are usually classified by the nature of the trigger: bifurcation-induced tipping occurs when a parameter crosses a critical threshold, noise-induced tipping is caused by random perturbations, rate-induced tipping occurs when a system fails to track a moving attractor, and phase-induced tipping is triggered by timed perturbations relative to an oscillatory state. In this paper, we identify a new mechanism for tipping: frequency-induced tipping, in which periodic forcing drives a transition through resonant amplification.
arxiv:2610.39113.authors: Shan Gao, Silas Poloni, Hao Wang, Mark Lewis

arxiv:2610.39116.title: Some results on intersecting families of triangulations
arxiv:2610.39116.summary: Kalai conjectured that the largest intersecting family of triangulations of an $n$-gon is the family consisting of all triangulations that contain a fixed ear (a chord of length $2$). What happens if we strengthen the intersecting condition to the condition that any two of the triangulations must intersect on a chord from a specified family of chords -- for example, what if any two triangulations intersect on a chord from some fixed point of the $n$-gon, or intersect on an ear? In this paper we verify Kalai's conjecture for families of triangulations in which any two intersect on a chord from some fixed point.

arxiv:2610.39120.title: CA2 numbers and the Riemann hypothesis: a numerical investigation of Ramanujan's inequalities
arxiv:2610.39120.summary: Robin's criterion reduces the Riemann hypothesis to an inequality for colossally abundant (CA) numbers, and Wu's theorem reduces the test further to the subclass CA2. We study this reduction numerically and consider smaller subsets on which the same criterion remains sufficient. We also show that the logarithmic decay law suggested by Briggs's computations follows from Ramanujan's conditional bounds.
arxiv:2610.39120.authors: Dmitry R. Leshchiner, Oleg R. Musin, James Thompson

arxiv:2610.39127.title: The inverse local-relative correspondence and the Nekrasov--Shatashvili vanishing blowup equation
arxiv:2610.39127.summary: We prove the Nekrasov--Shatashvili vanishing blowup equation for the local Gromov--Witten theory of smooth weak del Pezzo surfaces, by identifying its unique formal solution with the inverse of the local-relative correspondence. We construct this inverse through an associative set-partition convolution and establish the identification using Zagier's recursion for the Bloch--Okounkov $n$-point function. The proof applies in all genera and includes non-toric surfaces.
arxiv:2610.39127.authors: Jianjun Fu, Shuai Guo, Qingsheng Zhang

arxiv:2610.39176.title: Simplified dense model theorem for random discrete structures
arxiv:2610.39176.summary: Dense model theorems of Conlon and Gowers associate to each subset of a sparse random structure a dense set with approximately the same size and configuration counts after rescaling. This allows dense extremal results to be transferred to the random setting. Allen, B\"ottcher, Lada, and Mergoni Cecchelli recently generalised this approach and established a dense model theorem in an abstract hypergraph framework, with hypotheses that are readily verified in many applications.

arxiv:2610.39187.title: Generalized Discrete Fractal Dimensions of Graph Families
arxiv:2610.39187.summary: Quantifying the self-similarity of complex networks via discrete fractal dimensions is a fundamental problem in network science. In this paper, we investigate some general fractal dimensions of graph families based on q-energy and R\'enyi entropy. We first establish several bounds for the energy, and then discuss the monotonicity, measure invariance of the dimensions, as well as some concrete graph families.
arxiv:2610.39187.authors: Jiantao Liu, Cheng Zeng, Yumei Xue, Qingcheng Zeng

arxiv:2610.39228.title: Every group is the automorphism group of a set-theoretic solution of the Yang--Baxter equation
arxiv:2610.39228.summary: We give an affirmative answer to the abstract group problem for the category $\YB$ of all set-theoretic solutions of the Yang--Baxter (YB) equation: every group is isomorphic to the automorphism group of a YB-solution, which can be chosen on a finite set if the group is finite. In the terminology of L\'aszl\'o Babai, this means that the category $\YB$ is universal and finitely universal, which is an analogue of Frucht's classical theorem for graphs. Furthermore, the YB-solutions can be chosen within three very small classes: the solutions of the Frobenius-Separability equation, the solutions of the Baaj--Long--Skandalis equation and the recently introduced bipartite solutions.

arxiv:2610.39235.title: Error terms for sums of two linear transformations
arxiv:2610.39235.summary: Let $d$ be a positive integer, and let $\mathcal L_1,\mathcal L_2$ be irreducible and coprime linear transformations from $\mathbb{Z}^d$ to $\mathbb{Z}^d$. In this paper, we prove that, for every finite nonempty set $A\subseteq\mathbb{Z}^d$, \[ |\mathcal L_1A+\mathcal L_2A| \ge \left(|\det\mathcal L_1|^{1/d}+|\det\mathcal L_2|^{1/d}\right)^d|A|-O\left(|A|^{1-1/d}\right). \] This confirms the conjecture of Conlon and Lim on the error term for two linear transformations.

arxiv:2610.39242.title: The Liouville property for geometric graphs in the plane
arxiv:2610.39242.summary: We show that every bounded discrete harmonic function with respect to the cotangent Laplacian on a Delaunay triangulation of the Euclidean plane is constant; equivalently, the cotangent-weighted triangulation has the Liouville property. Our main theorem establishes this property for a more general class of connected weighted geometric graphs in the plane. Furthermore, we show that a planar Delaunay triangulation with cotangent weights could be transient but is recurrent if edge lengths are uniformly bounded.
arxiv:2610.39242.authors: Kuijun Liu, Feng Luo, Yanwen Luo, Zhenghao Rao

arxiv:2610.39257.title: The Stable Tamari Lattice
arxiv:2610.39257.summary: We introduce the stable Tamari lattice $\mathcal{ST}_n$, an infinite lattice on $\mathbb{N}^n$. The $r$-Tamari lattices on $r$-Dyck paths of height $n+1$ occur as a nested family of principal lower order ideals whose union is $\mathcal{ST}_n$. Partition-indexed principal lower order ideals recover the $\nu$-Tamari lattices associated with partition boundaries.
arxiv:2610.39257.authors: Herman Chau, Spencer Daugherty, Sean Grate, Mark D. Haiman, Juan Carlos Mart\'inez Mori, Anna Pun

arxiv:2610.39281.title: Dynamic invisibility of implicit and nested state-dependent delays in a class of externally forced delay equations
arxiv:2610.39281.summary: Delayed feedback is a fundamental mechanism in many systems and is often modeled by delay differential equations (DDEs). While delays are frequently assumed to be constant, in realistic feedback processes they may depend on the state and even be defined implicitly or in a nested fashion by the feedback relation itself. In this work, we address the question of how such implicit and nested state-dependent delays affect the observed behavior of a class of externally forced systems with negative switched feedback.
arxiv:2610.39281.authors: Samuel Bolduc-St-Aubin, Priya Subramanian, Bernd Krauskopf

arxiv:2610.39284.title: Generalized Iskovskikh surfaces and unirationality of del Pezzo surfaces of degree $2$
arxiv:2610.39284.summary: We introduce generalized Iskovskikh surfaces and study their relation to quasi-\'etale double covers. As an application, we prove that a del Pezzo surface of degree $2$ over an infinite field of characteristic different from $2$ is unirational if it has a rational generalized Eckardt point. This resolves a previously open case not covered by Manin's construction.

arxiv:2610.39298.title: On two problems concerning the geodesic transversal number of graphs
arxiv:2610.39298.summary: We establish sharp upper and lower bounds on the geodesic transversal number of hypercubes. We also obtain a lower bound on the geodesic transversal number of Hamming graphs. As applications, we provide negative answers to two open problems concerning the geodesic transversal number.
arxiv:2610.39298.authors: Shi Chen, Xuanlong Ma, Tingzeng Wu

arxiv:2610.39317.title: Linear hereditary quasirandomness
arxiv:2610.39317.summary: Conlon, Fox and Sudakov (\emph{Math. Proc. Cambridge Philos.

arxiv:2610.39318.title: Pre-modular fusion categories of global dimension $2p$
arxiv:2610.39318.summary: Let $p>5$ be a prime. In this paper, we show that a pre-modular fusion category of global dimension $2p$ is either pointed or tensor equivalent to $\text{Rep}(D_{2p})$.

arxiv:2610.39336.title: Point Corrections and Wall-Crossing Geometry on the Quintic del Pezzo Threefold
arxiv:2610.39336.summary: Let $X=V_5$ be the quintic del Pezzo threefold. Along the negative zero-tilt-slope paths for rational-curve ideal classes, degree five is the first degree admitting a positive point correction. We determine the resulting degree-five outer good moduli space: it is reduced with exactly two irreducible components, a normal ten-dimensional principal branch and a smooth corrected branch $X\times\mathrm{Gr}(2,7)$.

arxiv:2610.39364.title: A Uniform Upper Bound on the Length of MDS Codes from Genus-Two Curves
arxiv:2610.39364.summary: We study the maximal length of MDS algebraic geometry codes from genus-two curves over finite fields. Let $C_\mathcal{ L}(D,G)$ be such a code over $\mathbb F_q$, with length $n$ and dimension $k$. Assume that $3\leq k\leq n-3$.

arxiv:2610.39366.title: Graded Automorphism of Multiparameter Quantum Matrix Algebra
arxiv:2610.39366.summary: We determine the graded automorphism group of the multiparameter quantum matrix algebra $\mathcal O_{\lambda,\mathbf p}(M_n(\Bbbk))$ over an arbitrary field $\Bbbk$ for all $n\ge2$ and $\lambda\ne1$. No other restrictions are assumed on $\mathbf p$ or $\lambda$. Every graded automorphism is a torus automorphism, possibly followed by transposition or by simultaneous reversal of the row and column indices.

arxiv:2610.39368.title: Bloch's conjecture for (anti-)symplectic automorphisms of K3 surfaces
arxiv:2610.39368.summary: We prove Bloch's conjecture for (anti-)symplectic automorphisms of smooth projective complex K3 surfaces of Picard number two. Together with the recent result for abelian surfaces and the known K3 cases, this settles the remaining case of Bloch's conjecture for (anti-)symplectic automorphisms of smooth projective complex surfaces with trivial canonical bundle. More generally, we prove Bloch's conjecture for (anti-)symplectic derived autoequivalences of projective K3 surfaces whose Picard number is at least three, or is two with anisotropic N\'eron--Severi lattice.

arxiv:2610.39430.title: Diameter-two graphs whose mutual-visibility chromatic number equals their chromatic number
arxiv:2610.39430.summary: A set $S$ of vertices of a graph $G$ is a mutual-visibility set if every pair of vertices of $S$ is joined by a shortest path whose internal vertices avoid $S$, and the mutual-visibility chromatic number $\chi_\mu(G)$ is the least number of mutual-visibility sets into which $V(G)$ can be partitioned. Klav\v{z}ar, Kuziak, Valenzuela Tripodoro and Yero (2025) proved that $\chi_\mu(G)\le\chi(G)$ whenever $G$ has diameter two, observed that equality holds for complete bipartite graphs, and asked whether there are any other diameter-two graphs attaining equality. We answer this question in the affirmative.

arxiv:2610.39440.title: A short proof of the Segal conjecture for $C_p$
arxiv:2610.39440.summary: We give a new proof of the generalized Segal conjecture for the cyclic group of prime order p, i.e. the fact that the Tate diagonal of any bounded below spectrum is a p-completion. The idea, inspired by Hahn and Wilson's argument, is to use descent along the equivariant map from the p-fold tensor power of the field with p elements to its topological Hochschild homology. The only computational input that we use is the calculation of the homotopy rings of this topological Hochschild homology and its Tate construction, together with the map induced by the cyclotomic Frobenius.

arxiv:2610.39443.title: The entropy spectra of chaotic maps of an interval
arxiv:2610.39443.summary: For a continuous self-map f of a real interval L, let ent(f) denote the supremum of the topological entropies of the restrictions of f to its compact invariant sets; for a compact interval this is the usual topological entropy. For a class P of maps, the entropy spectrum of P is the set of values ent(f) taken by the maps f in P. We determine the entropy spectra of the three standard classes of chaotic maps of the compact interval [0,1].

arxiv:2610.39445.title: Tur\'{a}n numbers for suspensions of bipartite 2-regular graphs
arxiv:2610.39445.summary: For a graph $R$, let $\widehat R:=K_1+R$ denote its suspension, obtained by adding a new vertex adjacent to every vertex of $R$. For every fixed nonempty bipartite $2$-regular graph $R$, we determine $\operatorname{ex}(n,\widehat{R})$ for all sufficiently large $n$ and characterize all extremal graphs. Three distinct cases arise, according as $R$ is $2C_6$, a disjoint union of copies of $C_4$, or neither of these.

arxiv:2610.39448.title: Arithmetic localization for quasiperiodic long-range operators with monotone potentials
arxiv:2610.39448.summary: We study one-dimensional quasiperiodic operators with $\alpha$-H\"older monotone potentials and long-range hopping satisfying $|T(x,y)|\leq \varepsilon e^{-\rho |x-y|}$. Under an explicit smallness condition on $\varepsilon$, we establish uniform Anderson localization for such operators in the regime $\rho>\alpha\beta $, where $\beta$ is the exponential strength of frequency resonances. Our proof extends the arithmetic localization strategy for monotone quasiperiodic Schr\"odinger operators by Jitomirskaya and Kachkovskiy to the long-range setting, without relying on the Lyapunov exponent.

arxiv:2610.39456.title: Affinizations and braided module categories
arxiv:2610.39456.summary: We relate affinizations of braided monoidal categories to braided module categories, allowing a twist by a braided monoidal automorphism. Our main theorem establishes a bijection between twisted braided structures on a right module category and extensions of its action to the corresponding twisted affinization. We also show that the twisted affinization is the free twisted braided module category on one object.
arxiv:2610.39456.authors: Hadi Salmasian, Alistair Savage, Yaolong Shen

arxiv:2610.39460.title: A polynomial method over formal power series
arxiv:2610.39460.summary: We give new upper bounds on families of integer vectors with prescribed coordinate multiplicities and a forbidden scalar product. Our method uses coefficient functions over formal power series and recovers the Frankl--Wilson bound for binary vectors. For vectors in $\{-1,0,1\}^n$, we obtain an exponential improvement over the ordinary polynomial count in a wide range; in certain regimes, we determine the lower limit of the exponential base.
arxiv:2610.39460.authors: Artur Akhiiarov, Mikhail Koshelev, Andrey Kupavskii, Andrei Raigorodskii

arxiv:2610.39461.title: The maximum number of triangles in regular graphs
arxiv:2610.39461.summary: We determine the maximum number of triangles in $n$-vertex $k$-regular graphs and characterize all extremal graphs for all admissible orders when $k$ is odd and for an explicit range of orders when $k$ is even. For even $k$, we also give explicit lower and upper bounds for the remaining orders. As a consequence, we obtain a lower bound on the number of independent sets of size three in $k$-regular graphs and characterize all equality cases.
arxiv:2610.39461.authors: Ya-Hong Chen, Shi-Cai Gong, Changhong Lu, Zhuojie Tu, Long-Tu Yuan

arxiv:2610.39462.title: Balancing tautological intersection numbers
arxiv:2610.39462.summary: We prove the three balancing inequalities conjectured by the authors about 20 years ago: moving one unit from a larger index to a smaller one cannot decrease a mixed tautological intersection number, whether the two distinguished insertions are psi classes, kappa classes, or Hodge Chern classes.

arxiv:2610.39469.title: Guaranteed indirect delivery in directed networks: The joint extremal function and explicit attaining constructions
arxiv:2610.39469.summary: A messenger and a pursuer move alternately on a finite loopless directed graph, with complete information and waiting permitted. The messenger moves first and wins upon reaching a designated recipient, before interception there. We determine the maximum number $M(n,m)$ of ordered nonadjacent source--recipient pairs for which delivery is guaranteed against every initial pursuer position, among graphs with $n$ vertices and $m$ arcs.

arxiv:2610.39474.title: Higher order unknotting numbers for knots and links
arxiv:2610.39474.summary: Ohyama, Taniyama and Yamada showed that finite type knot invariants are insensitive to the unknotting number: for any integer n and any knot K, there is an unknotting number 1 knot which cannot be distinguished from K by any finite type invariant of order $\le n$. We generalize this result in three directions. First, we prove an analogous result for all higher order unknotting number given by $C_n$-moves.
arxiv:2610.39474.authors: Jean-Baptiste Meilhan, Harumi Ogita, Akira Yasuhara

arxiv:2610.39481.title: $e$-Positive caterpillars have maximum degree at most three
arxiv:2610.39481.summary: Dahlberg, She, and van Willigenburg conjectured that every $e$-positive tree has maximum degree at most three. We prove this conjecture for caterpillars. Our proof introduces a specialization--cone method: we evaluate chromatic symmetric functions under finite-support specializations that are nonnegative on the elementary symmetric functions, express the evaluations through transfer matrices, and certify negativity using finitely generated cones.
arxiv:2610.39481.authors: Davion Q. B. Tang, David G. L. Wang, Monica M. Y. Wang

arxiv:2610.39485.title: Strongly explicit Ramanujan 2-lift towers via Hilbert modular forms
arxiv:2610.39485.summary: Expander graphs have been central objects of study for over fifty years. Ramanujan graphs attain the asymptotically optimal nontrivial adjacency-eigenvalue threshold for infinite fixed-degree families. The original arithmetic constructions by Lubotzky-Phillips-Sarnak (1988) and Margulis (1988), and the iterative $2$-lift method of Bilu-Linial (2006) provide different approaches to Ramanujan graph constructions.
arxiv:2610.39485.authors: Olga Kharlampovich, Igor Pak, Alina Vdovina

arxiv:2610.39486.title: On the Tur\'an Number of the Cartesian Product of Two Stars
arxiv:2610.39486.summary: We study the Tur\'an number of the Cartesian product of two stars, a family whose order of magnitude is known. For most pairs of star sizes, we determine the leading coefficient exactly. In the remaining congruence class, we give explicit lower and upper bounds for the coefficient at the leading scale.

arxiv:2610.39490.title: A Sharp Bound of Crossing Limit Cycle for Planar piecewise linear Systems with a Straight Switching Line
arxiv:2610.39490.summary: Determining the maximum number of crossing limit cycles in planar discontinuous piecewise linear systems separated by a straight line is a central problem in nonsmooth dynamical systems and a natural piecewise-linear counterpart of Hilbert's sixteenth problem, yet its sharp uniform upper bound has long remained an open problem. In this paper, we prove that any such system admits at most three crossing limit cycles. Combined with known examples realizing three crossing limit cycles, this result establishes that three is the sharp uniform upper bound.

arxiv:2610.39498.title: Poincar\'e series of degree-two Chow varieties
arxiv:2610.39498.summary: Let $C_{p, 2}(\mathbb{P}^{n})$ denote the Chow variety parametrizing effective algebraic $p$-cycles of degree two on $\mathbb{P}^{n}$. We show that its rational cohomology is pure Tate and concentrated in even degrees. An anti-invariant Chern class identity yields a presentation of the cohomology ring as a fiber product, which in turn determines the cohomology over $\mathbb{Z}[1/2]$.
arxiv:2610.39498.authors: Youming Chen, Wenchuan Hu, Deyuan Ma

arxiv:2610.39501.title: The complete existence spectrum of periodic complementary ternary pairs of weight nine
arxiv:2610.39501.summary: For two sequences with entries $0,\pm1$, periodic complementarity means that their periodic autocorrelation functions sum to zero at every nonzero shift. We give necessary and sufficient conditions on the length for the existence of such pairs of total weight nine, where weight counts nonzero entries. The conditions decide existence at any prescribed length by divisibility tests.

arxiv:2610.39535.title: Local Convergence of Triadic Closures of Sparse Random Graphs
arxiv:2610.39535.summary: Triadic closure is a natural mechanism for modeling the clustering phenomenon observed in many real-world networks. Given a possibly random undirected graph $H$, we consider pairs of non-adjacent vertices that have a common neighbor. Conditional on $H$, each such pair is joined by an edge independently and simultaneously, with a probability depending on the degrees of its endpoints and on the number of their common neighbors.

arxiv:2610.39578.title: Off-diagonal Ramsey numbers for 3-uniform tight hypergraph cycles
arxiv:2610.39578.summary: Let $C^{(3)}_n$ be the $3$-uniform tight cycle on $n$ vertices, that is, the $3$-uniform hypergraph on a cyclically ordered set of $n$ vertices whose edges are precisely the triples of consecutive vertices in the given cyclic order. We asymptotically determine the off-diagonal Ramsey numbers of $3$-uniform tight cycles. This is an off-diagonal analogue of a result of Haxell, {\L}uczak, Peng, R\"odl, Ruci\'nski and Skokan [Combin.\ Probab.\ Comput.\ 18 (2009), no.\ 1-2, 165--203] on the diagonal Ramsey numbers of $3$-uniform tight cycles.

arxiv:2610.39580.title: Learning Kolmogorov Backward Operators for Spectral Analysis and Forecasting: A Data-Driven Variational Galerkin Framework
arxiv:2610.39580.summary: For a time-homogeneous Markov process, the fixed-lag solution operator \( (T_\tau f)(x)=\mathbb E[f(X_{t+\tau})\mid X_t=x] \) of the Kolmogorov backward equation evolves observables linearly and deterministically, even when the dynamics are stochastic. We approximate this operator using a two-stage method where we first approximate this operator directly from data, without knowledge of the governing equation (e.g., Fourier Neural Operator), and then compress the Galerkin projection onto a finite-dimensional observable space that is fixed in advance or selected variationally. The error analysis traces the learning error of the estimator, the sampling error of the Galerkin inner products, and…
arxiv:2610.39580.authors: Yuanchao Xu, Claire Valva, Ben Gao, Isao Ishikawa

arxiv:2610.39583.title: On equivariant affineness in elliptic cohomology
arxiv:2610.39583.summary: We investigate equivariant affineness in spectral algebraic geometry: the phenomenon where $\infty$-categories of quasi-coherent sheaves of a spectral stack are equivalent to $\infty$-categories of modules over an equivariant ring spectrum. In the nonequivariant case, this is known as 0-affineness, and has been studied by Gaitsgory, Mathew--Meier, amongst others. Allowing for equivariant phenomena opens up a much wider class of spectral stacks to be studied through the lens of spectra.
arxiv:2610.39583.authors: Jack Morgan Davies, Sil Linskens, Leonard Tokic

arxiv:2610.39589.title: Finite-dimensional irreducible representations of Yangians
arxiv:2610.39589.summary: We present a direct proof of the well-known classification of finite-dimensional representations of the Yangian $Y(\mathfrak{sl}_2)$ following an approach by Chary-Pressley for $U_q(\mathfrak{ \hat sl_2})$.

arxiv:2610.39593.title: Topological Insights and Combinatorial Frameworks for Twist Knot Complements
arxiv:2610.39593.summary: The complement of a knot in $\mathbb{S}^3$ is a fundamental object in $3$-manifold topology and serves as a primary building block in the study of geometric structures on manifolds. For a large class of knots, these complements admit complete hyperbolic metrics, motivating the development of various frameworks for their classification and analysis. A twist knot is formed by applying a series of half-twists to a closed loop and linking the ends.
arxiv:2610.39593.authors: Biplab Basak, Mangaldeep Saha, Ayushi Trivedi

arxiv:2610.39595.title: The number of $C_4$-free graphs
arxiv:2610.39595.summary: Erd\H{o}s, Frankl and R\"odl showed that the number of graphs on $n$ vertices with no copy of a non-bipartite graph $H$ is $2^{(1+o(1))ex(n,H)}$, whereas Morris and Saxton showed that this fails for $C_6$. Answering a question of Erd\H{o}s, we prove that the number of $C_4$-free graphs on $n$ vertices is $2^{(1+o(1))ex(n,C_4)}$. The proof combines a modified hypergraph container method that treats pairs of vertices with large codegree separately, with a new bound on the number of matchings in a graph.

arxiv:2610.39597.title: Non-linear contexts and dependent operads
arxiv:2610.39597.summary: We study the category $\mathbf{Dep_{aff}}$ of finite posets and opfibrations between them, and prove that it is a perfect operator category in the sense of Barwick. Based on its additional properties, we propose a definition for a dependent operator category, and formulate a notion of dependent affine operad in a fibered way. In the particular case of $\mathbf{Dep_{aff}}$, we investigate the basic theory of such operads, establishing that the category of algebras for an operad is monadic over a canonical presheaf topos of "dependent sets".

arxiv:2610.39599.title: Tiling circular $n$-boards with squares and (1,1)-fences
arxiv:2610.39599.summary: We show that the number of ways to tile a circular $n$-board (an annulus divided into $n$ curved unit square cells) with appropriately curved unit squares and curved (1,1)-fences is a Lucas number squared if $n$ is even and an odd-indexed Lucas number otherwise. A curved (1,1)-fence is composed of two curved unit squares separated by a gap in the shape of another curved unit square. This combinatorial interpretation of the Lucas numbers squared and the odd-indexed Lucas numbers allows us to obtain various identities concerning these sequences in a quick and lucid manner.

arxiv:2610.39611.title: Existence and spectral instability of steady rolls in the Nikolaevskiy equation: a computer-assisted study
arxiv:2610.39611.summary: The Nikolaevskiy equation is a model of short-wave pattern formation coupled to a neutral long-wave mode, and it is believed that all of its spatially periodic steady states are unstable. Existing results are formal, numerical, or restricted to a small neighbourhood of onset. We give computer-assisted proofs of three results.
arxiv:2610.39611.authors: Nikita V. Konev, Fedor A. Vyazanitsyn, Igor A. Knyazev

arxiv:2610.39627.title: Automorphism groups of smooth quartic threefolds
arxiv:2610.39627.summary: We classify finite groups of automorphisms of smooth quartic threefolds over $\mathbb{C}$. Every such group embeds into one of $17$ maximal groups, which we realize by explicit equations and matrix generators. Among finite subgroups of $\mathrm{PGL}(5,\mathbb{C})$ preserving a smooth quartic threefold, there are exactly $24$ maximal ones up to conjugacy, and we use them to determine the $194$ groups that occur as full automorphism groups.

arxiv:2610.39630.title: Symbolic depth functions of edge ideals via local graph structure
arxiv:2610.39630.summary: We study the depth of symbolic powers of edge ideals, focusing on local properties of graphs. First, we give several sufficient conditions for the symbolic depth function to be non-increasing, using local properties of graphs and local cohomology. Next, we give a counterexample to a conjecture of Minh, T.N.

arxiv:2610.39637.title: Solutions to several problems on infinite sumset configurations
arxiv:2610.39637.summary: We resolve a number of the problems collected by Kra, Moreira, Richter and Robertson in their survey "Problems on infinite sumset configurations in the integers and beyond". Our main result is that in every countably infinite abelian group, every set of positive upper Banach density contains a sumset $B_1+\dots+B_k$ of $k$ infinite sets, for every $k$; the proof uses the Kronecker factor, but no higher-order Host-Kra structure theory, nilsystems of step greater than one, or nilspaces. We also answer, positively or negatively, questions on monochromatic sets $B+mB$, on sumsets in sets of logarithmic density, on polynomial sumset configurations, on sums of the form $B_{i_1}+\dots+B_{i_m}$…

arxiv:2610.39653.title: On edge-ordered Ramsey numbers of hypergraphs
arxiv:2610.39653.summary: For an integer $h\geq2$, an edge-ordered $h$-uniform hypergraph $H^<$ is an $h$-uniform hypergraph with a linear ordering of its hyperedges. For an integer $q \geq 1$, the edge-ordered Ramsey number $R_{\mathrm{edge}}(H^<;q)$ of $H^<$ is the smallest positive integer $N$ such that there exists an edge-ordered $h$-uniform hypergraph $G^<$ on $N$ vertices such that, for every $q$-coloring of the hyperedges of $G^<$, there is a monochromatic copy of $H^<$ in $G^<$ preserving the hyperedge order. In this note, we show that, for every edge-ordered $h$-uniform hypergraph $F^<$ on $n$ vertices with $m\geq1$ hyperedges, $R_{\mathrm{edge}}(F^<;q) \leq R_h(F;q)^{Cm^2}$ where $F$ is the underlying…

arxiv:2610.39698.title: Unified transform method for nonautonomous linear evolution equations: rigorous analysis and qualitative theory
arxiv:2610.39698.summary: Established herein is the rigorous extension of the celebrated Fokas unified transform method for linear evolution PDE with time-dependent coefficients. As illustrative examples, considered below and rigorously analysed in detail are non-homogeneous initial-boundary-value problems, formulated on the half-line, for the heat equation and the modified heat (also widely known as Barenblatt's pseudo-parabolic) equation with reaction terms and temporally varying coefficients. Solution formulae are derived formally via suitable implementation of the UTM, and rigorously verified a posteriori, in the classical sense.
arxiv:2610.39698.authors: Andreas Chatziafratis, Spyridon Kamvissis, Alain Miranville, Tohru Ozawa

arxiv:2610.39722.title: Slow Entropy of Quasi-Unipotent Actions on S-Arithmetic Homogeneous Spaces
arxiv:2610.39722.summary: We study metric and topological slow entropy for translations on a class of finite-volume $S$-arithmetic homogeneous spaces with a real and $p$-adic factor. We consider translations whose real component is quasi-unipotent and whose $p$-adic component lies in a compact open subgroup. At polynomial scales, we show that the metric and topological slow entropies coincide and are determined by the chain structure of the real adjoint action.

arxiv:2610.39753.title: Four-Coloring Planar Graphs in Linear Time
arxiv:2610.39753.summary: The famous Four Color Theorem (4CT) states that any planar graph can be colored with four colors, but how do we find a 4-coloring? In our previous paper [FOCS'26], we presented a simple combinatorial algorithm to 4-color planar graphs in $O(n\log n)$ time. We improve it here to $O(n)$ time, which is optimal.
arxiv:2610.39753.authors: Yuta Inoue, Ken-ichi Kawarabayashi, Atsuyuki Miyashita, Bojan Mohar, Carsten Thomassen, Mikkel Thorup

arxiv:2610.39759.title: Minimum-degree thresholds beyond bounded colourability
arxiv:2610.39759.summary: We survey recent developments on minimum-degree thresholds in extremal graph theory, with an emphasis on structural refinements of the chromatic-threshold problem. The chromatic threshold asks when a linear minimum-degree condition forces bounded chromatic number in an \(H\)-free graph; its complete classification shows a striking finite trichotomy. We discuss several stronger and related threshold notions in which bounded colourability is replaced by bounded \(H\)-free homomorphic images, bounded neighbourhood complexity via VC-dimension, exact blowup structure for maximal \(H\)-free graphs, and improved quantitative bounds in graph removal lemmas.

arxiv:2610.39760.title: EPPA for Reducts of the Random Graph
arxiv:2610.39760.summary: We prove that finite two-graphs have coherent EPPA and that neither graphs modulo global complementation nor two-graphs modulo global complementation have EPPA. This completes the classification of EPPA and coherent EPPA for the reducts of the random graph, answering a question and confirming a conjecture of Evans, Hubi\v{c}ka, Kone\v{c}n\'y and Ne\v{s}et\v{r}il.
arxiv:2610.39760.authors: Sofia Brenner, Jan Hubi\v{c}ka, Mat\v{e}j Kone\v{c}n\'y

arxiv:2610.39767.title: Formality transmission
arxiv:2610.39767.summary: Across mathematics, formality results are usually established through general criteria rather than by constructing explicit equivalences. These criteria include domination, puncturing, highly-connected formality, intrinsic formality, formality descent, formality in families, purity, etc. In this article, we prove that all these criteria are instances of a single theorem, formality transmission.

arxiv:2610.39799.title: Solid Arithmetic D-modules
arxiv:2610.39799.summary: We introduce a solid ring of arithmetic differential operators analogue to Berthelot's D-dagger, and its derived infinity-category of solid quasi-coherent modules. We show that there is a fully faithful functor from Berthelot's derived category of bounded complexes of D-dagger-modules with coherent cohomology into our new category.

arxiv:2610.39811.title: A complete theory of local minimizers for periodic variational problems
arxiv:2610.39811.summary: We study the periodic problem in the Calculus of Variations and give a complete characterization of the positive definiteness of the second variation, extending the Reid Roundabout Theorem to periodic boundary conditions. Two formulations are established: one in terms of conjugate and semi-coupled points, and one in terms of the existence of a symmetric solution of the associated Riccati equation satisfying a boundary inequality. We show by an explicit example that the latter condition, while sufficient, is not necessary except in dimension one.

arxiv:2610.39820.title: Rational points of exact period three for the quadratic family
arxiv:2610.39820.summary: For the quadratic family $f_c(x) = x^2 + c$ over $\Q$, we isolate a general $S$-unit and ABC template for rational periodic cycles: under the ABC conjecture, any rational quantity built from the consecutive-point sums of a rational period-$n$ cycle whose value and shift-by-$1$ are both $S$-units (with $S$ the support of the denominator of $c$) has logarithmic height at most $(1+\eps)\sum_{p \in S} \log p + O_\eps(1)$. Specializing to period $3$ in the change of coordinates $u = x_0 + x_1$ and $v = x_0 + x_2$, the period-$3$ condition reduces to $v = -1/(1+u)$, forcing the parameter $t = u$ to satisfy $t, t+1 \in \Z[S^{-1}]^\times$; the template then yields, under ABC, $\max\{|a|,|b|,|a+b|\}…

arxiv:2610.39833.title: Exact Avoid-or-Compress Extrema for Dense Reachable Images: Defects Four and Five
arxiv:2610.39833.summary: Let $S$ be a reachable image of a strongly connected synchronizing automaton and $\varnothing\ne A\subsetneq S$. We determine the maximum shortest avoid-or-compress length over binary and arbitrary finite alphabets for $m=n-|S|=4$ and $m=5$. The exact values are $\min(n-|A|,11)$ and $\min(n-|A|,14)$, respectively.

arxiv:2610.39838.title: The Kawatani--Okawa conjecture in dimensions three and four
arxiv:2610.39838.summary: We prove that a smooth projective threefold or fourfold whose bounded derived category admits no nontrivial semiorthogonal decomposition has nef canonical divisor, confirming the Kawatani--Okawa conjecture in these dimensions. The proof combines the classification of extremal contractions with constructions of admissible subcategories. In dimension four, we refine the descriptions of isolated surface fibers and construct exceptional objects supported on certain fibers.

arxiv:2610.39863.title: From Trees to Binary Trees: Approximation Algorithms and a PTAS
arxiv:2610.39863.summary: Kellerhals, Krebs, Nichterlein, and Schmid introduced the optimization problem Tree in Binary Tree (TBT), where, given a tree $T$, the task is to find a binary tree $S^*$ with $V(T)=V(S^*)$ that minimizes $\sum_{uv\in E(T)} \operatorname{dist}_{S^*}(u,v)$. They also introduced the variant Tree in Binary Tree With Steiner Nodes (TBT-SN), where the condition $V(T)=V(S^*)$ is relaxed to $V(T)\subseteq V(S^*)$. We give a simple linear-time $\frac{8}{3}$-approximation algorithm for TBT and a polynomial-time approximation scheme (PTAS) for TBT-SN.

arxiv:2610.39870.title: Optimal self-orthogonal binary linear codes
arxiv:2610.39870.summary: We complete the determination of the minimum possible length of eight-dimensional binary self-orthogonal codes with given minimum distance. For dimension nine we give exact values and bounds for minimum distance at most $64$. By exploiting the geometric reformulation of linear codes as multisets of points, we fully redo the classification for dimension at most seven in a simplified and computer-free manner.

arxiv:2610.39874.title: Isospectral congruence manifolds, spectral rigidity, and a converse to Vign\'eras
arxiv:2610.39874.summary: Let $B$ be a quaternion division algebra over a number field $k$ that gives rise to arithmetic Fuchsian or Kleinian groups, and let $\mathcal{O}$ be a maximal order of $B$. We show that every closed orientable Riemannian manifold isospectral to a principal congruence hyperbolic surface $X_\mathcal{O}(\mathfrak{a})$ is isometric to $X_{\mathcal{O}'}(\mathfrak{a})$ for some maximal order $\mathcal{O}'$ of $B$, provided that no prime factor of $\mathfrak{a}$ ramifies in $B$ and that $\mathfrak{a}$ satisfies a mild condition at the primes over $2$. This is a converse to the construction of Vign\'eras, which produces isospectral manifolds from maximal orders of different types.

arxiv:2610.39900.title: The asymptotic number of zonotopes
arxiv:2610.39900.summary: We provide a sharp estimate for the asymptotic number of lattice zonotopes inscribed in [0, n] d as n tends to infinity. Our estimate refines the logarithmic equivalent established by B{\'a}r{\'a}ny, Bureaux, and Lund when the sum of the generators of the zonotope is prescribed. As we shall see, the exponential part of our estimate is a polynomial of degree d in n 1/(d+1) , plus a term involving the non-trivial zeros of the Riemann zeta function.

arxiv:2610.39907.title: Cocycles on Tiling Spaces
arxiv:2610.39907.summary: The space of tilings by rectangles form an interesting collection of multidimensional subshifts. Here, we study cocycles on such tiling spaces and provide an algorithmically decidable necessary and sufficient condition for the tiling space associated with a collection of rectangles to admit a nontrivial cocycle. Along the way, we also prove that the tiling spaces corresponding to a class of rectangular tile sets satisfy certain mixing properties.

arxiv:2610.39908.title: Low-rank matrices with three prescribed off-diagonal values over $\mathbb{F}_p$
arxiv:2610.39908.summary: Let $p$ be a prime such that $2$ is a primitive root modulo $p$. We prove that, for every three-element set $L\subseteq\mathbb{F}_p$ and every integer $n\geq1$, there exists a symmetric $n\times n$ matrix over $\mathbb{F}_p$ with zero diagonal, off-diagonal entries in $L$, and rank $O_{p,L}(n^{1/3})$. This answers a question of Bukh for all such primes and, in particular, settles the case $L=\{1,4,6\}\subseteq\mathbb{F}_{19}$ singled out on his problem list.

arxiv:2610.39928.title: On record behaviours of returns for interval maps
arxiv:2610.39928.summary: Given a dynamical system $(X,T)$ and an ergodic invariant measure $\mu$, a $\mu$-typical point $x\in X$ under $T$ visits arbitrarily small neighbourhood of $x$. We will use techniques based on extreme value theory and Laplace functional for point process to show that, for interval maps with suitable mixing and anti-clustering conditions, the limiting distributions of the record times and values of the return process $Y_j(x)=-\log d(T^jx,x)$, after possible normalisation, has Poisson-type laws.

arxiv:2610.39941.title: Block-exchange descent for insertion: commuting projections and minimum masks
arxiv:2610.39941.summary: For fixed nonempty words $u,v$, the minimum insertion degree of a shuffle is the least number of inserted-source runs among its representations. We prove that, after a block exchange from a minimum mask of degree $r$, the minimum over masks with commuting source projections is exactly $r-1$; a larger decrease occurs precisely when a noncommuting mask has fewer runs. If either source is unary, every such exchange is exact.
arxiv:2610.39941.authors: Haobo Ma, Wenlin Zhang, Charles E. Hughes

arxiv:2610.39945.title: Compatibility of Perverse Truncation of Ng\^o Fibrations
arxiv:2610.39945.summary: We study compatibility of perverse truncations for morphisms between Ng\^o fibrations with rationally smooth total spaces. We show that, under an effective rank inequality, equivariant pullbacks preserve the normalized perverse truncations. Applied to the diagonal, this gives multiplicativity of perverse truncations for Hitchin systems with rationally smooth total spaces.
arxiv:2610.39945.authors: Bin Wang, Shihao Wang, Chenglong Yu

arxiv:2610.39957.title: Dense Minors from the Crux
arxiv:2610.39957.summary: Let $G$ be a graph with average degree $d>0$ and $C_\alpha(G)$ be the minimum order of a subgraph whose average degree is at least $\alpha d$ for any fixed $0<\alpha<1$. Then $G$ has a minor of average degree $\Omega(\sqrt{d\,C_\alpha(G)})$, which is asymptotically tight up to a constant factor. This reveals a unified mechanism underlying previous results on dense minors in locally sparse graphs.

arxiv:2610.39966.title: On the maximum interval index of a graph
arxiv:2610.39966.summary: For a connected graph P G on n vertices, the interval index is defined by Int(G) = {u,v} subset V(G) (|I(u, v)| - 1), where I(u, v) denotes the set of all vertices lying on a shortest u - v path. It was conjectured that, among all connected graphs on n vertices, the path Pn attains the maximum value of the interval index. In this paper we settle this conjecture, and we prove that the maximum is attained only for Pn, except for n = 4, when the cycle C4 attains the same value.

arxiv:2610.39982.title: Complexity of finding color-avoiding connected components
arxiv:2610.39982.summary: Two vertices of a (not necessarily properly) arc-colored digraph are called arc-$\ell$-color-avoiding strongly $k$-arc-connected if, after the removal of the arcs of any at most $\ell$ colors, they remain strongly $k$-arc-connected. The arc-$\ell$-color-avoiding strongly $k$-arc-connected components are maximal sets of vertices such that any two of those vertices belonging to the set are arc-$\ell$-color-avoiding strongly $k$-arc-connected in the graph. We investigate the problems of finding the arc-$\ell$-color-avoiding strongly $k$-arc-connected components and the maximal arc-$\ell$-color-avoiding strongly $k$-arc-connected subgraphs of an arc-colored digraph.
arxiv:2610.39982.authors: Panna T\'{i}mea Fekete, Roland Molontay, Kitti Varga

arxiv:2610.39996.title: A Yau-Tian-Donaldson correspondence for degenerations
arxiv:2610.39996.summary: We prove an equivalence between the existence of a unique K\"ahler-Einstein metric on a degeneration of Fano varieties and uniform CM minimization. This proves a discretely valued analogue of the (uniform) Yau-Tian-Donaldson conjecture, in the sense of non-Archimedean geometry. As a main tool, we prove that Ding stability of a degeneration implies uniform Ding minimization, proving a converse to work of Blum-Xu.

arxiv:2610.40013.title: Integrable and non-integrable LR geodesic flows on 5-dimensional 2-step nilpotent Lie groups
arxiv:2610.40013.summary: We investigate sub-Riemannian geodesic flows on 5-dimensional nilpotent Lie groups endowed with left-invariant Riemannian metrics. Up to isomorphism, there are exactly two such groups: the Heisenberg group $H_5$ and the 5-dimensional nilpotent Lie group with a 2-dimensional commutator subgroup. For each group, we study geodesic flows associated with both left-invariant (LL) and right-invariant (LR) distributions, deriving explicit descriptions of the corresponding geodesics and comparing their integrability properties.

arxiv:2610.40025.title: One Polynomial Field for Every Euler Step and the Flow: Polynomial Dynamics for P and PSPACE
arxiv:2610.40025.summary: We construct, for each deterministic Turing machine that halts on all inputs, one polynomial vector field with rational coefficients that performs the same logical computation at unit Euler step, at every smaller or variable step in $(0,1]$ with divergent sum, and along the flow. This unifies discrete-time and continuous-time computation by polynomial dynamics, which earlier characterizations treated separately. For a machine making $T$ transitions in space $H$, a logical scale $h=2^{-s}$ with $s=O(H)$ suffices, with physical time $O(s(T+s))$, drift disturbances up to $h^{2K}$ for a fixed exponent $K$, and $2Ks+3$ fractional bits at unit step.

arxiv:2610.40028.title: On Terao's conjecture for at most nine planes
arxiv:2610.40028.summary: In this note we show that Terao's freeness conjecture holds for arrangements of at most nine planes in the complex projective $3$-space. Moreover, we show that every essential and irreducible free arrangement of at most nine planes in $\mathbb{P}^{3}_{\mathbb{C}}$ is divisionally free, and we list all intersection lattices of such arrangements. Our approach is based on Ziegler's restriction theorem and a simple count involving the numbers of multiple lines.

arxiv:2610.40032.title: Submodular decompositions: a bounded-variation counterexample and an exact planar cut formula
arxiv:2610.40032.summary: B\'erczi, Geh\'er, Imolay, Lov\'asz, and Schwarcz (SIAM J. Discrete Math. 40(2026), 308--335) asked whether every set function of bounded variation is a difference of two bounded submodular functions, and how to determine the optimum in a monotonic sum-decomposition of a planar graph cut function. In this paper, we answer both questions and obtain quantitative extensions.
arxiv:2610.40032.authors: Guoqing Wang, Linlin Wang, Jun Yue

arxiv:2610.40034.title: Quasimodularity of $q$-series associated to root lattices
arxiv:2610.40034.summary: Motivated by conjectures arising in part from the study of class-$\mathcal{S}$ vertex algebras associated with four-dimensional supersymmetric field theories, we study multiple $q$-zeta functions attached to finite-dimensional simple Lie algebras. We prove their conjectured quasimodularity for all classical Lie algebras of types $A$, $B$, $C$, and $D$, as well as a more general Weyl-symmetrized version in which the exponents attached to the positive roots are allowed to vary, under a suitable parity condition. Our proof is based on a substantially more general result.
arxiv:2610.40034.authors: Antun Milas, Jan-Willem M. van Ittersum

arxiv:2610.40035.title: Degenerate complex structures on surfaces and stability conditions
arxiv:2610.40035.summary: Physical heuristics suggest that the space of Bridgeland stability conditions of a projective Calabi-Yau manifold $X$ should be related to the moduli space of complex structures on its mirror $X^\vee$. On the other hand, recent work in the literature introduces a modular partial compactification, $\mathcal{A}\mathrm{Stab}(X)$, of a quotient of the space of stability conditions on $\mathcal{D}^{b}(X)$. We provide some mathematical evidence for the aforementioned heuristics by proving that for curves and surfaces, certain boundary strata in $\mathcal{A}\mathrm{Stab}(X)$ describe degenerate complex structures on $X^\vee$.

arxiv:2610.40040.title: The Torelli Group and Euler Class Zero $\mathrm{PSL}(2,\mathbb{R})$ Representations
arxiv:2610.40040.summary: We prove that every representation of a closed surface group of genus at least $3$ into $\mathrm{PSL}(2,\mathbb{R})$ that is sufficiently close (but not equal to) a representation that has non-compact solvable image has a simple closed separating curve that is mapped to a non-trivial elliptic element in $\mathrm{PSL}(2,\mathbb{R})$. This can be seen as evidence for an affirmative answer to a question of Bowditch and a conjecture of Goldman.
arxiv:2610.40040.authors: Marit Bobb, James Farre, Peter Smillie

arxiv:2610.40041.title: G-equivariant Alterfold TQFT in any dimension
arxiv:2610.40041.summary: For a discrete group $G$, we construct an $(n+1)$-dimensional $G$-equivariant Alterfold topological quantum field theory from a $G$-equivariant $S^n$-algebra satisfying strong semisimplicity, complete finiteness, and Morita invariance. We use state sum on triangulation to define a partition function and prove that it is invariant under local surgery relations and is invariant under gauge transformations relative to the boundary. If the input is given a reflection-positive structure, the theory is unitary.

arxiv:2610.40057.title: Invariant probability measures on holomorphic functions on the unit disk
arxiv:2610.40057.summary: We study probability measures on the space of holomorphic functions on the unit disk that are invariant under pre-composition by conformal automorphisms and give no mass to constant functions. We determine the slowest possible growth of functions supported by such measures. Let $M_f(R)$ denote the maximum modulus of $f$ on the hyperbolic ball of radius $R$ centered at the origin.

arxiv:2610.40058.title: Quantum cluster structures on bosonic extensions
arxiv:2610.40058.summary: We construct a quantum cluster algebra structure on the standard $\mathbb Z[q^{\pm1/2}]$-form of the bosonic extension algebra $\widehat A(b)$ for every positive braid $b$ and every symmetrizable generalized Cartan matrix. The proof realizes this algebra as the degree-zero part of a localization of a larger quantum unipotent coordinate ring, obtained by thickening a word for $b$. For symmetric Cartan matrices, this realization also gives a monoidal categorification of the quantum cluster algebra.

arxiv:2610.40067.title: Singularity of harmonic measure on Poisson--Voronoi tessellations in hyperbolic spaces
arxiv:2610.40067.summary: We prove that the harmonic measure of simple random walk on the Poisson--Voronoi tessellation in $\mathbb{H}^d$ is almost surely singular with respect to Lebesgue measure on the boundary. This answers a question of Benjamini, Paquette, and Pfeffer in the hyperbolic plane and establishes the analogous result in higher dimensions. Our proof is based on ergodic theory of rerooting relations and their boundary extensions.

arxiv:2610.40074.title: Harmonically lifting linear series from curves to K3 surfaces
arxiv:2610.40074.summary: We investigate the question of which Brill--Noether special linear series on a curve on a K3 surface lift to the surface. Work of Reid, Donagi--Morrison, Green--Lazarsfeld, Lelli-Chiesa, and others shows that Brill--Noether special linear series admits lifts in many cases, in particular when the linear series computes the Clifford index of the curve. Using the recently defined notion of harmonic filtrations of Lazarsfeld--Mukai bundles, we show the same is true for a linear series computing the Brill--Noether special Clifford index, an analogue of the classical Clifford index considering only Brill--Noether special linear series, and show that the Brill--Noether special Clifford index is…

arxiv:2610.40076.title: A Dolbeault complex for the contact quantised flag manifolds of type $\mathrm{C}_{2}$ and $\mathrm{D}_{4}$
arxiv:2610.40076.summary: Differential calculi on non-irreducible quantised flag manifolds of the $\mathrm{A}$-series have recently been investigated using Lusztig positive root vectors, revealing that several features of classical differential geometry persist in the noncommutative setting. We extend this investigation to quantised flag manifolds associated with the lowest-rank quantum groups of types $\mathrm{C}$ and $\mathrm{D}$ whose classical spaces are holomorphic contact manifolds. Building on the Heckenberger--Kolb framework, we construct covariant first order differential calculi.

arxiv:2610.40079.title: The bivariate generating function for cylindric partitions of rank three
arxiv:2610.40079.summary: Using a rational analogue of an $\mathrm{A}_2^{(1)}$ Rogers--Ramanujan type identity discovered by Warnaar, we establish sum-like expressions for a bivariate generating function for cylindric partitions of rank three. These expressions provide the finishing touch towards conjectures of Warnaar and Kanade--Russell.
arxiv:2610.40079.authors: Shane Chern, Trieu Nguyen, Chanh Tran, Tanay Wakhare

arxiv:2610.40095.title: On the Erd\H{o}s--Ginzburg--Ziv Problem for $\mathbb{Z}_n^r$
arxiv:2610.40095.summary: The Erd\H{o}s--Ginzburg--Ziv problem is a classical extremal problem in discrete geometry. We prove that, for all positive integers $n$ and $r$, every sequence of $4^r n$ lattice points in $\mathbb{Z}^r$ contains $n$ points whose centroid is again a lattice point.

arxiv:2610.40097.title: Holomorphic 1-forms without zeros on K\"ahler manifolds
arxiv:2610.40097.summary: Assuming the existence of good minimal models, we give a bimeromorphic classification of compact connected K\"ahler manifolds admitting a holomorphic 1-form without zeros.

arxiv:2610.40132.title: Full immersions in Eulerian group-labeled graphs
arxiv:2610.40132.summary: An immersion of a graph H in a graph G is full if the immersion uses every edge of G. We give a structure theorem for group-labeled Eulerian graphs excluding a fixed group-labeled graph as a full immersion.
arxiv:2610.40132.authors: Ioannis Eleftheriadis, Rose McCarty, Caleb McFarland, Evangelos Protopapas, Paul Wollan

arxiv:2610.40136.title: The Kodaira dimension and minimal models of $\mathcal{A}_6$
arxiv:2610.40136.summary: We prove that the moduli space $\mathcal{A}_6$ of principally polarized abelian sixfolds has Kodaira dimension zero, determining the remaining case in the Kodaira classification of the spaces $\mathcal{A}_g$. More precisely, every nonzero scalar Siegel modular form of genus six, weight $k$ and positive boundary order $b$ satisfies $k\geq 7b$, with equality precisely for powers of the weight-fourteen harmonic theta series of Dittmann, Salvati Manni and Scheithauer. The canonical ring is therefore a polynomial ring on one generator of degree two.

arxiv:2610.40145.title: A lifted entropy splitting lemma and applications
arxiv:2610.40145.summary: We give a matrix lifting of the entropy-splitting theorem of Csisz\'ar, K\"orner, Lov\'asz, Marton, and Simonyi, and show several applications. We use it to prove the Cartesian-product inequality conjectured by Sinjorgo and Sotirov for the generalized Lov\'asz theta number, and we also answer the saturation and convexification questions of Carli Silva, Coutinho, Oliveira, and Tun\c{c}el on the same theme. For the strong Hoffman bound, we answer a question of Wocjan, Elphick, and Darbari concerning orthogonal rank, and show that optimization over matrix weights gives exactly the ceiling of the theta number of the complement.

arxiv:2610.40147.title: Dynamical relations on $\mathbb{P}^1$, higher bifurcations, and arithmetic bigness
arxiv:2610.40147.summary: In this article, we study algebraic relations among rational maps on $\mathbb{P}^1$ and among their preperiodic points. Working over $\mathbb{C}$, we characterize algebraic families of positive-dimensional varieties in $(\mathbb{P}^1)^N$ and tuples of maps $(f_1, \ldots, f_N)$ for which the subvariety is dynamically special for a Zariski-dense set of parameters. Moreover, outside of well-understood elliptic phenomena, we show that all families of maps and subvarieties that bifurcate are maximally bifurcating.

arxiv:2610.40150.title: Packing and covering random trees
arxiv:2610.40150.summary: We study the sizes of optimal packings and coverings of conditioned branching processes by balls with growing radii. We find a universal limiting constant, and thereby establish universality of packing and covering numbers across different scales and different offspring distributions. To be precise, for $\mu$ an offspring distribution with mean $1$ and finite variance $\sigma^2$ we let $T_n$ be a Bienaym\'e tree with offspring distribution $\mu$ conditioned to have size $n$.
arxiv:2610.40150.authors: Caelan Atamanchuk, Simon Briend, Serte Donderwinkel, Elaine Herrera

arxiv:2610.40152.title: Non-Archimedean Rigidity and the Uniform Dynamical Manin--Mumford for $\left(\mathbb{P}^1\right)^n$
arxiv:2610.40152.summary: We prove a uniform form of the dynamical Manin-Mumford conjecture for split endomorphisms $\Phi = \left(f_1,\ldots,f_n\right): \left(\mathbb{P}^1\right)^n \to \left(\mathbb{P}^1\right)^n$ over $\mathbb{C}$, where each $f_i$ has degree $d \geq 2$ and at most one $f_i$ is exceptional. Specifically, we bound the number of irreducible components of $\overline{\operatorname{Prep}\left(\Phi\right)\cap V\left(\mathbb{C}\right)}^{\operatorname{Zar}}$ uniformly, depending only on $\left(n,d,\operatorname{deg} V\right)$. We also obtain uniform statements for the dynamical Bogomolov conjecture.

arxiv:2610.40183.title: Linking-form splitting and four-dimensional genera of knots
arxiv:2610.40183.summary: By Gilmer's splitting lemma, the linking form of a rational homology sphere that bounds a 4-manifold is the orthogonal sum of a metabolic summand and a summand presented by a form of the rank of the intersection form. The lemma underlies Gilmer's slice genus theorem and the rank criteria of Murakami-Yasuhara and Gilmer-Livingston for nonorientable surfaces and the 4-dimensional clasp number. We show that the lemma and these results, as stated, are false.

arxiv:2610.40200.title: The $6\frac{1}{2}$-functor formalism of Cartier modules
arxiv:2610.40200.summary: Let $p$ be a prime. We construct a coherent formalism of geometric operations on Cartier modules with coefficients in ind-coherent sheaves on noetherian derived $\mathbb F_p$-schemes. For such a scheme $X$, we consider the stable presentable category $\mathrm{Cart}(X)$ of ind-coherent sheaves $M$ equipped with a structural morphism $F_{*,X}M \to M$, where $F_X$ denotes the Frobenius endomorphism.

arxiv:2610.40209.title: The Segal conjecture for large objects and semiadditive lifts
arxiv:2610.40209.summary: We prove a projection formula for homotopy fixed points of trivial actions of finite $p$-groups. More precisely, for every bounded-below, $p$-complete spectrum $X$ whose mod-$p$ homology is $I$-complete, the canonical map \[ (\mathbb S_p)^{BG}\otimes X \overset{\simeq}{\rightarrow} X^{BG} \] is an equivalence for every finite $p$-group $G$, where $I$ is the augmentation ideal of the Steenrod algebra. Building on earlier joint work with Burklund, our proof combines the Adams--Gunawardena--Miller calculation with an adaptation of Carlsson's induction.

arxiv:2610.40228.title: On stable twist 2-groups of quasi-Hopf algebras
arxiv:2610.40228.summary: For any finite-dimensional quasi-Hopf algebra $A$, we define the notion of a stable twist of $A$. We show that stable twists form a strict 2-group $\2ust(A)$, which is equivalent to $\OAut(\C{A})^{\rev}$. Given a group homomorphism $\rho: G \to \ost(A)$, we determine the obstruction in $H^3(G,Z_G(A))$ to lift $\rho$ to a $G$-action on $\C{A}$.

arxiv:2610.40235.title: Three-dimensional QCA that are not stably circuits
arxiv:2610.40235.summary: We prove that the three-dimensional chiral $\Z_p$ Clifford quantum cellular automata of Haah and of Sun--Yang--Wang--Tantivasadakarn--Chen are, for every odd prime $p$, not finite-depth quantum circuits, even after tensoring with arbitrary ancillary degrees of freedom and composing with translations. Previously such statements were known only inside the Clifford category. As a consequence, the group of three-dimensional QCA modulo stabilized circuits and translations is not finitely generated.
