arxiv:2610.40237.title: Ergodic treeable equivalence relations are richly ergodic
arxiv:2610.40237.summary: We study the density of ergodic subrelations in the canonical Polish space of subequivalence relations of a probability-measure-preserving countable Borel equivalence relation. Our main result establishes rich ergodicity for ergodic treeable equivalence relations. The proof combines a strongly increasing exhaustion with relative ergodic hyperfinite decomposition.

arxiv:2610.40245.title: Skein reduction and stabilization for the odd Khovanov spectra of $T(2,m)\sqcup T(2,n)$
arxiv:2610.40245.summary: For split links the even Khovanov spectrum is a smash product of the spectra of the pieces; the odd one is not. For $T(2,m)\sqcup T(2,n)$ we show that the odd spectrum is, in each quantum grading, a wedge of spheres and copies of a suspension of $\mathbb{CP}^{2}$. Using the skein cofiber sequence at the level of spectra, we prove that for fixed $q-m-n$ the number of these copies is determined by finitely many small links and stabilizes for large $m$ and $n$.

arxiv:2610.40270.title: On separators in $K_t$-minor-free graphs
arxiv:2610.40270.summary: This manuscript presents a proof of the Alon--Seymour--Thomas conjecture developed under the author's guidance using ChatGPT 6pro. The author has checked every formula and theorem by hand and used Codex to assist with writing. GPT 6.1 Sol (Max) was also used to check the proof repeatedly and to generate numerous examples for verification.

arxiv:2610.40279.title: The Borodin--Kostochka Conjecture for Two Classes of Diamond-Free Graphs
arxiv:2610.40279.summary: We prove the Borodin--Kostochka conjecture for $(\mathrm{diamond},L_4)$-free graphs and $(\mathrm{diamond},K_5^+)$-free graphs, where $L_4$ is obtained from $K_4$ by attaching a path of length two to one clique vertex, and $K_5^+$ is obtained from $K_5$ by adding a vertex adjacent to exactly one clique vertex. The proof uses structural properties of maximum cliques in diamond-free vertex-critical graphs with $\chi=\Delta$.

arxiv:2610.40286.title: Gromov-Hausdorff versus Hausdorff distances for Euclidean submanifolds with positive reach
arxiv:2610.40286.summary: This paper is about comparing the Gromov-Hausdorff distance between a pair of sets to the Hausdorff distance between the pair. Recent work on this problem has focused on two settings, Riemannian manifolds and metric graphs. Here, we focus on embedded submanifolds of Euclidean space endowed with the Euclidean metric.

arxiv:2610.40321.title: Computer-Assisted Results for \(n\)-Sided Non-Transitive Dice Taking Face Values in \([n]\)
arxiv:2610.40321.summary: We consider non-transitivity among dice with \(n\) sides restricted to taking face values in the set \(\{1,\ldots,n\}\). We give a computer-assisted proof that \(n=6\) is the smallest \(n\ge3\) which admits a non-transitive cycle of maximum length \(n\) with uniform and minimal winning advantage. For \(n=6\), we identify the two unique non-transitive cycles of length \(6\).

arxiv:2610.40335.title: Galois module structure of Deligne--Lusztig varieties for $\mathrm{GL}_3$
arxiv:2610.40335.summary: Let $\overline{\mathbf{Y}}(w)\to\overline{\mathbf{X}}(w)$ be the ramified Galois cover of compactified Deligne--Lusztig varieties. Our objects of study are the Lefschetz numbers for the action of the finite covering group $T^{wF}$ on the coherent cohomology of the structure sheaf of $\overline{\mathbf{Y}}(w)$. The Lefschetz numbers for all elements of $T^{wF}$ determine the virtual $T^{wF}$-representation given by the alternating sum of these cohomology groups.

arxiv:2610.40336.title: Degeneration of (-1)-shifted symplectic stacks and categorification of Donaldson-Thomas invariants
arxiv:2610.40336.summary: We study cohomological Donaldson-Thomas invariants of perfect complexes in a semistable degeneration of projective Calabi-Yau threefolds, with smooth components $X_1,X_2$ meeting along a smooth anticanonical surface $S$. The generic fiber of degeneration family is a $(-1)$-shifted symplectic stack. Over the special fiber, the derived restriction to $S$ is derived Lagrangian, and its homotopy fiber product is also $(-1)$-shifted symplectic.

arxiv:2610.40342.title: A p-adic Valuation Calculus for Permutations with Restricted Cycle Lengths
arxiv:2610.40342.summary: Let a_A(n) be the number of permutations of {1,...,n} all of whose cycle lengths lie in a set A. We develop a valuation calculus for these numbers. Mobius inversion writes the exponential generating function as an Euler product, and at a prime p the factors with non-p-integral exponents, the blocks, determine a finite knapsack problem.

arxiv:2610.40351.title: Analytic Kasparov product for non-separable C$^*$-algebras
arxiv:2610.40351.summary: We develop an analytic framework for the explicit construction of Kasparov products on uncountably generated Hilbert modules over non-separable C$^*$-algebras by extending the classical Kasparov bimodule picture. In particular, this yields a well-defined functor from the category of general C$^*$-algebras whose restriction to separable C$^*$-algebras coincides with classical KK-theory and which satisfies several properties expected of non-separable KK-theory. A key idea of the extension is to replace a single Fredholm operator on a Kasparov bimodule with a net and to encode the directed system of separable C$^*$-subalgebras.

arxiv:2610.40352.title: Moduli space of irregular singular $\lambda$-connections and the relative symplectic form
arxiv:2610.40352.summary: We study the moduli space of $\lambda$-connections with ramified singularities on a smooth projective curve $X$. We construct a quasi-projective relative moduli scheme $M^{\alpha}_{\mathrm{Hod}} \to \Lambda$ of $\alpha$-stable $\lambda$-connections over a base parameter space $\Lambda$. This moduli space connects the irregular de Rham moduli space ($\lambda=1$) and the irregular Dolbeault moduli space of Higgs bundles equipped with non-zero irregular local exponents ($\lambda=0$).

arxiv:2610.40355.title: Bounds on the Diagonal Degree of the Biadjoint Scalar Amplitude Matrix
arxiv:2610.40355.summary: Biadjoint scalar theory partial amplitudes, $m_n(\alpha,\beta)$, define an $(n-1)!/2\times (n-1)!/2$ matrix, $M_n$, with rows and columns labeled by orderings. The CHY construction of $M_n$ implies that its rank is $(n-3)!$. Invertible submatrices of maximal rank enter in the KLT construction relating graviton amplitudes to gluon amplitudes.

arxiv:2610.40367.title: Johnson optimality and uniqueness for distance ratio $1:\sqrt{2}$
arxiv:2610.40367.summary: We prove that a two-distance set in $\mathbb R^d$ with distance ratio $1:\sqrt{2}$ has at most $d(d+1)/2$ points for every $d\ge9$. Equality in full affine dimension characterizes the Johnson construction; for $d\ge10$, the full-dimensional condition is automatic. The proof separates configurations according to the connectivity of the short-distance graph.
arxiv:2610.40367.authors: Bryan Bu, Chin-Yen Lee, Yu-Hang Sheng, Meng-Tsung Tsai, Hyunjun Yi, Wei-Hsuan Yu

arxiv:2610.40369.title: Half-Optimal Induced Matchings in Random Graphs: Online and Low-Degree Algorithms
arxiv:2610.40369.summary: For many optimization problems on random graphs, most prominently the largest independent set problem, natural algorithms reach only half the optimum, and such factor-two gaps are known to be sharp within broad algorithmic classes. We prove such a gap for finding large induced matchings in Erd\H{o}s-R\'enyi random graphs. In the worst case, requiring a matching to be induced turns a polynomial-time solvable problem into an NP-hard one; our results reveal an average-case counterpart.
arxiv:2610.40369.authors: Abhishek Dhawan, Eren C. K{\i}z{\i}lda\u{g}, Neeladri Maitra, Cheng Mao, Timothy L. H. Wee

arxiv:2610.40380.title: The maximum degree of Nosal graphs
arxiv:2610.40380.summary: A graph $G$ with $m$ edges is a Nosal graph if its spectral radius $\lambda(G)$ exceeds $\sqrt m$. At the threshold $\lambda(G)=\sqrt m$, the star $K_{1,m}$ shows that one vertex can be incident with all $m$ edges. In contrast, Li, Liu and Zhang [J.

arxiv:2610.40392.title: A dynamical approach to Frobenius splitting
arxiv:2610.40392.summary: A dynamical system can be associated to the process of decomposing iterated Frobenius pushforwards of modules into indecomposable direct summands. Via this connection, we apply the theory of Markov chains to study asymptotic counts of multiplicities of indecomposable summands in the iterated Frobenius pushforwards of the given module, as the number of iterations grows. Our results recover and extend the existing results on the existence of the (generalized) F-signature due to Hashimoto--Symonds, Hashimoto--Kobayashi, Smith--Van den Bergh, Tucker, and Yao.

arxiv:2610.40426.title: Aerodynamic Shape Optimization of unsteady flapping wings
arxiv:2610.40426.summary: This study introduces a new approach for building surrogate models, in the form of Reduced Order Models (ROMs), for PDE-constrained optimization. A physics-constrained data-driven framework is developed to transform large-scale non-linear optimization problems into ROM-constrained optimization problems. Unlike conventional methods, which suffer from instability of the forward sensitivity function, the proposed approach projects optimization problems to system dynamics optimization problems in Hilbert space to increase stability, diminish memory requirements, and lower computational cost.
arxiv:2610.40426.authors: Hamid R. Karbasian, Brian C. Vermeire

arxiv:2610.40438.title: On generic subsystems of a Smale space
arxiv:2610.40438.summary: We study properties of generic compact invariant subsystems of a fixed Smale space in the Hausdorff topology. For a transitive Smale space, we show that the hyperspace of all subsystems contains an open and dense family of NMC subsystems, a dynamically degenerate class with finite orbit structure. A substantially different picture emerges in the closure of the infinite transitive locus: minimality, unique ergodicity, and zero topological entropy are generic, while subsystems conjugate to regular Toeplitz shifts are dense.

arxiv:2610.40448.title: Process matrices on generalised theories
arxiv:2610.40448.summary: We extend the process-matrix framework for defining indefinite causal orders to a broad class of generalised physical theories. We give a simple re-axiomatisation of spacetime contexts in terms of naturality over classical probes, which precisely captures non-contextual assignment together with compatibility with convexity and coarse-graining within local laboratories. Using this compositional perspective, we give a clean characterisation of theories in which abstract spacetime contexts admit a process-matrix representation, and we pin down the precise conditions (satisfied by classical theory, quantum theory, and a Boxworld-like theory) under which the supermap and process-matrix…
arxiv:2610.40448.authors: Matt Wilson, James Hefford, Timoth\'ee Hoffreumon

arxiv:2610.40458.title: Thin ends and topological spanning trees
arxiv:2610.40458.summary: Halin conjectured in 1964 that every connected graph has an end-faithful spanning tree. He proved this for countable graphs, but in the early 1990s Seymour and Thomas and, independently, Thomassen found uncountable counterexamples. Both are infinitely connected and hence one-ended, and their unique end has uncountable degree (i.e.\ contains uncountably many pairwise disjoint rays).

arxiv:2610.40472.title: Bilinear operators along variable curves
arxiv:2610.40472.summary: Motivated by Zygmund's differentiation conjecture and Stein's conjecture for Lipschitz vector fields, we study bilinear singular integral and maximal operators along variable curves given by $$ \begin{aligned} BH_a^\alpha(f,g)(x) &= \operatorname{p.v.}\int_{\mathbb R} f(x-t) g\left(x + a(x)t^\alpha\right)\,\frac{dt}{t},\\ BM_a^\alpha(f,g)(x) &= \sup_{r>0}\frac{1}{2r}\int_{-r}^{r} \left|f(x-t)g\left(x+a(x)t^\alpha\right)\right|\,dt,\\ BSH_c^\alpha(f,g)(x) &= \operatorname{p.v.} \int_{\mathbb R} f(x-t) g(x + t^\alpha)\, \frac{dt}{t-c(x)}, \end{aligned} $$ where $\alpha > 0$ and $a,c:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ are measurable. For every $\alpha>0$ and $0<A<B<\infty$, we construct a smooth, globally…

arxiv:2610.40475.title: Finite-rank rigidity and Nash-curve discreteness for correlation potentials
arxiv:2610.40475.summary: For every nonconstant real polynomial P of degree k and every positive rational exponent a/b, minimizing the spherical energy with potential |P(t)|^{a/b} admits a discrete solution with at most $\binom{d+2ak-1}{2ak}+\binom{d+2ak-2}{2ak-1}$ support points, where a/b is reduced. This finite-replacement consequence needs no denominator threshold. Under a multiplicity-sensitive denominator condition, we prove the stronger conclusion that every minimizer has an explicit uniform support bound; suitable negative positive-semidefinite perturbations preserve that bound.

arxiv:2610.40486.title: Average pairwise Hamming distance of a subset in a hypercube
arxiv:2610.40486.summary: In this note, we prove that for a subset $\mathcal{F}$ of $\{0,1\}^n$ of density $\frac{1}{8}$, its average pairwise Hamming distance is at least $\frac{n-3}{2}$, with equality attained only by $(n-3)$-dimensional subcubes. This answers a question of Lei Yu, and solves an important open case of a more general question posed by Ahlswede and Katona in 1977.

arxiv:2610.40489.title: Multiple representations in difference sets under polynomial density constraints
arxiv:2610.40489.summary: Motivated by the classical study of additive representation functions and the combinatorial phenomenon of sum-difference asymmetry, we investigate the subtractive representation function $d_{\mathcal{B},\mathcal{A}}(n)$, which counts the number of solutions of the equation $n = b - a$ with $a\in \mathcal{A}$ and $b\in \mathcal{B}$. Specifically, we study lower bounds and the asymptotic behavior of $d_{\mathcal{B},\mathcal{A}}(n)$ under polynomial density constraints of orders $x^\alpha$ and $x^{1-\alpha}$, where $0 < \alpha < 1$. We first establish a general lower bound for the first moment of $d_{\mathcal{B},\mathcal{A}}(n)$.
arxiv:2610.40489.authors: Yuchen Ding, S\'andor Z. Kiss, Wei Niu, P\'eter P\'al Pach, Csaba S\'andor

arxiv:2610.40496.title: Real-rooted Ehrhart $h^*$-polynomials of crown posets and wheel and whirl matroids
arxiv:2610.40496.summary: We prove that the Ehrhart $h^*$-polynomials of crown order polytopes are real-rooted, settling a conjecture of Lundstr\"om and Saud Maia Leite. For each integer $r\ge3$, the crown order polytope on $2r$ elements and the rank-$r$ whirl base polytope have the same $h^*$-polynomial. The $h^*$-polynomials of the rank-$r$ wheel and whirl base polytopes, as well as every convex combination of the two, have $2r-2$ distinct negative roots.

arxiv:2610.40498.title: Dihedral pointed fusion categories: diagrammatics, 3-cocycle representatives, and planar algebras
arxiv:2610.40498.summary: We construct a diagrammatic presentation by generators and relations for all dihedral pointed fusion categories $\mathrm{Vec}_{\mathrm{D}_{2n}}^{\omega}$. Applying a jellyfish algorithm on our diagrammatics, we obtain an explicit closed formula for a complete set of normalized 3-cocycle representatives of $\mathrm{D}_{2n}$. As applications of our diagrammatics, we prove a universal property and show that in some cases we can recover affine $A$ unshaded subfactor planar algebras.

arxiv:2610.40521.title: Directed Cut-Query Complexity of Finding a King
arxiv:2610.40521.summary: A king in a tournament is a vertex from which every other vertex is reachable by a directed path of length at most two. We study the deterministic query complexity of finding a king when a query specifies a set of vertices and returns the number of edges directed from that set to its complement. We prove that this complexity is $\Theta(n)$ for $n$-vertex tournaments.
arxiv:2610.40521.authors: Ziad Ismaili Alaoui, Oded Lachish, Nikhil S. Mande

arxiv:2610.40568.title: Presentations for sisters of one-cusped Picard modular groups
arxiv:2610.40568.summary: We generalize a method devised by Mark and Paupert for finding group presentations of the single-cusped standard Picard modular groups $\text{PU}(2, 1; \mathcal{O}_d)$, where $\mathcal{O}_d$ is the ring of integers of $\mathbb{Q}(i\sqrt{d})$, to a more general class of lattices in $\text{PU}(2, 1)$. As an application, we give presentations for the so-called \textit{sisters} of the standard Picard modular groups for $d=3, 7,$ and $11$. In particular, this shows that the sister of $\text{PU}(2, 1; \mathcal{O}_7)$ is a perfect group.

arxiv:2610.40570.title: Supersaturation: Cliques and Positive Square Energy
arxiv:2610.40570.summary: Let $G$ be a simple graph of order $n$ and let $k_r$ denote the number of unlabeled copies of $K_r$ in $G$. Let $s^+$ denote the sum of the squares of the positive adjacency eigenvalues of $G$. For every fixed integer $r\geq2$, we prove that, as $n \to \infty$ \[ \sqrt{s^+}>\left(1-\frac1r\right)n \quad\Longrightarrow\quad k_{r+1}\geq \left(\frac1{r^{r-1}}-o_r(1)\right)n^{r-1}.
arxiv:2610.40570.authors: Abhay Jayarajan, M. Rajesh Kannan, Shivaramakrishna Pragada

arxiv:2610.40571.title: On the Quantum Chromatic Gap II
arxiv:2610.40571.summary: We confirm a conjecture of the first author [SODA'26] on a strong form of pseudo-telepathy for Khot's $d$-to-$1$ games: for every $d\geq 4$, every $\epsilon>0$, and every $k\in\mathbb N$, there is a $d$-to-$1$ label-cover game of classical value less than $\epsilon$ that admits a perfect quantum strategy using finite-dimensional shared entanglement with measurement contexts of radius at least $k$. As a consequence, there exist graphs whose quantum chromatic number $\chi_q$ is $3$ and whose classical chromatic number $\chi$ is arbitrarily large. This is the first improvement on the quantum chromatic gap since the work of Brassard, Cleve, and Tapp [Phys.

arxiv:2610.40583.title: Asymptotic GIT-stability of KSB-stable varieties
arxiv:2610.40583.summary: We prove that KSB-stable varieties introduced by Koll\'ar and Shepherd-Barron as a generalization of Deligne-Mumford's stable curves are stable in the sense of geometric invariant theory (GIT). More precisely, we show that KSB-stable varieties are asymptotically GIT-stable with respect to a sequence of linearizations defined by the Hodge bundle.

arxiv:2610.40590.title: An Adian-Rabin theorem for quantum automorphism groups of graphs
arxiv:2610.40590.summary: Given a graph $G$, does it have quantum symmetries, or in other words, is the algebra of the quantum automorphism group non-commutative? In the world of ordinary groups, determining whether a finitely presented group is commutative is undecidable. This is an immediate consequence of the Adian-Rabin theorem, which shows that many natural properties of finitely presented groups are undecidable.
arxiv:2610.40590.authors: Josse van Dobben de Bruyn, William Slofstra

arxiv:2610.40602.title: Permutation twisted cohomology, reduced and immersed
arxiv:2610.40602.summary: In this paper, we introduce a `reduced' form of permutation twisted cohomology as introduced by Balmer--Gallauer and further developed by Miller. This ring is bigraded by a well-chosen choice of endotrivial complex, rather than multigraded by a family of endotrivial complexes. The Balmer spectrum of the small derived category of permutation modules openly immerses into the homogeneous spectrum of this ring.
arxiv:2610.40602.authors: Juan Omar G\'omez, Sam K. Miller

arxiv:2610.40622.title: The Number of Tropical Order Types and Coherent Matching Fields
arxiv:2610.40622.summary: We investigate counting problems for discrete (geometric) structures in tropical settings, motivated by the comparison of the expressivity of linear programs and mean-payoff games. First, we give an upper bound on the number of coherent matching fields of type $(n,r)$ and a lower bound on the number of combinatorial types of $n$-hyperplane sequences in the max-plus tropical space of dimension $r-1$. These structures are closely related, and our bounds establish that as $n \to \infty$, for every fixed $r$ their number equals $n^{(r-1)^2n+o(n)}$.
arxiv:2610.40622.authors: Xavier Allamigeon, Yiyuan Chen, St\'ephane Gaubert, Xavier Goaoc

arxiv:2610.40639.title: Multicomplexes in Action: Strong Formality of Compact Hyperk\"ahler Manifolds
arxiv:2610.40639.summary: We show that all compact hyperk\"ahler manifolds are bigraded strongly formal in the sense of Milivojevi\'c and Stelzig, proving that in the context of pluripotential homotopy theory they play the same role as compact K\"ahler manifolds in rational homotopy theory. Indeed, the main result arises from general algebraic considerations on categories of objects with more differentials, that of multicomplexes and commutative $n$-differential graded algebras. For them we discuss a standard model category structure, introduce a generalization of the $\partial\bar{\partial}$-Lemma and establish an algebraic formality theorem.

arxiv:2610.40661.title: Weighted flip graphs from cyclic quantum mutations: pentagon inequalities and exponential separations
arxiv:2610.40661.summary: Positive cyclic quantum mutations at a third root of unity induce an explicit weight on polygon flip graphs. We study the resulting discrepancy between minimum flip count and minimum accumulated normalization loss. Every pentagon three-to-two replacement strictly decreases weight, and in connected types $A_1$, $A_2$, and $A_3$ every minimum-weight path is a flip geodesic.

arxiv:2610.40667.title: Tree-based Algorithms for Breakpoint Median and Near-Median Genomes
arxiv:2610.40667.summary: Median genomes serve as candidates for ancestral reconstruction and help study the diversity of parsimonious rearrangement solutions. However, the breakpoint median problem is NP-hard for unichromosomal genomes, and medians are non-unique, making their diversity important to study. In this paper, we develop tree-based algorithms for studying breakpoint medians of linear unichromosomal genomes represented as unsigned permutations.
arxiv:2610.40667.authors: Poly H. da Silva, Arash Jamshidpey, David Sankoff

arxiv:2610.40673.title: Descent and Decomposability of Algebras of Exponent 2 in characteristic 2
arxiv:2610.40673.summary: We define an invariant of central simple algebras of degree 8 and exponent 2 over fields of characteristic 2. It is built from the discriminant Pfister forms of symplectic involutions, takes values in a quotient of the third part of the graded group associated to the fundamental filtration of the Witt group of quadratic forms, and vanishes on tensor products of three quaternion algebras, thus giving a necessary condition for decomposability. Variants of the consctuction yield necessary and sufficient conditions for a biquaternion algebra to descend from a quadratic extension of the base field, and for a quaternion algebra to descent from a biquadratic extension that is not purely…

arxiv:2610.40683.title: A Winner Classification for Rooted Partizan Edge Geography on Heterogeneous Bouquets of Cycles
arxiv:2610.40683.summary: We consider an undirected edge-traversal game on a finite bouquet of simple cycles. Each of two players controls a token, both tokens begin at the common root, and the players alternate traversing edges that have not been used by either token. A player with no legal move loses.

arxiv:2610.40691.title: Sharp bounds, stability, and arithmetic fluctuations for induced pentagons
arxiv:2610.40691.summary: We prove that every graph with $m>0$ edges contains at most $\frac{3}{2\sqrt{2}}(\frac{m}{5})^{5/2}$ induced pentagons. Equality holds precisely for balanced blow-ups of the Clebsch graph, together with isolated vertices. The bound and equality classification extend to arbitrary nonnegative vertex weights and to all graphons, including fractional graphons.

arxiv:2610.40694.title: Four runners that are barely lonely
arxiv:2610.40694.summary: For positive integers $v_1,\dots,v_n$ let $\mathrm{ML}(v_1,\dots,v_n)=\max_t\min_i\|v_it\|$, where $\|x\|$ is the distance to the nearest integer. Kravitz asked which values below $1/n$ occur. For $n=4$, Jain and Kravitz showed that the values below $1/4$ are $m/(4m+2)$, $m\ge2$, up to finitely many undetermined exceptions.
arxiv:2610.40694.authors: Hyunjun Yi, Karam Gill, Bryan Bu

arxiv:2610.40696.title: Asymptotic stability of clique-saturating edges near Tur\'an thresholds
arxiv:2610.40696.summary: Let $f_{p+1}(n,m)$ denote the minimum number of $K_{p+1}$-saturating edges in an $n$-vertex $K_{p+1}$-free graph with $m$ edges. In this paper, we investigate the stability of this parameter near the Tur\'an thresholds, with particular emphasis on the role of the minimum degree. We introduce the refined parameter $f_{p+1,p}(n,m,\delta)$.

arxiv:2610.40703.title: The Hibi--Li (2016) conjecture is fully resolved
arxiv:2610.40703.summary: Hibi and Li conjectured that the order polytope $\mathcal{O}(P)$ of a finite poset $P$ has at most as many faces of each dimension as its chain polytope $\mathcal{C}(P)$, and that equality in some dimension $k$ with $1\leq k\leq|P|-1$ forces the two polytopes to be unimodularly equivalent. Fourier proved the inequality in a 2026 preprint. Let $X$ be the five-element poset in which an element lies above two incomparable elements and below two other incomparable elements.

arxiv:2610.40712.title: Anti-concentration and Graham's rearrangement problem in finite abelian groups
arxiv:2610.40712.summary: Let $S$ be a subset of $n$ elements of a group $G$. An ordering $x_1,\ldots,x_n$ of its elements is valid if the partial sums $x_1,x_1+x_2,\ldots,x_1+\cdots+x_n$ are pairwise distinct. This notion has a long history in combinatorial group theory, dated back to Gordon's works in early 1960.
arxiv:2610.40712.authors: Hoi H. Nguyen, Tuan Tran, Van H. Vu

arxiv:2610.40746.title: Homotopy in enriched functor categories: Frobenius exact structures and weak Serre functors
arxiv:2610.40746.summary: Let $(\V, \otimes, I,[-,-])$ be a closed symmetric monoidal category with finite (co)limits. Assume that $\V$ is weakly idempotent complete and additive. For a given small $\V$-category $\A$, we investigate sufficient conditions on $\A$ under which the ordinary category $[\A, \V]_0$ of $\V$-functors from $\A$ to $\V$, equipped with the exact structure $\mathcal{E}_{\textrm{lowt}}$, is a Frobenius exact category,and hence, induces a triangulated stable category.

arxiv:2610.40750.title: Systolic Geometry and Combinatorics of Surfaces
arxiv:2610.40750.summary: This thesis investigates two themes. The first studies systolic embeddings of graph on translation surfaces, proving existence results for essential and cellular systolic embeddings and determining extremal genera for certain graph families. The second examines hyperbolic surfaces in the Thurston set, constructing a one-parameter deformation that increases the sys- tole length and produces Bolza-like surfaces, i.e., surfaces whose systolic geodesics decompose the surfaces into triangles, for infinitely many genera.

arxiv:2610.40777.title: On Boundary State Screening via Solitons
arxiv:2610.40777.summary: We present a coarse classification scheme for the boundary data of massive QFTs based on transitions of boundary states via soliton / kink profiles. Starting from the lattice of boundary states, we introduce the boundary screening group $\mathbb{B}$: the equivalence classes of boundary states which cannot be connected by such transitions. In string theory backgrounds which geometrically engineer an interacting QFT in the target space, $\mathbb{B}$ computes the worldsheet analog of the target space defect group $\mathbb{D}$.
arxiv:2610.40777.authors: Vivek Chakrabhavi, Babak Haghighat, Jonathan J. Heckman

arxiv:2610.40779.title: Monopole-Fermion Scattering from Twisted Conformal Boundary States
arxiv:2610.40779.summary: We derive monopole-fermion scattering correlators from conformal boundary states in twisted sectors. The key ingredient is that symmetry-preserving boundary conditions contain sectors twisted by topological symmetry lines. Their overlaps determine correlators of operators attached to these lines, including the outgoing excitations required by charge conservation in the Callan-Rubakov effect.
arxiv:2610.40779.authors: Clay C\'ordova, Diego Garc\'ia-Sep\'ulveda, Lian-Tao Wang, Yen-Chieh Wang

arxiv:2610.40802.title: Exotic involutions on irreducible 4-manifolds from Real Seiberg--Witten theory
arxiv:2610.40802.summary: Using Real Seiberg--Witten theory, Miyazawa constructed infinitely many exotic involutions on ${\overline{\mathbb{CP}}{}^2}$, and Baraglia extended this construction to $X\#{\overline{\mathbb{CP}}{}^2}$ for a broad class of $4$-manifolds $X$ equipped with an involution $c$. We show that, under suitable Real Seiberg--Witten hypotheses, the ${\overline{\mathbb{CP}}{}^2}$ summand can be omitted when $X$ is non-spin and the complement of the fixed locus is simply-connected. Our construction also yields infinite families of topologically isotopic but smoothly non-isotopic embeddings of the branch surface in the quotient $X/\langle c\rangle$.

arxiv:2610.40806.title: Tate and Artin--Tate Motivic Tensor-Triangular Geometry
arxiv:2610.40806.summary: We compute the Balmer spectra of geometric Tate and Artin--Tate motives with $\mathbb{F}_p$-coefficients over any field whose characteristic differs from $p$. For Tate motives, we find the bigraded comparison map to be a homeomorphism to the homogeneous spectrum of the motivic cohomology of the base field. For Artin--Tate motives, we describe the spectrum as a gluing of the spectrum of Artin motives computed by Balmer--Gallauer with the punctured Tate spectrum.

arxiv:2610.40811.title: Integral Hodge structures and atoms of fourfolds
arxiv:2610.40811.summary: Following the recent work by OpenAI on the irrationality of very general cubic fourfolds in Hassett divisors, we prove some compatibility of Iritani's blow-up formula with the classical blow-up decomposition of integral Hodge structures. As a consequence, we express OpenAI's birational invariant in terms of the theory of atoms developped by Katzarkov--Kontsevich--Pantev--Yu. We also show that, for every smooth complex rational cubic fourfold, the primitive cohomology is isometric as an integral Hodge structure to the twisted middle cohomology of a K3 surface and we prove irrationality of the very general Verra fourfold.

arxiv:2610.40815.title: Integral Brauer--Manin Obstruction for Fermat Near Misses
arxiv:2610.40815.summary: We study the integral Hasse principle for the affine surfaces given by $x^4+y^4-w^2=m^2$, where $m>1$ is odd and squarefree. We give a criterion to determine if there is an integral Brauer--Manin obstruction, which depends only on simple congruence conditions on the prime factors of $m$ modulo $8$. We use this to show that for $100\%$ of such surfaces there is no integral Brauer--Manin obstruction to the Hasse principle for integral points.

arxiv:2610.40863.title: The Cranston--Li--Su--Wang--Xu (2026) conjecture is true
arxiv:2610.40863.summary: Let $A$ be a finite abelian group. A nowhere-zero $A$-flow of a graph gives every edge a direction and a non-zero value in $A$, so that at every vertex the sum of the values on the entering edges equals the sum on the leaving edges. Such a flow can be changed along a cycle: going around the cycle, add a fixed non-zero element of $A$ to the value of every edge that points forward and subtract it from the value of every edge that points backward.

arxiv:2610.40882.title: Foatic Homomesy
arxiv:2610.40882.summary: Using a unified method of identifying a telescoping function for each statistic-action pair, we prove conjectures of La Croix and Roby, and of Sheridan-Rossi that various permutation statistics, such as the number of fixed points, are homomesic under Foatic actions: compositions of the Foata bijection and dihedral symmetries of one-line notation. Underlying these results is a family of bijective identities relating permutation statistics across the Foata bijection; one of them --- an unexpected invariance of the number of right-to-left minima under reverse-complement, proved by an explicit bijection --- may be of independent interest. The telescoping functions also turn out to be shared…

arxiv:2610.40891.title: Truncated Grassmannians: polytopes, representations, and Cauchy formulas
arxiv:2610.40891.summary: The goal of this paper is to develop algebraic and combinatorial techniques for studying the geometric properties of truncated Grassmannians, a class of algebraic varieties obtained via certain projections of classical Grassmannians within their Pl\"ucker embeddings. We introduce a class of cyclic representations of maximal parabolic subalgebras of the general linear Lie algebra, which are proved to serve as duals of the homogeneous components of coordinate rings of truncated Grassmannians. We prove that the characters of these representations are computed via truncated Cauchy formulas and establish a connection with coordinate rings of complete collineations.

arxiv:2610.40896.title: Equivariant Gradient Degree Comparison via Clarke Duality for Strongly Indefinite Hamiltonian Systems
arxiv:2610.40896.summary: We study equivariant gradient degree comparisons for strongly indefinite Hamiltonian systems through Clarke duality. Under suitable convexity and compactness assumptions, we establish a correspondence between the primal and dual equations that preserves the symmetries of their solutions. We derive an identity relating their negative spectral representations and show that the Galerkin-normalized local index of the primal linearization coincides with the equivariant gradient degree determined by the dual Hessian.

arxiv:2610.40915.title: Higher limits over the fusion orbit category via subgroup complexes
arxiv:2610.40915.summary: Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a saturated fusion system over a finite $p$-group $S$, and $\mathcal{O}^c (\mathcal{F})$ denote the centric orbit category of $\mathcal{F}$. Suppose that $G$ is a discrete group realizing $\mathcal{F}$, and $\mathcal{C}$ is the collection of all $p$-centric subgroups in $G$. We prove that for every $\mathbb{Z}_{(p)} \mathcal{O} ^c (\mathcal{F})$-module $M$, the higher limits $\lim ^* _{\mathcal{O}^c (\mathcal{F})} M$ are isomorphic to the equivariant cohomology $H_ G ^* (|\mathcal{C}| ; \mathcal{M} )$, where $\mathcal{M}$ is the $G$-equivariant coefficient system on $|\mathcal{C}|$ induced by $M$.

arxiv:2610.40950.title: Uniformization of compact K\"ahler Threefolds of Zero Kodaira Dimension
arxiv:2610.40950.summary: Given two smooth compact K\"ahler threefolds $X$ and $Y$ whose universal covers are biholomorphic, we show that $\kappa(X) = 0$ if and only if $\kappa(Y) =0$.

arxiv:2610.40957.title: On lens spaces which may embed in the complex projective plane
arxiv:2610.40957.summary: Using an obstruction derived by Owens and relying on Donaldson's Diagonalisation Theorem, we obtain a complete classification of lens spaces of Lisca type $(2)$ or $(3)$ that are unobstructed from embedding in a homology complex projective plane. This classification is further refined for lens spaces $L(p,q)$ with $p$ even, using an obstruction due to Lidman--Moore--Vazquez based on work of Lin. This article is extracted from the author's PhD thesis.

arxiv:2610.40984.title: RC Prediction: A Python Package for Parameter-Aware Reservoir Computing
arxiv:2610.40984.summary: A nonlinear dynamical system can be characterized by the autonomous evolution of its state in time and its dependence on system parameters. As a parameter varies, the dynamics can change quantitatively and, at bifurcation points, qualitatively. When the governing equations are unknown, a data-driven model should therefore capture both elements from observational data, rather than reproduce the dynamics at a single operating condition only.
arxiv:2610.40984.authors: Jin-Cheng Rao, Zheng-Meng Zhai, Ying-Cheng Lai

arxiv:2610.40987.title: Handlebodies separate elements of surface groups
arxiv:2610.40987.summary: In this note I prove that every non-trivial element of the fundamental group of a closed orientable surface X is non-trivial in the fundamental group of some handlebody with boundary X. This result appears to be folklore. I have uploaded a proof as the result is needed in a joint project with Clement Dupont on mapping class group actions on configuration spaces.

arxiv:2610.40989.title: Hyperelliptic curves on $(1,d)$ abelian surfaces for $d\leq 15$
arxiv:2610.40989.summary: Bryan, Oberdieck, Pandharipande and Yin predicted the number of hyperelliptic curves on general abelian surfaces under a transversality condition. Some of the numbers have already been confirmed. In this paper we construct singular hyperelliptic curves on $(1,d)$ polarised abelian surfaces for $d\leq 15$ confirming a few predicted numbers, namely of (geometric) genus $g=d$ and of geometric genus $k+3$ on $(1,2k)$ and $(1,2k+1)$ polarised surfaces.
arxiv:2610.40989.authors: Pawe{\l} Bor\'owka, Paolo Grossi, Anatoli Shatsila

arxiv:2610.41002.title: Lengths of closed geodesics on random non-compact hyperbolic surfaces
arxiv:2610.41002.summary: We study the asymptotic distribution of the number of primitive, closed geodesics on Weil-Petersson random hyperbolic surfaces with genus $g$ and $n(g)$ cusps, under various growth rates of $n(g)$ as $g\to\infty$. We prove that the limiting distribution is Poisson with parameter depending explicitly on the limit of $n(g)^2/g$. This work is inspired by that of Mirzakhani and Petri's on closed surfaces and Hide and Thomas when $g$ is fixed.

arxiv:2610.41010.title: The Table Problem for Convex Domains
arxiv:2610.41010.summary: We prove a generalized Table Theorem for bounded convex domains in the plane. Then we prove a variation of the Table Problem for compactly supported functions on the plane. Our method is based on relating the table problem on a surface to the square peg problem for a configuration of star-shaped curves in the tangent bundle of the surface.

arxiv:2610.41013.title: Functorial Analysis of Group-Alphabet Cellular Automata
arxiv:2610.41013.summary: Let $G$ be a group and let $n\in\mathbb N$. We consider one-dimensional cellular automata of length $n$ over the alphabet $G$, with periodic boundary conditions and with local rules $\phi$ given by words. We construct a functor $F$ from $\mathbf{Grp}$, the category of groups (or any similar algebraic structure), to the category of pointed digraphs, and show its faithfulness.

arxiv:2610.41031.title: Rational curves of submaximal quantum index
arxiv:2610.41031.summary: On a complex toric surface, oriented real rational curves tangent to the toric boundary at real points are distinguished by their value of quantum index. Using variants of usual Welschinger multiplicities, G. Mikhalkin defined enumerative invariants $W_{\tilde{\Delta}}^{\kappa}$ that are provided by a signed count of oriented real rational curves with given quantum index $\kappa$ and fixed tangency points on the boundary of the positive quadrant (the tangency orders being encoded by $\tilde{\Delta}$).

arxiv:2610.41060.title: An explicit bound on the extremal function for complete graph minors
arxiv:2610.41060.summary: Kostochka and Thomason independently proved that every graph with density at least $\beta\,t\sqrt{\log t}$ has a $K_t$ minor, for some constant $\beta$. Thomason later proved that the least such density is $(0.319\ldots+o(1))\,t\sqrt{\log t}$. However, the $o(1)$ term in this formula is not explicit, so the formula gives no bound for any specific value of $t$.

arxiv:2610.41068.title: Initial Subcategories via Free Presentations of the Constant Functor
arxiv:2610.41068.summary: Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a small category. We characterize the full initial subcategories of $\mathcal{C}$ as precisely those whose representables give a free presentation of the constant functor $\Delta_{\mathcal{C}}\mathbb{K}:\mathcal{C}\to\mathrm{Vect}$. Such a presentation yields a formula for the limit of any functor $\mathcal{C} \to \mathrm{Vect}$ as the kernel of a morphism between products of evaluations.
arxiv:2610.41068.authors: Thomas Br\"ustle, Justin Desrochers, Samuel Leblanc

arxiv:2610.41096.title: Unavoidable flats in matroids excluding a uniform minor
arxiv:2610.41096.summary: We extend a theorem of Geelen, Kroeker, and Nelson on unavoidable flats in $\operatorname{GF}(q)$-representable matroids. For all integers $1\le a\le b$ and $n\ge1$, we prove that every simple matroid of sufficiently large rank with no $U_{a,b}$-minor has a rank-$n$ flat whose restriction is free or isomorphic to a projective or affine geometry over a finite field.

arxiv:2610.41102.title: Variance Bounds and Strict Log-Concavity for Forest Coronas
arxiv:2610.41102.summary: We prove that the size of a random independent set in every nonempty forest has variance strictly smaller than its mean at common activity $0<t\le1$. A rooted quadratic reserve gives quantitative forms of this inequality. Mean matching transfers the bounds to fixed-weight canonical completion laws, and exact binomial moments prove strict log-concavity for every forest corona and every well-covered forest.

arxiv:2610.41105.title: Defect TQFTs, the Generalized Cobordism Hypothesis, and Algebraic $K$-Theory
arxiv:2610.41105.summary: By constructing a fully dualizable category $\mathrm{Bord}^{\mathcal{C}}_n$ as the left adjoint of the forgetful functor, we state a generalized cobordism hypothesis. As a corollary, we establish a generalized Pontryagin-Thom isomorphism that gives a geometric interpretation of higher algebraic $K$-theory using cobordism classes of framed manifolds and stratified spaces decorated by categorical string diagrams, which we call lasagnas. For finite-dimensional vector spaces over a field, these decorations are branched local systems.

arxiv:2610.41110.title: Deck Reconstruction for Restricted Word Classes
arxiv:2610.41110.summary: For a binary word $x\in \{0,1\}^+$, the $k$-deck of $x$ is the multiset of all length-$k$ subsequences counted with multiplicity. The deck reconstruction problem asks for the minimum $k$ such that every word of a fixed length is uniquely determined by its $k$-deck. In this paper, we study deck reconstruction for several restricted classes of binary words, including words with exactly $s$ ones, words with at most $\ell$ runs of ones, and words where the indices of ones are given by a monotone polynomial of degree $d$.
arxiv:2610.41110.authors: Krishna Angal, Ruben Ascoli, Simon X. He, Xiaoyu He, Logan Post, Arker Oke Soe, Olga Zhukova

arxiv:2610.41120.title: Quantum Vehicle Routing Problem: a smart initialization strategy for ill-conditioned optimization landscapes
arxiv:2610.41120.summary: With the expansion of complex transport infrastructure, new paths for linking different destinations have emerged, allowing the definition of multiple routes. The introduction of new roads may also lead to disruptions in traffic flow. This problem can be generalized into a special case of VRP, which aims to find the optimal route for a fleet of vehicles within a network of destinations.
arxiv:2610.41120.authors: Emanuele Casciaro, Mario De Simone, Stefano Martina, Fabio Mascherpa, Alfonso Amendola, Filippo Caruso

arxiv:2610.41123.title: Circular regular dessins with underlying graphs ${\bf K}_{2^e,2^f}^{(2^d)}$: the metacyclic case
arxiv:2610.41123.summary: A dessin is a 2-cell embedding of a connected bipartite graph into an orientable closed surface. It is regular if the colour- and orientation-preserving automorphism group acts regularly on edges, and circular if every face boundary is a simple cycle. We classify and enumerate circular regular dessins of the complete bipartite multigraph ${\bf K}_{2^e,2^f}^{(2^d)}$ ($e\ge f\ge 2$, $d\ge 1$) whose automorphism group is {\it metacyclic}.

arxiv:2610.41125.title: Bounds for lattice points in terms of volume and successive minima
arxiv:2610.41125.summary: We prove, in every dimension, the upper bound conjectured by Betke, Henk and Wills for the lattice-point enumerator in terms of volume and successive minima. For every convex body $K\subset R^n$ and full-rank lattice $\Lambda$, we establish $$ \#(K\cap\Lambda)\le\frac{\mathrm{vol}_n(K)}{\det\Lambda}\prod_{i=1}^n\left(1+\frac{i\lambda_i}{2}\right), $$ where $\lambda_i$ are the successive minima of $(K-K)/2$ with respect to $\Lambda$. Equality holds precisely for lattice translates of positive integral dilates of unimodular simplices.

arxiv:2610.41150.title: Smith Algebra from $\mathfrak{sl}_2$ Tensor Product Branching via the Mickelsson-Zhelobenko Algebra
arxiv:2610.41150.summary: Let $L_n$ be the finite-dimensional irreducible $\mathfrak{sl}_2$-module of highest weight $n$. We study the space of highest-weight vectors in $L_n\otimes L_m$ for the diagonal $\mathfrak{sl}_2$-action. The extremal projector constructs these singular vectors and gives operators connecting the highest-weight lines in the Clebsch-Gordan decomposition.
arxiv:2610.41150.authors: Kohei Hasegawa, Takuya Matsumoto, Akito Takashima

arxiv:2610.41151.title: Solyanik Estimates for Ergodic Flows
arxiv:2610.41151.summary: Let $\{T_t\}_{t\in\mathbb R}$ be a measure-preserving flow on a probability space $(\Omega,\Sigma,\mu)$ and let $T^*$ be the associated one-sided ergodic maximal operator. We show that the sharp Tauberian constant $C(\alpha)=\sup_{\mu(E)>0}\frac{\mu(\{T^*\chi_E>\alpha\})}{\mu(E)}$,$0<\alpha<1$, equals $1/\alpha$ for every $\alpha\in(0,1)$, unless every measurable set is invariant modulo null sets, in which case $C(\alpha)=1$ for every $\alpha$. In particular the Solyanik estimate $\lim_{\alpha\to1^-}C(\alpha)=1$ holds for every measure-preserving flow, and for ergodic flows on nonatomic spaces the estimate $C(\alpha)-1\le 1/\alpha-1$ holds with equality.

arxiv:2610.41155.title: Changing parameters in Hall-Littlewood functions
arxiv:2610.41155.summary: We study the transition coefficients $b_{\lambda,\mu}(q,t)$ of the Hall--Littlewood $P$-functions $P_\lambda(t)$ expanded in the basis $P_\mu(q)$. We find a tableaux formula when $\lambda$ is a hook shape which generalizes term-by-term Lascoux-Schutzenberger's charge formula as well as Macdonald's monomial expansion formula for Hall-Littlewood functions. We conjecture that $b_{\lambda,\mu}(t+1,t)\in\mathbb{Z}_{\ge0}[t]$ and prove it when $\lambda$ is a hook shape, when $\lambda$ has two-columns and some more simple cases.
arxiv:2610.41155.authors: Aritra Bhattacharya, Ziyi Dai, Qilin Hou, Edward Tong

arxiv:2610.41156.title: Sharp Solyanik Estimates for Discrete and Ergodic Hardy--Littlewood Maximal Operators
arxiv:2610.41156.summary: Let $U_1,\dots,U_n$ be commuting invertible measure-preserving transformations of a probability space, and let $C^{*}_{\mathrm{HL}}(\alpha)$ denote the sharp Tauberian constant of the associated ergodic uncentered Hardy--Littlewood maximal operator. Hagelstein and Parissis showed that $C^{*}_{\mathrm{HL}}(\alpha)-1\lesssim_n(1/\alpha-1)^{1/(n(n+1))}$ as $\alpha\to1^-$ and asked whether this exponent is sharp. We prove that $C^{*}_{\mathrm{HL}}(\alpha)-1\lesssim_n(1/\alpha-1)^{1/n}$ for all such transformations, and that this is sharp: equality of the ergodic and discrete Tauberian constants holds for every action admitting arbitrarily large Rokhlin towers (in particular for every free…

arxiv:2610.41174.title: An atomic approach to Shokurov's conic-bundle conjecture
arxiv:2610.41174.summary: In this paper, we apply a weaker version of Hodge atoms to show that a standard conic bundle over a smooth complex projective rational surface $S$ is irrational if $|2K_S+\Delta|\ne\emptyset$, where $\Delta$ is the discriminant divisor. This proves Shokurov's conjecture on rationality of conic bundle threefolds. As an application, we deduce precisely which nodal quartic double solids are rational.
arxiv:2610.41174.authors: Leonardo F. Cavenaghi, Ludmil Katzarkov, Daniel Pomerleano, Zhijia Zhang

arxiv:2610.41178.title: Traveling Salesman Problem on Graphs with Proportional Independent Set
arxiv:2610.41178.summary: We give a deterministic algorithm for minimum-cost Hamiltonian cycle in undirected graphs with arbitrary real edge costs and an independent set of size at least $\alpha n$, for any fixed $3/7<\alpha\le1/2$. It runs in $O^*(\gamma(\alpha)^n)$ time for an explicit constant $\gamma(\alpha)<2$; for bipartite graphs, the bound is $O^*((1+2\sqrt2)^{n/2})\approx O^*(1.957^n)$. The algorithm is based on a restricted Held--Karp dynamic program.
arxiv:2610.41178.authors: Ethan X. Fang, Shengtao Guo, Junwei Lu, Yuan Yao

arxiv:2610.41203.title: Rainbow Hamiltonian paths in graph collections under edge-size conditions
arxiv:2610.41203.summary: Let $\mathbf{G}=\{G_1,\dots,G_{n-1}\}$ be a collection of not necessarily distinct graphs of order $n$ on the same vertex set $V$. A path $P$ with $V(P)\subseteq V$ is called \emph{rainbow} in $\mathbf{G}$, if there exists an injection $\phi\colon E(P)\to [n-1]$ such that $e\in E(G_{\phi(e)})$ for each $e\in E(P)$. In this paper, we show that if $n\ge3$, $e(G_i)> \binom{n-2}{2}+2$ for each $i\in[n-1]$ and $G_j$ is connected for some $j\in[n-1]$, then there exists a rainbow Hamiltonian path in $\mathbf{G}$ unless $n=6$ with $G_1=G_2=\dots=G_{5}\cong K_2\vee 4K_1$, or $n=8$ with $G_1=G_2=\dots=G_{7}\cong K_3\vee 5K_1$.

arxiv:2610.41233.title: Orientations for skein-valued curve counting
arxiv:2610.41233.summary: Ekholm and Shende's skeins-on-branes formalism provides invariant counts of holomorphic curves with boundary on a Maslov zero Lagrangian within a Calabi-Yau 3-fold. This paper proves the orientation relations required for worldsheet skein relations to cancel codimension-one boundary strata. However, standard Cauchy-Riemann Fredholm orientations reveal an unexpected sign puzzle: the orientation relation at a curve with a hyperbolic boundary crossing depends on whether the crossing lies on distinct boundary components or the same component.

arxiv:2610.41237.title: Odd-Degree Rigidity and a Numerical Characterization of Complete Flag Varieties
arxiv:2610.41237.summary: Let $F=G/B$ be the complete flag variety of a connected semisimple complex linear algebraic group. We prove that if a smooth Fano variety $X$ has the same dimension and Picard number as $F$, then the existence of a continuous map $X\to F$ of odd topological degree implies $X$ is isomorphic to $F$. In particular, a smooth Fano variety homotopy equivalent to $F$ is isomorphic to $F$.

arxiv:2610.41243.title: Generative SDEs with Trainable Diffusion and Density-Based Losses
arxiv:2610.41243.summary: We develop a divergence-kernel method for jointly optimizing neural SDE drift and diffusion fields and the initial Gaussian distribution, using losses that depend directly on the terminal density. In two- and eight-dimensional Gaussian-mixture experiments, we learn time-independent fields and obtain far fewer off-mode samples than score-based generators with similar parameter counts. The drift attracts samples toward the modes, while the diffusion helps disperse excess probability between them.

arxiv:2610.41266.title: A note on decompositions into 3-chromatic graphs
arxiv:2610.41266.summary: Delcourt and Postle recently introduced the `discharging in the dual' proof technique, leading to a breakthrough proof of Nash-Williams' conjecture on triangle decompositions. Independently, and almost simultaneously, the first and second authors built on the `condensation' method of Bryant, Dukes, Horsley, Maenhaut and Montgomery to determine the decomposition threshold of all odd cycles of length at least $73$. In this note, we explain how the `discharging in the dual' and `condensation' methods can be combined to determine the decomposition threshold of cycles of any odd length, as well as the approximate decomposition threshold of a range of other $3$-chromatic graphs.
arxiv:2610.41266.authors: Bertille Granet, Daniel Horsley, Jeffrey N. Santrio

arxiv:2610.41286.title: On the Tur\'an number for the Cartesian product of an odd cycle and a tree
arxiv:2610.41286.summary: Let $T$ be a fixed tree on at least two vertices. We determine the Tur\'an number and all extremal graphs for the Cartesian product of an odd cycle $C_{2m+1}$ and $T$, for every fixed integer $m\ge1$ and all sufficiently large $n$, in terms of its decomposition family. Every extremal graph is the join of an independent set and an extremal graph for that family.
arxiv:2610.41286.authors: Ya-Hong Chen, Yong Lu, Quan Sun, Qi Wu, Long-Tu Yuan

arxiv:2610.41287.title: Semipositivity and complete subvarieties of projectivised strata of holomorphic differentials
arxiv:2610.41287.summary: We show that if the projectivised stratum $\mathbb{P}{H}_g(\mu)$ associated to a partition $\mu=(m_1,\ldots,m_n)$ of $2g-2$ contains a complete curve, then \[ \kappa_\mu:=\sum_{i=1}^n\frac{m_i(m_i+2)}{m_i+1}>12. \] The weak inequality follows from semipositivity applied to a quotient of the Hodge bundle, while equality is excluded using the second Fujita decomposition and the geometry of fibred surfaces with maximal unitary rank. Consequently, no projectivised holomorphic stratum in genus $g\leq5$ contains a positive-dimensional complete subvariety.

arxiv:2610.41306.title: Pebbling Numbers and Generator Reinforcement of Cayley Graphs
arxiv:2610.41306.summary: We study inverse-closed generator additions of minimum size that make the optimal pebbling number of a finite Cayley graph at most three while preserving its specified regular action. A weighted vertex-cover formulation on inverse orbits yields an $O(|\Gamma|^2)$ algorithm for abelian groups in the explicit multiplication-table model. We derive formulas for central involutions and cubelike graphs, with an inverse-closure correction determined by square roots in the uncovered set.
arxiv:2610.41306.authors: Yuan Yang, Bocheng Li, Qingzhong Ji

arxiv:2610.41312.title: A Model for Fast Mining Blockchains
arxiv:2610.41312.summary: We study a Markovian model for a blockchain mining process. In the limit where there is an infinite number of miners, the model satisfies a functional law of large numbers due to Barbour and Luczac (2008), leading to an infinite set of coupled ODEs characterising the blockchain heights. We show that the sequence of solutions to this system converges uniformly, to a limiting profile in an appropriate comoving frame.
arxiv:2610.41312.authors: Rhys Bowden, Cengiz Gazi, Jan de Gier, Peter Taylor

arxiv:2610.41325.title: A reciprocal Schoenberg inequality and its extensions
arxiv:2610.41325.summary: We study reciprocal moments of the critical points of a polynomial with a simple zero at the origin. A positive similarity transforms a reciprocal derivative companion into a complex symmetric matrix. This gives a short proof of the reciprocal Schoenberg inequality and a refinement for every elementary symmetric function.

arxiv:2610.41340.title: Clique-factors in randomly perturbed hypergraphs
arxiv:2610.41340.summary: In this paper we establish the following result for clique-factors in randomly perturbed hypergraphs when the cliques are large enough. For integers $k \geq 3$ and $t\geq t_0(k)$, we show that for every $\alpha> 0$, there exists $C>0$ such that for sufficiently large $n\in(t+1)\mathbb{N}$, the union of a $k$-uniform hypergraph on $n$ vertices with minimum codegree at least $\alpha n$ and a binomial random $k$-uniform hypergraph $H^{(k)}(n,p)$ with $p\geq Cn^{-{t/\binom{t+1}{k}}}$ on the same vertex set contains a $K_{t+1}^{(k)}$-factor asymptotically almost surely. The bound on $p$ is asymptotically best possible and extends the graph case, resolved by Balogh, Treglown and Wagner.
arxiv:2610.41340.authors: Yulin Chang, Jie Han, Patrick Morris, Lin Sun

arxiv:2610.41344.title: Disconnectedness of stability manifolds and their geometric loci, and separation of braid orbits of semiorthogonal decompositions
arxiv:2610.41344.summary: This paper proves that the Bridgeland stability manifold $\mathrm{Stab}(X)$ has infinitely many connected components for general quintic threefolds, other general complete intersection Calabi--Yau threefolds, certain odd-dimensional Calabi--Yau varieties, and certain rational weak Fano varieties. Moreover, we show that the geometric locus $\mathrm{Stab}^{\mathrm{geo}}(X)$ meets distinct connected components of $\mathrm{Stab}(X)$ for general quintic threefolds and their products with varieties with finite Albanese morphisms, which gives examples in any dimension at least three. For the weak Fano examples, we also construct semiorthogonal decompositions in infinitely many braid group orbits.

arxiv:2610.41353.title: Separating hash families with large universe II
arxiv:2610.41353.summary: For fixed integers $t,k\ge 2$, put $N=(t-1)(k-1)+1$. We prove that the maximum universe size of a $t$-perfect hash family of length $N$ over an alphabet of size $q$ satisfies $ p_t(N,q)\ge q^{k-o(1)}$. Together with monotonicity in the length, this gives a positive answer to a question of Blackburn, Etzion, Stinson and Zaverucha for every choice of feasible parameters.

arxiv:2610.41357.title: Two-coloring the points of a projective plane
arxiv:2610.41357.summary: Let us color the points of a projective plane of odd order $n$ with two colors, say red and blue. Erd\H{o}s asked the question of determining the maximum number of balanced lines (that have the same number of red and blue points). The answer is $n^2$, and in the corresponding trivial coloring the unbalanced lines go through a point.
arxiv:2610.41357.authors: Aart Blokhuis, \'Ad\'am Mark\'o, Tam\'as Sz\H{o}nyi, Zsuzsa Weiner

arxiv:2610.41371.title: $K_r$-Packings in Graphs with $t_{r-1}(n)+k$ Edges
arxiv:2610.41371.summary: Fix an integer $r\ge 3$. Let $K_r$ denote the complete graph on $r$ vertices and $t_{r-1}(n)$ the Tur\'an number for $K_r$. For each integer $k$ satisfying $0\le k \le \binom{n}{2}-t_{r-1}(n)$, $\rev{\phi_r(n,k)}$ denotes the minimum, over all $n$-vertex graphs with $t_{r-1}(n)+k$ edges, of the maximum size of a $K_r$-packing \rev{(a family of edge-disjoint copies of $K_r$)} in the graph.
arxiv:2610.41371.authors: Hanzhi Bai, Fuhong Ma, Jin Yan

arxiv:2610.41372.title: New results on openly disjoint cycles in regular digraphs
arxiv:2610.41372.summary: Given a digraph \(D\), let \(c(D)\) be the largest size of a collection of openly disjoint directed cycles through a common vertex, and let \(c_r\) be the minimum of \(c(D)\) over all \(r\)-regular digraphs \(D\). In 2005, Seymour asked whether every \(r\)-regular digraph satisfies \(c(D)=r\). Mader answered Seymour's problem negatively for every \(r\ge 8\), but conjectured that nevertheless \(\lim_{r\to\infty}c_r=\infty\).
arxiv:2610.41372.authors: Bin Chen, Wenshen Wu, Meishaung Chen

arxiv:2610.41385.title: The lattice of antichains of intervals: Dyck paths, level sets, and sweep dimension
arxiv:2610.41385.summary: The Clarke-Cormack-Burkowski lattice $\mathcal{E}_n$ is the lattice of antichains of intervals of the chain $\{0,1,\dots,n-1\}$, the algebraic structure underlying minimal-interval semantics, a query semantics used in information retrieval. We give an explicit, elementary anti-isomorphism between $\mathcal{E}_n$ minus its top element and the Stanley lattice of Dyck words of semilength $n+1$ (an anti-isomorphism whose existence is implicit in work of Ferrari and Munarini), under which the rank of an antichain is $\binom{n+1}{2}$ minus the area of the associated Dyck word. Hence the rank generating function of $\mathcal{E}_n\setminus\{\top\}$ is the reverse of the Carlitz-Riordan $q$-Catalan…

arxiv:2610.41417.title: IRA Rigidity and boomerang subalgebras of group von Neumann algebras
arxiv:2610.41417.summary: We introduce the notion of Boomerang subalgebras of group von Neumann algebras and study their general properties. We show that every Boomerang subalgebra of $L(\Gamma)$ is the group von Neumann algebra of a Boomerang subgroup when $\Gamma$ is a countable $C^*$-simple acylindrically hyperbolic group or a finite product of such groups. Consequently, every such group is invariant random algebra (IRA) rigid: every IRA arises as the pushforward of an invariant random subgroup (IRS) under the group von Neumann algebra construction.
arxiv:2610.41417.authors: Tattwamasi Amrutam, Yair Glasner, Yair Hartman, Yongle Jiang

arxiv:2610.41468.title: A local-to-global fixed point theorem for $\CAT(0)$ spaces with a uniform elliptic gap
arxiv:2610.41468.summary: A finitely generated group acting locally elliptically on a complete \CAT(0) space of finite geometric dimension fixes a point if distances to elliptic fixed sets are uniformly controlled by displacements. For arbitrary groups, the same hypothesis gives a fixed point in the space or its visual boundary. The proof combines a first-moment random-walk displacement estimate with Izeki's zero-drift theorem.

arxiv:2610.41502.title: Sink polynomials of line graphs and weighted matching polynomials
arxiv:2610.41502.summary: Chromatic quasisymmetric functions and unicellular LLT polynomials give symmetric-function interpretations of graph orientations counted by sinks. For natural unit interval graphs, we prove that the acyclic sink polynomial is real-rooted for every nonnegative ascent weight. Equivalently, the elementary coefficients of the chromatic quasisymmetric function, grouped by partition length, form a real-rooted polynomial.
arxiv:2610.41502.authors: Per Alexandersson, Leonardo Saud Maia Leite

arxiv:2610.41527.title: Composition factor algebras and finite representation type
arxiv:2610.41527.summary: An Artin algebra is called a composition factor algebra if its indecomposable finitely generated modules are determined, up to isomorphism, by their composition factors. We prove that every composition factor algebra is representation-finite. This settles a conjecture of Auslander, Reiten and Smal\o.

arxiv:2610.41529.title: Equivariant Ehrhart series for rational simplices and rational cross-polytopes
arxiv:2610.41529.summary: Equivariant Ehrhart theory was introduced by Stapledon (2011) and has since been extensively studied. A central question is whether the numerator in a certain rational function expression for the equivariant Ehrhart series is both a polynomial and effective. In this paper, we propose a modification of the denominator in the rational function expression for the equivariant Ehrhart series of rational polytopes.

arxiv:2610.41545.title: On $t$-designs supported by self-orthogonal codes
arxiv:2610.41545.summary: We study self-orthogonal $t$-$(v,k,\lambda)$ designs satisfying the condition that the codes generated by the designs are self-orthogonal codes whose codewords of minimum weight $k$ correspond to the blocks. A classification of such designs is given under the conditions that $t\geq \lfloor k/4\rfloor+1\geq2$ and $t \le 11$. This yields a classification of self-orthogonal codes of minimum weight $k$ whose codewords of minimum weight form a $t$-design under the same conditions.

arxiv:2610.41551.title: Composing Double Categories
arxiv:2610.41551.summary: Many kinds of generalised syntax, including internal categories, T-categories or polynomial monads, arise as monads in bicategories of a certain flavour: maps are some kind of span, and composition is some kind of pullback. We explain the pattern behind these similarities: each bicategory is stitched together from two simpler pieces by a distributive law, where the distributivity is governed by pullback. A key novelty is in the kind of distributive law we consider; where Rosebrugh and Wood considered distributive laws between categories, we instead consider pseudo-distributive laws between double categories.

arxiv:2610.41555.title: Haiman's conjecture for n <= 10: Kazhdan-Lusztig positivity of monomial immanants
arxiv:2610.41555.summary: Haiman conjectured that for every partition $\lambda\vdash n$ and every $w\in S_n$ the polynomial $c_{\lambda,w}(q)$, a monomial character of the Hecke algebra evaluated at the Kazhdan-Lusztig basis, has non-negative integer coefficients and is symmetric and unimodal, and he verified this by computer for $n\le7$. We verify it for every $n\le10$. A stability lemma reduces the statement to $n=10$, which we settle by an exact computation that stores only the 1,252,173,030 pairs $(x,w)$ in $S_{10}$ with $x$ maximal in its double coset for the descent sets of $w$, and takes the traces of the standard basis from the class polynomials of Geck and Pfeiffer.

arxiv:2610.41566.title: The coanalyticity of the reduced K-theory on modules over free tensor algebras of dualizable t-categories
arxiv:2610.41566.summary: In this paper, we formulate Land-Tamme's $\boxtimes$-construction and $\odot$-construction for continuous exact monads on dualizable stable $\infty$-categories, and establish the behaviour of localizing invariants on pushouts of left modules over continuous exact monads on dualizable stable $\infty$-categories. Combining the Land-Tamme theory of continuous exact monads with the theory of analytic functors in Goodwillie calculus, we show that the reduced K-theory on modules over free tensor algebras of dualizable t-categories is modified 1-coanalytic or modified 2-coanalytic, depending on the coconnectivity of the base algebras. In particular, this answers Efimov's question concerning…

arxiv:2610.41572.title: Perfect state transfer on unicyclic graphs
arxiv:2610.41572.summary: We characterize adjacency perfect state transfer in connected unicyclic graphs: the transfer vertices are opposite degree-two vertices of a four-cycle, and the two attached trees satisfy a characteristic-polynomial condition. Except for the four-cycle, the transfer pair is unique and the minimum transfer time is $\pi/\sqrt2$. Outside the four-cycle, we obtain sharp lower bounds of $46$ on the order and $10$ on the maximum degree, and classify all examples of maximum degree at most $20$.

arxiv:2610.41573.title: Iterated toric descent obstruction and homogeneous spaces over geometric global fields
arxiv:2610.41573.summary: We study torsors under tori and groups of multiplicative type together with the obstruction they define to the existence of rational points in the setting of geometric global fields. Our methods give two new arithmetic applications: the iterated toric descent obstruction coincides with the toric decent obstruction and the toric obstruction is the only obstruction to the existence of rational points for homogeneous spaces of connected linear groups with either connected or abelian geometric stabilizers. These applications generalize some known results for classical global fields, due to Borovoi, Colliot-Th\'el\`ene, and Sansuc, while exhibiting novel behaviors.

arxiv:2610.41577.title: A Fan-Type Theorem for Hamiltonian Berge Cycles in 3-Uniform Hypergraphs
arxiv:2610.41577.summary: Let $H$ be a simple $3$-uniform hypergraph on $n\ge7$ vertices, and put $\tau_n=\binom{\lfloor(n-1)/2\rfloor}{2}$. We prove that $H$ has a Hamiltonian Berge cycle if its $2$-shadow is $2$-connected, every pair at Berge distance two has an endpoint of hypergraph degree at least $\tau_n+1$, and every pair of codegree one has both endpoints above $\tau_n$. The distance-two threshold is sharp, and the order range cannot be extended to $n=4,5,6$.

arxiv:2610.41578.title: Tropicalization and Polyhedral Completions of Weyl Algebras
arxiv:2610.41578.summary: We construct weighted and polyhedral completions of the Weyl algebra over a complete nonarchimedean field and organize them into a structure sheaf on a polyhedral $G$-site. For discretely valued fields, we prove two-sided flatness for $\Gamma$-rational polyhedral completions, yielding exact base change for finitely generated $D$-modules. For compact integral polyhedra, we also construct finite-type integral models whose special fibers are toric face rings and describe the reduction of Gauss points in terms of toric strata.

arxiv:2610.41581.title: On sparse universally rigid graphs in $\mathbb{R}$
arxiv:2610.41581.summary: A graph is said to be 1-universally rigid if, for any generic realization of its vertices on the real line, the realization cannot be deformed out of the line in any higher-dimensional Euclidean space while preserving all edge lengths. In this paper, we investigate the sparsity of 1-universally rigid graphs in different manners. First, we show that an Erd\H{o}s-R\'enyi random graph $G(n,p)$ is 1-universally rigid with high probability whenever $p \geq C\log n \cdot \log\log n/n$ for some sufficiently large constant $C>0$.
arxiv:2610.41581.authors: Ole Gabsdil, Ezra Hirschi, Julien Portier

arxiv:2610.41587.title: Extended Tropical Characteristic Fibers and Slopes of Binomial D-Modules
arxiv:2610.41587.summary: For a holonomic $D$-module, we consider the extended tropicalization of the reduced $L$-characteristic fiber along the family $L_s=F+(s-1)V_Y$. For $A$-hypergeometric systems, this tropical fiber determines the complete $(A,L)$-umbrella and hence recovers the classical slopes. We extend this result to holonomic binomial $D$-modules, for which the tropical jump parameters are exactly the classical slopes at the origin.

arxiv:2610.41603.title: Worst-Case Relative Growth of Functionally Generated Portfolios under Restricted Market-Weight Dynamics
arxiv:2610.41603.summary: We study the worst-case relative growth rate of a fixed functionally generated portfolio under restrictions on market-weight dynamics over a compact convex market state space. For a nonempty compact forward shift-invariant path family, the pathwise wealth decomposition identifies the global rate with the minimum invariant average of the one-step $L$-divergence. For paths generated by a compact one-step transition relation, this rate is also the minimum over balanced transition measures, and a minimizing measure can be chosen on one relation basic set.

arxiv:2610.41605.title: Restricted conformal blocks and the braiding on Zhu algebra modules
arxiv:2610.41605.summary: Let $V$ be a vertex operator algebra (VOA), not necessarily rational or $C_2$-cofinite, such that the category $\mathcal C_1(V)$ of $C_1$-cofinite grading-restricted generalized $V$-modules is semisimple and contains the generalized Verma modules associated to finite-dimensional modules over the Zhu algebra $A(V)$. Such VOAs include affine VOAs at admissible and generic levels. We prove that the bottom degree of Huang-Lepowsky's $P(w)$-tensor product module $M^1\boxtimes_{P(w)}M^2$ is isomorphic to the left $A(V)$-module $M^1\odot_{w,0}M^2$ arising from the restricted conformal blocks on $(\P^1,\infty,w,0)$.

arxiv:2610.41620.title: List 3-Coloring in tame classes of graphs in quasipolynomial time
arxiv:2610.41620.summary: A class of graphs $\mathcal{G}$ is tame if there is a constant c such that every $n$-vertex graph in $\mathcal{G}$ has at most $n^c$ minimal separators. Many important graph classes are tame, including chordal graphs, permutation graphs, and circle graphs. Several fundamental problems, most notably Max Weight Independent Set, can be solved in polynomial time on every tame class, which explains in a unified way their tractability on all these classes.

arxiv:2610.41631.title: Numerical Kawamata--Viehweg vanishing for rank-three matroids
arxiv:2610.41631.summary: We prove the numerical Kawamata--Viehweg conjecture for every matroid of rank three: the Euler characteristic of the inverse of an integral big and nef line bundle class is nonnegative. The proof reduces the conjecture to an inequality for a stone game.

arxiv:2610.41668.title: Proper conflict-free degree-choosability of graphs with maximum average degree less than $8/3$
arxiv:2610.41668.summary: A proper coloring $\varphi$ of a graph $G$ is called proper conflict-free if, for every non-isolated vertex $v$, some color appears exactly once in its open neighborhood $N_G(v)$. For a nonnegative integer $k$, a graph $G$ is proper conflict-free $(\mathrm{degree}+k)$-choosable if, for every list assignment $L$ satisfying $|L(v)|\ge d_G(v)+k$ for each $v\in V(G)$, there exists a proper conflict-free coloring $\varphi$ of $G$ with $\varphi(v)\in L(v)$ for each $v\in V(G)$. We prove that every connected graph other than the $5$-cycle $C_5$ with maximum average degree less than $8/3$ is proper conflict-free $(\mathrm{degree}+2)$-choosable.

arxiv:2610.41703.title: Exchange graphs and $g$-vectors of surface rigid algebras
arxiv:2610.41703.summary: We classify the connected components of support $\tau$-tilting graphs of surface rigid algebras associated with partial tagged triangulations of punctured marked surfaces with nonempty boundary. For a connected algebra, the graph is disconnected if and only if the algebra is weakly symmetric, has at least two simple modules, and has Cartan rank one. In this case, it has exactly two connected components.

arxiv:2610.41716.title: CRCs in four-dimensional lattice graphs
arxiv:2610.41716.summary: We obtain series of new completely regular codes in Cayley graphs of the groups $Z_q^n$ with the Lee metric. Combined with binary linear programming methods, the constructions lead to enumeration of all completely regular codes in such graphs for the groups $Z_q^4$, $q\leq 7$ up to parameter matrices.

arxiv:2610.41719.title: Relative Du Bois complexes over higher dimensional bases
arxiv:2610.41719.summary: We extend the notion of the right relative Du Bois complex to a smooth base of arbitrary dimension. We further show that this complex satisfies base change in the sense of Kov\'acs--Taji, for flat families with strict higher Du Bois fibers, extending the result by Ning over a smooth curve.

arxiv:2610.41725.title: An extension of the classic Buneman theorem from phylogenetic trees to networks
arxiv:2610.41725.summary: Phylogenetic networks provide a natural framework for representing reticulate evolutionary events such as horizontal gene transfer and hybridization. In the present manuscript, we investigate the identifiability of phylogenetic networks under (hardwired) parsimony, a natural extension of Maximum Parsimony from trees to networks. More precisely, we ask which structural features of a network can be uniquely inferred from so-called $A_k$-alignments under this criterion.

arxiv:2610.41727.title: Deformations of Calabi--Yau varieties over transversal or crystalline prisms
arxiv:2610.41727.summary: Recent work of Brantner and Taelman shows that derived deformation theory and period maps can recover strong mixed-characteristic lifting results. In this paper, we develop a prismatic version of this method for Calabi--Yau varieties over transversal or crystalline prisms, constructing compatible deformations over $A/I^n$ for every $n$ under suitable hypotheses. We also apply our method to $F$-split Calabi--Yau varieties over a field $k$ of characteristic $p>2$.

arxiv:2610.41735.title: Maximum edge overlap between independent random regular graphs
arxiv:2610.41735.summary: Optimising the vertex correspondence can substantially increase the number of edges shared by two independent realisations of the same random graph. We quantify this phenomenon for uniformly random $d$-regular graphs and derive corresponding results for their edge-based graph edit distance. For every fixed $d\geq 3$, we show that the maximum overlap is $n+\Theta_{\mathbb P}(n/\log n)$, where the leading term $n$ arises from Hamiltonicity, while the surplus captures the optimal order of the excess beyond it.

arxiv:2610.41737.title: $K$-tropical curves, Riemann-Roch and Serre duality
arxiv:2610.41737.summary: We endow a tropical curve with the structure of a ringed space and establish analogues of Riemann-Roch and Serre duality for these ringed spaces. As a corollary, we give a cohomological proof of the tropical Riemann-Roch theorem.

arxiv:2610.41766.title: An odd version of the Grothendieck--Teichm\"uller Lie algebra and the odd Deligne--Drinfeld conjecture
arxiv:2610.41766.summary: We study an ``odd'' version of the Grothendieck--Teichm\"uller Lie algebra that is obtained by replacing free Lie algebras in even generators by free graded Lie algebras in odd generators in the classical definition. These odd variants are related to the ``odd'' Kontsevich graph complex in the same way as the classical Grothendieck--Teichm\"uller group is related to the even Kontsevich graph complex. We show an odd analog of the Deligne--Drinfeld conjecture, namely that the odd Grothendieck--Teichm\"uller Lie algebra is isomorphic to a free graded Lie algebra in one odd generator of weight 3.

arxiv:2610.41771.title: Bounds on the maximum denominator of fractional chromatic numbers
arxiv:2610.41771.summary: For a positive rational number $x=p/q$, where $p$ and $q$ are coprime positive integers, let $\operatorname{den}(x)=q$. For a positive integer $n$, let $\operatorname{sd}(n)=\max\{\operatorname{den}(\chi_f(G)): |V(G)|=n\}$. Let $D(n)=2^{-n}(n+1)^{(n+1)/2}$.

arxiv:2610.41774.title: Coring morphisms presenting nonaffine noncommutative fibre bundles
arxiv:2610.41774.summary: We consider noncommutative analogues of associated fibre bundles where the total space, base space and even the fiber may be nonaffine, that is, not represented by a single algebra, and where the structure group is replaced by a Hopf algebra $H$. We choose to describe gluing of affine pieces by corings. In the role of a principal bundle we take an internal $E$-coring $M$ in the monoidal category of right $H$-comodules where $E$ is a faithfully flat right Hopf-Galois extension.

arxiv:2610.41787.title: Ore-degree conditions for hypergraph matchings
arxiv:2610.41787.summary: Let $\sigma_k(H)$ be the minimum sum of the vertex degrees over all non-edges of an $n$-vertex $k$-uniform hypergraph $H$. For every $k\ge3$, $n\geq ks$ and sufficiently large $n$, we establish a sharp Ore-type degree condition that forces a matching of size $s$ in $H$. Specifically, we prove that if \[ \sigma_k(H)>\max\left\{ k\left(\binom{n-1}{k-1}-\binom{n-s}{k-1}\right), (k-c)\binom{ks-2}{k-1}\right\}, \] then $H$ has a matching of size $s$, where $c=n-ks+1$.
arxiv:2610.41787.authors: Mingyang Guo, Tianhong Kan, Hongliang Lu, Feihong Yuan

arxiv:2610.41794.title: A note on surjective endomorphisms of Smale spaces
arxiv:2610.41794.summary: We give conditions that are all equivalent to surjectivity for endomorphisms of irreducible Smale spaces. This extends results previously obtained by Hedlund~\cite{hedlund-endomorphisms} for full shifts, by Coven and Paul and by Lind and Marcus for irreducible subshifts of finite type.

arxiv:2610.41802.title: Bethe Hessian Recovery through the Kesten-Stigum Regime
arxiv:2610.41802.summary: We show that outlier eigenvectors of the Bethe Hessian achieve weak recovery in the stochastic block model down to the Kesten-Stigum threshold, for every fixed common expected degree $d>1$. This extends previous recovery guarantees, which required $d$ to be sufficiently large. This threshold is information-theoretically optimal for the symmetric two-community model and is conjectured to mark the limit of efficient recovery in broader symmetric models.

arxiv:2610.41811.title: Coxeter Rigidity and ADE Classification of Fibonacci-Generated Tensor Categories
arxiv:2610.41811.summary: We propose a program to classify tensor categories generated by prescribed seed tensor categories.
