We carry out this program for finitely many marked copies of the positive Fibonacci category with pairwise nonisomorphic generating simple objects, in the setting of split locally finite semisimple rigid $\CC$-linear tensor categories with simple unit. We show that the Fibonacci fusion relation forces the fusion rules to be those of a specialized Coxeter--Hecke ring.

arxiv:2610.41820.title: The Alon-Tarsi number of 4-regular circulant graphs
arxiv:2610.41820.summary: This paper studies the Alon-Tarsi number of connected $4$-regular circulant graphs $C_n(s,t)$, where $1\le s<t<n/2$. We prove that if $n=\ell p^r$, where $p$ is an odd prime, $r\ge 1$, and $t\equiv\pm s\pmod{\ell}$, then $\operatorname{AT}(C_n(s,t))=3$ if $\ell$ is even, or if $\ell\ge 3$ is odd and $p\nmid 2^\ell-2$. We also prove that $\operatorname{AT}(C_{6m}(2,3))=3$ for $m\ge 2$, and $\operatorname{AT}(C_n(1,3))=3$ for $n\ge 8$.

arxiv:2610.41840.title: Revisiting the directed pathwidth of h-semicomplete digraphs
arxiv:2610.41840.summary: A digraph is $h$-semicomplete if every vertex has at most $h$ non-neighbors. In semicomplete digraphs, $k$-triples are obstructions to bounded directed pathwidth with many algorithmic applications: Fradkin and Seymour [JCTB 2013] showed that a large triple contains a subdivision of every small digraph, and triples were used for irrelevant vertex arguments in routing problems by Fomin and Pilipczuk [JCTB 2019] and Gomes, Lopes, and Sau [ICALP 2025]. Fradkin and Seymour also showed that there is a function $f(k)$ such that every semicomplete digraph of directed pathwidth at least $f(k)$ contains a $k$-triple, and their proof gives $f(k)$ triply exponential in $k$.
arxiv:2610.41840.authors: Guilherme C. M. Gomes, Raul Lopes, Matthias Mnich

arxiv:2610.41891.title: Finite Composites of the Fibonacci Category with Pointed Fusion Categories
arxiv:2610.41891.summary: We classify finite composites of the positive Fibonacci category with arbitrary pointed fusion categories, retaining the entire source functor and making no unitarity assumption on the target. Formal codegrees, dimension fields, and algebraic integrality exclude all dihedral Fibonacci rings $R_n$ with $n\ge4$ from categorification. Together with an independent graphical uniqueness argument, this gives the finite two-Fibonacci classification.

arxiv:2610.41904.title: Lax-idempotent monads in homotopy theory
arxiv:2610.41904.summary: We extend the theory of lax-idempotent monads to the setting of $(\infty,2)$-categories. In particular, we prove an analogue of Kock and Z\"oberlein's characterization of the category of algebras over a lax-idempotent monad. We then apply this theory to many examples that arise naturally in homotopy theory.

arxiv:2610.41929.title: Alcove walks, crystal structure and a Levi branching rule
arxiv:2610.41929.summary: In the Borel case $P=B$, we endow Haines' set of maximal-dimensional positively folded alcove walks (arXiv:2405.17174) with a crystal structure. We construct a bijection with the LS-gallery model of Gaussent and Littelmann (arXiv:math/0307122) and prove that it intertwines the root operators. This answers a question raised by Haines.

arxiv:2610.41930.title: Nonequilibrium Transient Centers in Continuous-Time Systems
arxiv:2610.41930.summary: Analysis of mathematical models in ecology and epidemiology often emphasizes asymptotic dynamics, such as stable equilibria, periodic orbits, and attractors. However, many biologically relevant trajectories exhibit long transient dynamics in which a relevant observable evolves slowly for an extended period before a comparatively rapid transition occurs. On finite time scales relevant to data collection, management, and intervention, such transient behavior can be more informative than the eventual asymptotic outcome.

arxiv:2610.41931.title: A Tropical Viewpoint on the Nagata--Biran--Szemberg Conjecture
arxiv:2610.41931.summary: We give a tropical perspective on the recent arguments announced by OpenAI for Nagata's conjecture and the Nagata--Biran--Szemberg conjecture. By degenerating to both the normal cone and a semistable model whose dual graph is a cycle, we replace sections on a surface by Laurent polynomials in two variables. In place of theta functions, tropical methods bound the exponents of these Laurent polynomials, and a lift of the tropical Abel--Jacobi class of the normal bundle controls the shape of the resulting exponent diagram.

arxiv:2610.41941.title: Type classifiers
arxiv:2610.41941.summary: We extend dependent type theory by type classifiers and construct an interpretation in the category of contextual categories with families. Type classifiers extend contexts by type variables, complementing the usual context extensions by term variables of specified types. This allows statements with arbitrary type parameters to be formulated without assuming a universe.

arxiv:2610.41950.title: Strong edge-colourings of truncations of cubic graphs
arxiv:2610.41950.summary: We study a problem posed by Kardo\v{s} asking whether the truncation of every connected simple bridgeless cubic graph has strong chromatic index six. The truncation $T(G)$ is obtained by replacing each vertex of $G$ with a triangle and attaching its incident edges to distinct vertices of that triangle. An affirmative answer was previously established for prism bases by Han and Cui.

arxiv:2610.41954.title: The metric Zariski multiplicity conjecture in dimension 4
arxiv:2610.41954.summary: Recently, OpenAI announced a counterexample to the Zariski multiplicity conjecture in dimension 4. Here, we prove that the metric Zariski multiplicity conjecture is true in dimension 4. More precisely, let $f,g\colon(\mathbb{C}^n,0)\to(\mathbb{C},0)$ be germs of reduced holomorphic functions, and let $\varphi\colon(\mathbb{C}^n,0)\to(\mathbb{C}^n,0)$ be a bi-Lipschitz homeomorphism such that $\varphi(V(f))=V(g)$.

arxiv:2610.41971.title: The 3-Color 2-Chromatic Gallai-Ramsey Number for Complete Graphs
arxiv:2610.41971.summary: For $1\le i\le j\le k$, let $gr^3_2(K_i, K_j, K_k)$ be the least $n\in \mathbb{N}$ such that every rainbow triangle-free $3$-coloring of $K_n$ (using red, blue, and green) contains a red/blue $K_i$, a red/green $K_j$, or a blue/green $K_k$. In this paper, we completely evaluate $gr^3_2(K_i, K_j, K_k)$ for all values of $i$, $j$, and $k$ in which $r(K_i,K_j)$ is known.

arxiv:2610.41973.title: Limit theorems for cuspidal orbits on Fuchsian groups
arxiv:2610.41973.summary: Let $\Gamma\subset \operatorname{SL}(2, \mathbb{R})$ be discrete, co-finite with cusps, and let ${\frak b}\in \mathbb{R}\cup\{\infty\}$ be a cusp of $\Gamma$. Let $f: \Gamma{\frak b} \to \mathbb{R}$ be a quantum modular form in the sense that the maps $$ \phi_\gamma(x) = f(x) - f(\gamma x) \qquad (x\in \Gamma{\frak b}, \gamma \in \Gamma) $$ extend to H\"older-regular functions. Under bounded moments assumptions of the shape $\sum_n n^{-2} \int |\phi_{\gamma^n}(x)|^\alpha d x < \infty$ for some $\alpha>0$ and every fixed parabolic element $\gamma\in \Gamma$, we prove asymptotic formulas for the characteristic functions of the values $f(x)$ for $x\in \Gamma{\frak b}$, ordered by growing…
arxiv:2610.41973.authors: Sandro Bettin, Sary Drappeau, Jungwon Lee

arxiv:2610.41977.title: Hedetniemi's conjecture for Shannon OR-capacity: counterexamples and asymptotic separation
arxiv:2610.41977.summary: We disprove the analogue of Hedetniemi's conjecture for Shannon OR-capacity, which asserts that the capacity of a categorical product equals the smaller capacity of its factors. For every sufficiently large complete graph, we construct a second graph of larger capacity such that their categorical product has capacity strictly below that of the complete graph. Further constructions show that, for every real threshold above an explicit constant, both factor capacities can exceed that threshold while the product capacity lies below it.

arxiv:2610.41984.title: Hilton-Zhao vertex-splitting conjecture for triangle-free graphs
arxiv:2610.41984.summary: Every graph obtained from a regular Class $1$ graph by a vertex-splitting is overfull and hence is of Class $2$; the central question is whether the resulting graph is edge-chromatic critical. We consider a revised version of the Hilton-Zhao vertex-splitting conjecture for triangle-free base graphs, excluding the known cubic exception that arises from the Wagner graph. Let $G$ be a connected $n$-vertex triangle-free $\Delta$-regular Class $1$ graph, and let $G^{*}$ be obtained from $G$ by splitting one vertex into two adjacent vertices.
arxiv:2610.41984.authors: Xuli Qi, Xin Tian, Gregory Gutin

arxiv:2610.41985.title: Suspense and surprise in matroid bingo
arxiv:2610.41985.summary: We present the game of Matroid Bingo and prove that it gets more suspenseful the longer the game goes on.

arxiv:2610.41996.title: Rationally slice knots that are not biprojectively H-slice
arxiv:2610.41996.summary: We show that rationally slice knots need not be biprojectively H-slice (BPH-slice), answering a question in the study of the rational knot concordance group. Our main tool is a lattice embedding obstruction to H-sliceness in $\#^n\mathbb{CP}^2$ for knots with vanishing signature, extending work of Kjuchukova--Miller--Ray--Sakall{\i}. We apply the obstruction to an infinite family of rationally slice knots, beginning with $8_{18}$.

arxiv:2610.41999.title: Ramsey numbers $R(K_{1,4},K_{m,n})$ for small $m$
arxiv:2610.41999.summary: We determine all currently unknown values of the generalized two-color Ramsey number $R(K_{1,4},K_{m,n})$ for $\min(m,n) \leq 8$. We also prove that the number $R(K_{1,4},K_{m,m})$ equals $26, 29, 31, 33$ for $m = 9, 10, 11, 12$ respectively.

arxiv:2610.42005.title: Tiling without a subspace complement: a sharp counterexample in dimension nine over the field with two elements
arxiv:2610.42005.summary: We construct an explicit 64-point subset of $\mathbb F_2^9$ which tiles by translation but has no linear-subspace tiling complement. Together with our earlier dimension-eight theorem and a product argument, this shows that every nonempty tile in $\mathbb F_2^d$ has a linear-subspace complement precisely when $d\le8$. The example is spectral, so it is not a counterexample to Fuglede's conjecture.

arxiv:2610.42006.title: Extremal character spectra of finite projective systems
arxiv:2610.42006.summary: Let $\mathcal M$ be a finite spanning multiset of points in ${\rm PG}(k-1,q)$, and let ${\rm Char}_{\mathcal M}$ be its character function. For $1\le r\le k$, we study the maximum number of distinct values attained by ${\rm Char}_{\mathcal M}$ on the codimension-$r$ flats under a total-multiplicity budget. The spectrum is subject to two natural upper bounds, whose extremal cases lead respectively to $r$-maximum character spectrum ($r$-MCS) and $r$-full character spectrum ($r$-FCS) systems.
arxiv:2610.42006.authors: Shitao Li, Yang Li, Gaojun Luo

arxiv:2610.42019.title: Modulo k-orientations of highly edge-connected signed graphs
arxiv:2610.42019.summary: A modulo $k$-orientation of a signed graph is an orientation in which the outdegree and indegree are congruent modulo $k$ at every vertex. We show that, for every odd integer $k\ge3$, every essentially $k$-unbalanced $(6k-10)$-edge-connected signed graph admits a modulo $k$-orientation. This improves the edge-connectivity bound of Zhu [JCTB, 112 (2015)] from $6k-7$ to $6k-10$.
arxiv:2610.42019.authors: You Lu, Zhengke Miao, Zhenyu Tian, Cun-Quan Zhang

arxiv:2610.42022.title: Spectral Beurling-Selberg Approximation and Applications to Effective Motivic Chebotarev-Sato-Tate Estimates
arxiv:2610.42022.summary: We establish a spectral Beurling-Selberg approximation theorem on compact connected Riemannian manifolds for sets whose boundaries have finite upper Minkowski content. Our majorants and minorants have controlled spectral coefficients and explicit stability under Hausdorff perturbations, uniformly over families satisfying a common Minkowski content bound. We extend the construction to singular spaces arising from Riemannian submetries with basic mean curvature, and apply it to equidistribution on quaternionic Shimura varieties.

arxiv:2610.42033.title: Treedepth is NP-Hard on Planar Graphs of Maximum Degree 3
arxiv:2610.42033.summary: Treedepth is an important parameter in algorithmic graph theory. It is known that the problem of computing the treedepth of a graph is NP-hard. It has been an open problem whether treedepth can be computed in polynomial time when the input graph is restricted to be planar, or of bounded degree.

arxiv:2610.42038.title: Berenstein-Zelevinsky polytopes for type $\mathrm{G}_{2}$
arxiv:2610.42038.summary: In 2001, Berenstein and Zelevinsky presented a polyhedral model for the problem of computing tensor-product multiplicities for semi\-simple Lie algebras. We provide explicit linear equations and inequalities for Berenstein--Zelevinsky (BZ) polytopes of type-$\mathrm{G}_{2}$ Lie algebras. We prove that the denominator of a type-$\mathrm{G}_{2}$ BZ~polytope divides $180$, and that this bound is sharp, while the quasi-period of the Ehrhart quasipolynomial of such a polytope is always a divisor of $6$.

arxiv:2610.42045.title: Motivic invariants of birational hyper-K\"ahler manifolds
arxiv:2610.42045.summary: We prove that birational projective irreducible holomorphic symplectic manifolds have equivalent integral cohomological motives as commutative algebra objects in $\mathrm{SH}(\mathbb C)$. Consequently, their algebraic K-theory spectra are equivalent as $E_\infty$-algebras, and their integral graded K-theory rings are isomorphic.

arxiv:2610.42067.title: Two choices suffice: $k$-out sampling leaves $O(n/k)$ intercomponent edges for $k\geq 2$
arxiv:2610.42067.summary: Given a simple undirected graph on $n$ vertices, random $k$-out sampling forms a spanning subgraph by having each vertex independently choose $k$ incident edges uniformly with replacement. We prove that, for every integer $k\geq2$, the expected number of original edges joining distinct sampled components is $O(n/k)$. This resolves the conjecture of Holm, King, Thorup, Zamir, and Zwick in its full range, improving their logarithmic sampling requirement to the optimal threshold of two choices per vertex.

arxiv:2610.42076.title: Constructing Lagrangian surfaces in all symplectic toric $4$-manifolds from multi-grid diagrams
arxiv:2610.42076.summary: We present a new diagrammatic construction of Lagrangian surfaces in all symplectic toric $4$-manifolds from objects called multi-grid diagrams. These are a generalisation of triple grid diagrams for Lagrangian surfaces in $\mathbb{CP}^2$ wherein the underlying trisection is replaced by the more general notion of a toric decomposition. We give examples of multi-grid diagrams for Lagrangian surfaces in a range of symplectic toric $4$-manifolds, including Evans' recent non-squeezable Klein bottle in $S^2 \times S^2$.

arxiv:2610.42077.title: Polynomial-Time Algorithms for Links
arxiv:2610.42077.summary: Every link in the \(3\)-sphere admits a generalised \(T\)-link presentation. In this paper, we give an explicit polynomial-time algorithm which, given a signed Artin braid word and the number of strands, computes such a presentation. Combining this construction with Yamada--Vogel braiding gives a polynomial-time conversion from arbitrary oriented combinatorial link diagrams to generalised \(T\)-link parameters.

arxiv:2610.42079.title: Holonomies of hyperbolic surfaces with one branch point
arxiv:2610.42079.summary: Let $S$ be a closed oriented surface of genus $g\geq 2$. We prove that any representation of $\pi_1(S)$ into $\mathrm{PSL}(2,\mathbb{R})$ with Euler class $3-2g$ is the holonomy of a hyperbolic metric on $S$ with one simple branch point.

arxiv:2610.42083.title: Long-time stochasticity for periodic iterations of random surface maps
arxiv:2610.42083.summary: Let $M$ be a closed Riemannian surface, and let $f_1,\ldots,f_s$ be area-preserving $C^2$ diffeomorphisms with fixed positive probabilities such that the resulting random dynamical system is uniformly expanding on average. For each $n$, choose $\omega_1,\ldots,\omega_n$ independently according to these probabilities and set $F=f_{\omega_n}\circ\cdots\circ f_{\omega_1}$. We prove that there exists $\alpha>0$ such that, with probability at least $1-e^{-\alpha n}$, the correlations of any two H\"older observables $\phi,\psi$ under $F^m$ are bounded by $e^{-\alpha n}\|\phi\|_{C^\beta}\|\psi\|_{C^\beta}$, for all $m\leq e^{\alpha n}$.
arxiv:2610.42083.authors: Dmitry Dolgopyat, Bassam Fayad, Alexey Okunev

arxiv:2610.42088.title: Delocalized region of bipartite Erd\H{o}s-R\'enyi graphs
arxiv:2610.42088.summary: We consider bipartite Erd\H{o}s-R\'enyi graphs $\mathbb{G}(n, p, d/\sqrt{np})$ with two parts of sizes $n$ and $p$, respectively, and edge probability $d/\sqrt{pn}$. We show that for $d > b_* \log (n+p)$ all eigenvectors of its adjacency matrix, with eigenvalues away from zero, are delocalized with high probability. The threshold $b_*$ is an explicit function of the size ratio $n/p$ and optimal for eigenvector delocalization near the spectral edges.

arxiv:2610.42090.title: Landscape Intervals: A Geometric Framework for Multiparameter Persistence Landscapes
arxiv:2610.42090.summary: Classical persistent homology provides a summary of the multiscale topology of a filtration of a space. These summaries are not naturally valued in a vector space, limiting their direct use in standard machine learning pipelines. To address this issue, Bubenik introduced persistence landscapes, vector-valued invariants of persistence modules, which operate by conveniently encoding the behavior of rank functions of modules along the parameter axis.
arxiv:2610.42090.authors: Pan Fang, Washington Mio, Tom Needham

arxiv:2610.42094.title: A Counterexample to the Alon-Krivelevich Conjecture and a New Lower Bound for Choosability of Bipartite Graphs
arxiv:2610.42094.summary: For an integer $k\ge 2$ and $r^2>2(2k-1)\ln (2k-1)$, we construct a bipartite graph $G$ whose two vertex classes are disjoint copies of the family of all $k$-subsets of a $(2k-1)$-element set, two vertices being adjacent when their sets intersect in at most $r$ elements. Assigning each vertex its corresponding subset as its color list, $G$ is not colorable, and thus its choice number $\ch(G)\ge k+1$. This implies that there are graphs with maximum degree $\Delta$ and $$\ch(G)\ge\Bigl(\frac1{32}-o(1)\Bigr)\frac{(\ln\Delta)^2}{(\ln\ln\Delta)^3}.$$ When $k\to\infty$, consequently $\ch(G)/\ln\Delta$ tends to infinity, which disproves the Alon--Krivelevich conjecture.

arxiv:2610.42099.title: On nowhere-zero ${3}$-flows in Cayley graphs on groups of order ${p^2n}$
arxiv:2610.42099.summary: We consider Tutte's $3$-flow conjecture in the class of Cayley graphs on groups $G$ of order $p^2n$, where $p$ is a prime and $n$ is square-free and coprime to $p$. The conjecture has been proved by J. Zhang and Z.

arxiv:2610.42107.title: Band Random Graphs: Connectivity, Geometry, and Transport
arxiv:2610.42107.summary: Let $G(n,p,m)$ be the random subgraph of the cycle power $C_n^m$ obtained by retaining each edge independently with probability $p$. We study connectivity, component geometry, and random walks throughout the regime $\log n\ll m<n/2$. We prove that $p\sim(\log n)/(2m)$ is a sharp threshold for connectivity.
arxiv:2610.42107.authors: Shantanav Chakraborty, Kyle Luh, Rudransh Pratap Singh

arxiv:2610.42110.title: Grassmannians of absolute Banach-Colmez Spaces
arxiv:2610.42110.summary: We introduce Grassmannians of absolute Banach--Colmez spaces and prove the $k$-Grassmannian is perfectoid if and only if the space has slope $< 1/k$. For $d=1$, this proves a conjecture of Hansen--Mann. The key ingredient is a Pl\"{u}cker morphism, which realizes the $k$-Grassmannian of a slope $d/n$ space as a Zariski closed subspace of the projectivization of a slope $kd/n$ space.

arxiv:2610.42123.title: Abelianization and moment maps
arxiv:2610.42123.summary: When $X_G=\mathbb{C}^n/\!/G$ is a GIT quotient of a vector space, replacing $G$ with a maximal torus $T \subset G$ produces a closely related toric variety $X_T:=\mathbb{C}^N/\!/T$, the \emph{Abelianization} of $X_G$. Abelian/non-Abelian correspondences connect structures on $X_G$ with structures on $X_T$. In this paper, we study the interaction between the toric moment map $\mu$ of $X_T$ and $X_G$, when $X_G=\mathrm{Gr}(r,n)$.
arxiv:2610.42123.authors: Elana Kalashnikov, Ruxandra Moraru, Francisco Villacis

arxiv:2610.42134.title: Baker--Akhiezer sections from Higgs bundles and Landau levels in hyperbolic band theory
arxiv:2610.42134.summary: As observed by Kienzle and the second author, rank-two $\mathcal{O}(3)$-twisted Higgs bundles on the projective line encode all hyperbolic crystals of genus two: the spectral curves are the unit cells, and the Hitchin fibers are the abelian Brillouin zones. In a uniform magnetic field of two flux quanta, the lowest Landau level is one-dimensional at every nonzero momentum, and, as found by Iengo and Li, its dimension jumps to two at the zero momentum. We identify the states of the lowest Landau level with the Baker--Akhiezer sections of the Higgs bundles, and their zeros, the vortices, with the Baker--Akhiezer divisors.

arxiv:2611.00068.title: Univalent Non-Associative Categorical Structures
arxiv:2611.00068.summary: We study category-like structures in which composition is not associative, especially Munch-Maccagnoni's duploids, in univalent foundations. Included is a definition of what a univalent duploid is: one where isomorphisms of a suitable kind render the objects indistinguishable to the type theory. We show that the existing construction of a duploid from an adjunction is not univalent as a "single-sorted" duploid, and provide a novel construction which is.

arxiv:2611.00070.title: The covering radius of RM(1,9) is precisely 242
arxiv:2611.00070.summary: Let $\text{RM}(r,n)$ be the $r$th order Reed-Mullet code of length $2^n$, and let $\rho(r,n)$ denote its covering radius. It is known that $242\le\rho(1,9)\le 244$, and the determination of $\rho(1,9)$ is a long-standing open question. We give a computer-assisted proof that $\rho(1,9)=242$, leveraging the classification of the $349$ orbits in $\text{RM}(3,9)/\text{RM}(2,9)$ under $\text{GL}(9,2)$ [1,3].
arxiv:2611.00070.authors: Xiang-Dong Hou, Evelyn Sabo, Freeman Slaughter

arxiv:2611.00094.title: Combinatorial Algorithms for Partial Inverse Min-Max Spanning Tree Problem under the Weighted Sum Hamming Distance
arxiv:2611.00094.summary: Given a connected weighted graph G=(V, E, w) and a forest F of G, the goal of partial inverse min-max spanning tree problem is to change the weight function as little as possible, so that there is a min-max spanning tree with respect to the new weight function containing F. In this paper, we study this problem under the weighted sum Hamming distance. We take the alternative set of the maximum edge weight in F with respect to the optimal weight function as a key factor, and further consider the case of this problem under the restriction of this factor.
arxiv:2611.00094.authors: Qingzhen Dong, Xianyue Li, Xiaowen Kong

arxiv:2611.00098.title: Comments on "Multidimensional Costas Arrays and Their Periodicity"
arxiv:2611.00098.summary: Rubio and Torres conjectured that a multidimensional Costas array, defined by a bijection between two boxes of integer points whose domain has at least as many dimensions as its image, can stay Costas in every window of its periodic extension only if its order is a power of two fixed by the dimension of the domain. We give a four-dimensional periodic Costas array of order $6$, with a two-dimensional domain and a two-dimensional image, so the conjecture is false. The verification reduces to $36$ windows.

arxiv:2611.00100.title: The optimal four-dimensional lattice quantizer and bounds from Voronoi facets
arxiv:2611.00100.summary: We prove that the root lattice $D_4$ uniquely minimizes the normalized second moment among four-dimensional lattices, up to similarity. The computer-assisted proof combines the classification of secondary cones with integration over Voronoi cells and weighted sums of squares. In dimensions at least two, comparison with circular cones gives a lower bound in terms of the number of Voronoi facets, improving the sphere bound and recovering the hexagonal value in dimension two.

arxiv:2611.00118.title: On the second smallest ideal right-angled hyperbolic four-polytope
arxiv:2611.00118.summary: The regular ideal right-angled 24-cell has volume $4 \pi^2/3$ and is the unique minimum-volume entirely ideal right-angled hyperbolic four-polytope. We prove that the next distinct volume is $8 \pi^2/3$ and that its unique equality case is the reflection double of the 24-cell across one octahedral facet. We also show that an entirely ideal right-angled four-polytope whose facets are regular ideal octahedra or their doubles across triangular faces decomposes into a chain of regular 24-cells, with opposite cutting facets in each intermediate cell.

arxiv:2611.00126.title: Graphs with three distinct distance eigenvalues, one of which is zero
arxiv:2611.00126.summary: Koolen, Hayat and Iqbal asked for the connected graphs whose distance matrix has exactly three distinct eigenvalues, the middle one being $0$. The examples they gave, namely the Johnson graphs, the Hamming graphs and the halved cubes, are distance-regular. In this note, we show that the distance spectrum of such a graph is $\{\rho,0,-c\}$ with integers $c\ge2$ and $c\mid\rho$.

arxiv:2611.00139.title: Blowdowns along Ricci flow in dimension four
arxiv:2611.00139.summary: We show that the blowdown shrinking Ricci soliton of Feldman, Ilmanen and Knopf is strictly dynamically stable in the following strong local sense: (1) The Ricci flow from every metric on a closed 4-manifold containing a region close to a rescaling of a sufficiently large compact subset of the soliton in either orientation and with controlled geometry elsewhere develops a singularity with unique tangent flow modeled on the soliton. (2) The singular time slice has an isolated conical singularity, and by Gianniotis-Schulze the flow can be continued by blowing down a sphere of self-intersection $\pm1$. (3) On a closed 4-manifold, the set of metrics whose Ricci flows have their first…

arxiv:2611.00142.title: Erratum to "Linear representations of 3-manifold groups over rings"
arxiv:2611.00142.summary: The fundamental groups of compact $3$-manifolds are known to be residually finite. Feng Luo conjectured that a stronger statement is true, by allowing only finite groups of the form $\mathrm{PGL}_2(R),$ where $R$ is a finite commutative ring with identity. In a prior paper, "Linear representations of $3$-manifold groups over rings", we, together with two co-authors, gave an equivalent formulation of Luo's conjecture via faithful representations, investigated variants of the conjecture where the target group is of type $\mathrm{SL}_2, \mathrm{GL}_2, \mathrm{PSL}_2$, or $\mathrm{PGL}_2$ as in the original conjecture, and claimed to provide a $3$-manifold group which violated all four variants…

arxiv:2611.00145.title: Hopf Algebra of Graphs for Operator Splitting Methods
arxiv:2611.00145.summary: Motivated by combinatorial identities arising in the study of operator splitting methods and their description in terms of bipartite rooted trees, we establish a connection between operator splitting methods and the theory of combinatorial Hopf algebras. We show that the inclusion-exclusion expansion of the elementary weight of a rooted tree over its rooted subforests can be interpreted as the antipode of Schmitt's Hopf algebra of graphs. This interpretation recovers known identities for operator splitting and partitioned Runge-Kutta methods from general properties of the antipode.

arxiv:2611.00148.title: The sum of sizes of nontrivial cross-intersecting families
arxiv:2611.00148.summary: Families $\mathcal A_1,\ldots,\mathcal A_m\subseteq\binom{[n]}k$ are cross-intersecting if every member of one family meets every member of each other family. A family is nontrivial if its members have no common element. For $n>2k$ and $m\ge3$, we determine the maximum sum of the sizes of $m$ nonempty, nontrivial cross-intersecting families.

arxiv:2611.00149.title: Large Maximal Intersecting Families with Covering Number Three
arxiv:2611.00149.summary: Let $n>2k$ and $k\ge4$. The largest size of an intersecting family of $k$-subsets of $[n]$ with covering number at least three is \[ g_1(n,k)=\binom{n-1}{k-1}-3\binom{n-k-1}{k-1}+\binom{n-k-2}{k-1}+\binom{n-2k}{k-1}+3, \] attained by a unique family up to isomorphism. We prove that every other maximal intersecting family $\mathcal F$ with covering number three satisfies \[ |\mathcal F|\le M(n,k)=\max\{q(n,k),g_2(n,k)\}, \] where \begin{align*} q(n,k)&=\binom{n-1}{k-1}-3\binom{n-k-1}{k-1}+\binom{n-k-3}{k-1}+\binom{n-2k+1}{k-1}+3,\\ g_2(n,k)&=g_1(n,k)-\binom{n-k-3}{k-3}+1.

arxiv:2611.00156.title: A Counterexample to the Gyarmati-Matolcsi-Ruzsa Conjecture
arxiv:2611.00156.summary: We provide a counterexample to the non-abelian Gyarmati-Matolcsi-Ruzsa conjecture. The construction comes from an equivalent maximal-coupling entropy inequality, for which a counterexample can be found in a lower-dimensional group. We give an explicit cardinality counterexample in $D_4^{14}$, the fourteenth direct power of the dihedral group of order $8$.
arxiv:2611.00156.authors: Chandra Nair, Aref Namayandeh, Zhaobang Zhu

arxiv:2611.00173.title: A new upper bound for $A(19,6,8)$
arxiv:2611.00173.summary: We compute Polak's bound $A_4(19,6,8)$ for binary constant weight codes, obtaining the numerical value $673.04001$. An exact rational certificate gives $A_4(19,6,8)\le 673.0400143064802474039375132665301315202504$, and hence $A(19,6,8)\le 673$. This improves the upper bound $693$ listed in Brouwer's table.

arxiv:2611.00217.title: The Dilate Rollercoaster
arxiv:2611.00217.summary: Given a finite subset $A\subseteq\mathbb{Z}$ and a multiset of non-zero integers $\Lambda=\{\lambda_1, \ldots, \lambda_k\}$, the dilate sum \[\Lambda\cdot A:=\lambda_1\cdot A+\lambda_2\cdot A+\cdots+\lambda_k\cdot A =\{\lambda_1a_1+\cdots+\lambda_ka_k: a_1, \ldots, a_k\in A\}.\] For a non-zero real number $r$, say that $\Lambda_2$ $r$-dominates $\Lambda_1$ if we can partition some of the elements of $\Lambda_2$ into blocks summing to the elements of $r\cdot\Lambda_1$. Then for all finite subsets $A\subseteq\mathbb{Z}$, $\Lambda_2\cdot A$ contains a translate of $r\cdot(\Lambda_1\cdot A)$, and hence $|\Lambda_1\cdot A|\le|\Lambda_2\cdot A|$ for all $A$. In a recent paper, Kravitz…

arxiv:2611.00220.title: Cuspidal sheaves on the stack of L-parameters
arxiv:2611.00220.summary: We introduce the notion of cuspidal coherent sheaves on the moduli stack of local L-parameters. We give a complete classification and relate them to Lusztig's cuspidal local systems (or character sheaves). Under the categorical local Langlands conjecture, these sheaves are expected to correspond to supercuspidal representations supported at basic points.

arxiv:2611.00251.title: Upper bounds for packings of cylinders around the unit sphere
arxiv:2611.00251.summary: In this note we study the problem of packing infinite circular cylinders tangent to the unit sphere. For a given number of cylinders $N$, $N\geq 3$, the maximal common cylinder radius $R_N$ is the maximum $R$ for which there exist $N$ circular cylinders of radius $R$ with non-overlapping interiors, all tangent to the unit sphere. In 1990, Kuperberg conjectured that there does not exist a packing of more than 6 cylinders of radius one tangent to the unit sphere, that is, $R_7<1$.

arxiv:2611.00254.title: Generic Linear Momentum Escape for Twist Maps
arxiv:2611.00254.summary: We prove that linear momentum escape is generic in the $C^{1,\alpha}$ topology for smooth potential perturbations of exact symplectic twist maps, for every $0<\alpha<1$. We assume a $C^2$ generating function, a uniform twist condition, and uniform upper bounds on $D_{11}S$ and $D_{22}S$. For an open dense set of potentials, every sufficiently small momentum drift is realized by an orbit.

arxiv:2611.00257.title: Porosity in Diophantine approximation
arxiv:2611.00257.summary: We provide a general framework for obtaining upper bounds on the packing dimension of certain sets arising from Diophantine approximation using the notion of porosity from geometric measure theory. In particular, the framework relies on showing that such sets are mean porous, as introduced by Koskela and Rohde (Math. Ann., 1997).

arxiv:2611.00258.title: Porteous Meets Walsh: Counting Critical Points for $\mathcal{H}_2$-Norm Model Order Reduction Using Algebraic Geometry Behind Multiparameter Eigenvalue Problems
arxiv:2611.00258.summary: Several polynomial systems arising in systems and control have been shown to exhibit a partially linear structure, which allows them to be reformulated as a multiparameter eigenvalue problem (MEP). In this work, we show how such MEP formulations can be leveraged to obtain refined information about the solution set of the polynomial system. We demonstrate, in the setting of single-input single-output $\mathcal{H}_2$-norm model order reduction, how the Thom--Porteous formula can be used to derive an exact count of the complex solutions of the critical equations derived from Walsh's theorem.
arxiv:2611.00258.authors: Sibren Lagauw, Leonie Kayser, Bart De Moor

arxiv:2611.00261.title: A Directed Cubical Framework for k-critical Bipersistence Modules
arxiv:2611.00261.summary: In topological data analysis, multiparameter persistence modules (MPMs) are used to analyze data with multiple parameters. Summarizing topological information for MPMs is a non-trivial task; one useful summary of bipersistence modules is the fibered barcode \cite{lesnick2015interactive,lesnick2025fast}. In this paper, we use a directed topological construction of the parameter space of a bifiltration to extend the fibered barcode.
arxiv:2611.00261.authors: Robin Belton, Robyn Brooks, Lisbeth Fajstrup, Brittany Terese Fasy, Elizabeth Vidaurre

arxiv:2611.00263.title: Two moments suffice for Bessel approximation: conditioned differences, contingency tables, and probabilistic divide-and-conquer
arxiv:2611.00263.summary: We develop Stein's method, with explicit constants throughout, for the discrete Bessel distribution: the law of a Poisson variable given its difference from an independent Poisson variable. The Bessel family is characterized by a birth-death operator with quadratic death rate $n(n+k)$ and as the exact fixed-point set of a centered quadratic-bias transform, and we prove a dependency expansion of Arratia-Goldstein-Gordon type: two joint moments of a column array control the total-variation distance from the conditioned row sum to a matched Bessel law. Applied to the row-constrained Fisher-Yates ensemble on $2\times c$ contingency tables -- independent Bernoulli or capped-Poisson entries…

arxiv:2611.00270.title: A nonarithmetic lattice from a mirror in the Couwenberg-Heckman-Looijenga construction
arxiv:2611.00270.summary: We prove that the stabilizer of a reflection mirror of the Couwenberg-Heckman-Looijenga lattice $\mathcal{C}(G_{29},3)$ induces a nonarithmetic lattice in $\operatorname{PU}(2,1)$. This lattice is not commensurable with any Deligne-Mostow lattice in $\operatorname{PU}(2,1)$ or any lattice in the twenty-two nonarithmetic classes listed by Deraux, Parker and Paupert.

arxiv:2611.00275.title: Stein's method for negative binomial and hyper-negative-binomial laws, with applications
arxiv:2611.00275.summary: We develop Stein's method for the negative binomial law and for the hyper-negative-binomial law, the law of the smallest row total of an array of independent geometric variables given the differences of the row totals, with every constant explicit. The main instrument is a comparison of two biasings of the approximated variable, which cancels the rate term exactly at the matched parameter. We provide total variation bounds for sums of independent geometric variables at drifting parameters, for sums of dependent geometric variables (the Arratia-Goldstein-Gordon theorem with geometric summands and the Poisson law as an endpoint), and for Poisson mixtures; the exact conditional law of…

arxiv:2611.00285.title: Quantitative spectral rigidity for negatively curved manifolds and Outer Space
arxiv:2611.00285.summary: Let $M$ be a closed manifold with fundamental group $G$. A subset of conjugacy classes $E \subset \text{conj}(G)$ is said to be spectrally rigid if when two negatively curved Riemannian metrics have the same marked length spectra on $E$, then their length spectra agree on all conjugacy classes. In this work we study spectrally rigid subsets from a quantitative perspective.

arxiv:2611.00311.title: On potential density of rational points on hyperkahler varieties
arxiv:2611.00311.summary: In this paper, we prove that the rational points on hyperk\"ahler varieties in each of the four known deformation families admitting a rational Lagrangian fibration are potentially dense. Furthermore, we give several applications and construct examples of hyperk\"ahler varieties beyond these families satisfying the potential density property. Our approach is first to prove that rational points on hyperk\"ahler varieties admitting two rational Lagrangian fibrations with distinct associated isotropic rays are potentially dense.

arxiv:2611.00313.title: Quasi-polynomial valuations of lattice polytopes
arxiv:2611.00313.summary: We prove that for any valuation $\varphi$ of lattice polytopes in ${\mathbb R}^m$, which is quasi-polynomial with respect to ${\mathbb Z}^m$-translations, and any lattice polytope $P$, the function $\varphi(nP)$ is quasi-polynomial in $n$.

arxiv:2611.00315.title: Isomorphism classes and geometric classification of three-dimensional Jordan algebras and the length function
arxiv:2611.00315.summary: We investigate the algebraic classification of Jordan algebras of dimensions at most three over arbitrary fields with more than two elements. Our approach combines the theory of nilalgebras and radicals with Peirce, Wedderburn decompositions and the length function. In characteristic two, we adapt the Peirce decomposition to organize the classification, including the field-dependent isomorphism conditions among parametrized families.
arxiv:2611.00315.authors: Isabel Hernandez, Maria Eugenia Martin, Rodrigo Lucas Rodrigues, Carlos Andre Gomes Silva

arxiv:2611.00321.title: Spherical Schubert varieties in $GL_n / P$
arxiv:2611.00321.summary: Let a general linear group act on a partial flag variety transitively, and consider the induced action of a Levi subgroup $L$. A Schubert variety is $\textit{$L$-spherical}$ if it is stable under the $L$-action and contains a dense open orbit of a Borel subgroup of $L$. It is $\textit{toric}$ if, in addition, $L$ is a torus.

arxiv:2611.00355.title: The recognition problem for 4-manifolds and the unknotting problem for 2-spheres in 4-manifolds
arxiv:2611.00355.summary: We show that there is no algorithm to decide whether or not a given 4-manifold is PL homeomorphic to the connected sum of 7 copies of S 2 x S 2 . We also show that the TOP and PL unknotting problems for all surfaces in the connected sum of 7 copies of S 2 x S 2 are unsolvable.

arxiv:2611.00363.title: Some Constructions in the Category of Topological Partial Actions
arxiv:2611.00363.summary: We present some theoretical aspects of the categories of global and partial group actions of topological groups on topological spaces, denoted by G-ActTop and G-pActTop, respectively. We construct topological partial actions on products and disjoint unions of topological spaces, and G-pinvariant subspaces. Furthermore, we provide an adequate definition of congruence (G-pcongruence), which enables the construction of quotient objects in the category of topological partial actions.

arxiv:2611.00379.title: A sharp plank theorem for cube annuli
arxiv:2611.00379.summary: We prove a conjecture of Andr\'as Bezdek on plank coverings of square annuli. A plank in a Euclidean space is the closed region between two distinct parallel hyperplanes, and its width is the distance between them. Let $Q$ be a unit square and let $H$ be a square of side length $1/2$ whose sides are parallel to those of $Q$.

arxiv:2611.00388.title: Online carpooling against an oblivious adversary
arxiv:2611.00388.summary: In the online carpooling problem, edges on $n$ vertices arrive one at a time and must be oriented immediately, so as to keep the difference between the indegree and the outdegree of every vertex small. We give a randomized online algorithm which bounds the largest absolute difference over the first $T$ edges by $O((\log T)^{1/3})$ with high probability on every input sequence fixed in advance. This proves a conjecture of Kulkarni, Reis and Rothvoss and matches the known worst case lower bound.

arxiv:2611.00435.title: Excedances and Deficiencies of Integer Partitions
arxiv:2611.00435.summary: The notion of a fixed point, applied by Blecher and Knopfmacher to integer partitions, can be considered as a permutation statistic. Here we apply two related permutation statistics, excedance and deficiency, to integer partitions. Using analytic and combinatorial techniques, we establish several generating functions and make connections to partition concepts including Dyson's crank statistic, overpartitions, and the Rogers--Ramanujan partitions.

arxiv:2611.00437.title: Two-point concentration for graph classes admitting sparse vertex deletion
arxiv:2611.00437.summary: For fixed $p\in(0,1)$, we prove that the maximum number of vertices in an induced subgraph of $G(n,p)$ from a given class is concentrated on two consecutive integers, unifying and extending several earlier results. We require that the class contain arbitrarily large graphs and that every sufficiently large $k$-vertex member have a vertex of degree $o(k)$ whose deletion leaves a graph in the same class. This condition holds for empty graphs, trees, forests, planar graphs, graphs of bounded maximum degree, degeneracy or treewidth, graphs excluding a fixed complete bipartite subgraph (including graphs containing no cycle of length four), and many other graph classes.

arxiv:2611.00445.title: Multivariate analogues of Ruijsenaars' hypergeometric function
arxiv:2611.00445.summary: We construct multivariate analogues of Ruijsenaars' hypergeometric function as nested products of overlap coefficients between eigenfunctions of twisted primitive elements in representations of the modular double of $U_q(\mathfrak{sl}_2)$. The construction is a hyperbolic counterpart of the nested multivariate Askey--Wilson polynomials and functions. Using iterated coproducts, we derive four systems of difference equations for which these multivariate functions are joint eigenfunctions.

arxiv:2611.00446.title: Analog and hybrid computing in the 21st century
arxiv:2611.00446.summary: Analog computers solve problems through physical representations of mathematical variables and relations, often using the dynamics of electronic circuits and their associated signals. Many analog computers directly represent nonlinear dynamical systems; they encode their solutions in the signals that they generate. Although most modern scientific computing relies on digital architectures with inherently discrete-valued representations and algorithmic approaches, the design constraints of such architectures increasingly limit both performance and energy efficiency.
arxiv:2611.00446.authors: Bernd Ulmann, Olivier Bournez, Corey J. Maley, Zhong Sun, Grace Li Zhang, Paul Manea, Michael D\"oll, Frank Delvigne, Alex J. H. Fedorec, Daniel Garza, Lucas Wetzel, Sara Obergassel, Pavol Pitonak, Christopher Jung, Daniel Thuerck, Mason A. Porter, Marcelo J. Rozenberg, Frederic Bergner, Bhaskar Choubey, Manyu Zhao, Ludovico Minati, Lucas B\"ottcher

arxiv:2611.00456.title: Spectral Fields and Unitary Descent: Local splitting, simultaneous norms, and transcendental obstructions
arxiv:2611.00456.summary: Spectral fields can recover matrix coefficients without standardizing the invariant Hermitian form. Over an algebraic subfield of $\mathbb{C}$ stable under nontrivial complex conjugation, we prove that every Zariski-dense subgroup in a normalized Hermitian model of dimension $m\ge4$ and signature $(m-1,1)$ at the fixed embedding contains a loxodromic element whose spectrum makes all diagonal coefficients norms. The element can be chosen so that every positive power is regular and generates the same splitting field.
arxiv:2611.00456.authors: Angel Cano, Nikolay Gusevskii, Marlon M. L\'opez-Flores

arxiv:2611.00457.title: Bilateral Christoffel-Geronimus-Uvarov formulas for mixed-type orthogonality on algebraic supports
arxiv:2611.00457.summary: Christoffel-type determinant formulas construct both normalized polynomial families and their reproducing kernel for mixed-type orthogonality in several variables after independent rational matrix transformations on the two arguments. The pairing may have a rectangular matrix of functionals, with separate degree bounds on each component, and may be supported on an algebraic variety. The reduced matrices are calculated from the original biorthogonal polynomials, rational moments, polynomial division and the masses left free by division; their nonvanishing determinants characterize existence and uniqueness.

arxiv:2611.00468.title: The symbolic pfaffian method I: A generalization of the Gallucio-Loebl-Tesler Theorem
arxiv:2611.00468.summary: The pfaffian number of a graph $G$, denoted by $\mathrm{pf}(G)$, is the minimum integer $k$ such that the generating function of perfect matchings of $G$ can be written as a linear combination of $k$ pfaffians of signed adjacency matrices. The Galluccio-Loebl-Tesler Theorem states that $\mathrm{pf}(G) \leq 4^g$, where $g$ is the orientable genus of $G$. We generalize this theorem by relating the pfaffian number of a graph to another graph parameter: the symbolic pfaffian number, denoted by $\mathrm{spf}(G)$.
arxiv:2611.00468.authors: Enrique Junchaya, Cl\'audio L. Lucchesi, Alberto A. A. Miranda

arxiv:2611.00485.title: On the Distribution of Prime Squares and Its Applications
arxiv:2611.00485.summary: We prove that, for every \(A>0\), all but \(O_A(X(\log X)^{-A})\) integers \(n<X\) satisfying \(n\equiv11\pmod{24}\) admit a representation \[ n=a^2+b^2+p^2, \] where \(p\) and \(a^2+b^2+1\) are prime and \((a,b)=1\). For ergodic averages along prime squares, we prove a universal divergence result for integrable functions, while establishing almost-everywhere convergence for near-integrable functions. We also quantify how the bounds used to establish convergence behave as one approaches integrability.

arxiv:2611.00493.title: Counterexamples to torsion-freeness in the $K$-theory of crystallographic group $C^*$-algebras
arxiv:2611.00493.summary: We give a negative answer to a question of S\'anchez Salda\~na--Vel\'asquez and L\"uck asking whether the topological K-theory of the reduced group C*-algebra of a split crystallographic group with finite cyclic holonomy is always torsion-free. For two explicit split crystallographic groups with translation subgroup of rank four and holonomy of order four, we compute the equivariant K-theory of the classifying space for proper actions and find nontrivial two-torsion. The equivariant universal coefficient theorem transfers this torsion to proper equivariant K-homology, and the Baum--Connes conjecture identifies the resulting groups with the topological K-theory of the corresponding reduced…

arxiv:2611.00517.title: Limits and Constants of OpenAI's Claimed ETH Refutation
arxiv:2611.00517.summary: A recent OpenAI preprint claims a deterministic algorithm that counts the satisfying assignments of a $k$-CNF formula in time $2^{O_k(n\log\log n/\sqrt{\log n})}$, and $2^{O(n/\sqrt{\log n})}$ at bounded clause density, which would refute the Exponential Time Hypothesis. The headline bound is proved by tensor contraction; the body develops an interpolation algorithm with the weaker exponent $n(\log\log n)^2/\sqrt{\log n}$. This note does four things.

arxiv:2611.00567.title: Sedentariness in Cayley graphs
arxiv:2611.00567.summary: Let $A$ be the adjacency matrix of a finite graph $\Gamma$. We say that vertex $u$ of $\Gamma$ is sedentary if for some constant $C>0$, $|\exp(itA)_{u,u}|\geq C$ for all $t\in\mathbb{R}$. In this paper, we investigate vertex sedentariness in walk-regular graphs with a focus on Cayley graphs and, more generally, vertex-transitive graphs.
arxiv:2611.00567.authors: Karen Meagher, Hermie Monterde, Tung T. Nguyen

arxiv:2611.00572.title: Total dominating sets and four-colorings of planar triangulations
arxiv:2611.00572.summary: In 2018, Goddard and Henning conjectured that every planar triangulation on at least four vertices has two disjoint total dominating sets. It was proved by Francis, Illickan, Jose, and Rajendraprasad in 2024. As a strengthening of this result, Goddard and Henning also conjectured that every planar triangulation with at least four vertices has a proper $4$-coloring with color classes $C_1,C_2,C_3,C_4$ such that $C_1\cup C_2$ and $C_3\cup C_4$ are total dominating sets.
arxiv:2611.00572.authors: Hyemin Kwon, Boram Park, Yoshio Sano

arxiv:2611.00591.title: A spectral Moore problem and the Yang-Koolen conjecture
arxiv:2611.00591.summary: We study the maximum order $v(k,\theta)$ of a connected $k$-regular graph whose second largest eigenvalue is at most $\theta$. For every real $\theta\geq1$, we prove that \[ T(\theta) =\limsup_{k\to\infty}\bigl(v(k,\theta)-2k\bigr) =2\left\lfloor1+\frac{\theta^2}{4}\right\rfloor. \] In particular, $T(\theta)>2\theta$ for every real $\theta\geq4$, disproving the Yang-Koolen conjecture.

arxiv:2611.00626.title: Lorentzian entropy, subgaussian matrix concentration, and sharp functional inequalities for all matroids
arxiv:2611.00626.summary: We prove complete entropy contraction for homogeneous Lorentzian laws and derive subgaussian matrix concentration and sharp functional inequalities for every matroid. Uniform retention of $\ell$ out of $r$ particles contracts matrix entropy by the optimal universal factor $\ell/r$, in every finite matrix dimension and positive field, including repeated labels. The matrix Laplace comparison retains matrix variance and arbitrary Hermitian offsets.

arxiv:2611.00629.title: Multivariate diagonal harmonics: character polynomials and proofs of two conjectures of Bergeron
arxiv:2611.00629.summary: We prove Bergeron's Hook-Components and Coefficient-Length conjectures for the Vandermonde polarization module and full diagonal harmonics in every rank and number of alphabets. Hook-label characters are elementary skewings of the alternating character, and the maximal Schur length in label $\mu$ is $n-\mu_1$. We compute character and dimension polynomials of diagonal coinvariants in every bosonic--fermionic superspace for $D\ge3$, $n\ge\max\{D,2D-6\}$, answering Church--Ellenberg--Farb's character and dimension questions.

arxiv:2611.00632.title: Completing the classification of Hopf superalgebras of dimension up to 10
arxiv:2611.00632.summary: We introduce a family of semisimple Hopf superalgebras obtained from abelian extensions. Using this family and bosonization, we complete the classification of Hopf superalgebras of dimension up to 10 over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero. We also determine the duals of the semisimple classes with nonzero odd part and give tables of the complete classification.
arxiv:2611.00632.authors: Taiki Shibata (Okayama University of Science), Kenichi Shimizu (Shibaura Institute of Technology), Ryota Wakao (Mathematical Society of Japan)

arxiv:2611.00663.title: $K_h$-Minor-Free Graphs Have Balanced Separators of Size $O(h\sqrt{n})$
arxiv:2611.00663.summary: We show that every $K_h$-minor-free graph with $n$ vertices has a balanced separator of size $O(h\sqrt{n})$ for any parameter $h \in \mathbb{N}$, resolving the conjecture posed by Alon, Seymour, and Thomas [AST90] in 1990. The proof is elementary, building on the combinatorial framework by Le [Le26]. A key new idea of the proof is the existence of a short hitting walk on vertex expanders: given $k$ large (not necessarily disjoint) subsets of vertices, there is a walk of length $O(k/\psi(G))$ hitting every subset, where $\psi(G)$ is the vertex expansion.
arxiv:2611.00663.authors: Jonathan Conroy, Hung Le, Jack Spalding-Jamieson

arxiv:2611.00679.title: Minimal quasisections of circle bundles
arxiv:2611.00679.summary: Let $E\xrightarrow{\pi}B$ be an oriented circle bundle over an oriented closed surface, and let $\mathcal E$ denote its Euler number. A \textit{quasisection} is a smooth surface $Q$, possibly with boundary, together with a generic smooth map $q:Q\to E$ such that $\pi\circ q(Q)=B$. The \textit{local formula} expresses the Euler number $\mathcal E$ of a bundle as a sum of the weights of the \textit{singular vertices} of a quasisection.
arxiv:2611.00679.authors: Ivan Kiselev, Gaiane Panina, Timur Shamazov

arxiv:2611.00693.title: On Certain Congruences for Partition $k$-Tuples with $5$-Cores
arxiv:2611.00693.summary: Let $A_{t,k}(n)$ denote the number of partition $k$-tuples of $n$ with $t$-cores. Using fifth-order modular equations and the Atkin $U_5$-operator, we prove the congruences $A_{5,125i+21}(25n+r)\equiv 0 \pmod{5^3}$ for $r\in\{9,14,19,24\}$, $A_{5,125i+41}(25n+r)\equiv 0 \pmod{5^3}$ for $r\in\{19,24\}$, and $A_{5,125i+111}(125n+r)\equiv 0 \pmod{5^4}$ for $r\in\{39,64,89,114\}$, which were stated by Tang \cite{tang2025iterative}.

arxiv:2611.00698.title: CLT for the Weight of the Minimum Spanning Arborescence on the Complete Directed Graph
arxiv:2611.00698.summary: The minimum spanning arborescence (MSA) with a fixed boundary, defined on weighted directed graphs, is the directed analogue of the minimum spanning tree (MST). The behaviour of the MSA has been of recent interest and is known to be quite different from that of its undirected counterpart. On the complete directed graph, and for edge weights given by i.i.d. random variables with a broad class of distributions, we prove a Central Limit Theorem for the weight of the MSA with appropriate scaling.
arxiv:2611.00698.authors: Swarnadeep Bagchi, Pablo de la Fuente, Kesav Krishnan

arxiv:2611.00702.title: Additive mappings of unweighted directed graphs preserving individual values of the cycle length
arxiv:2611.00702.summary: On the set of unweighted directed graphs on $n$ vertices, the union of graphs is defined as the union of their arc sets. A mapping of graphs is said to be additive if it preserves the union operation. In this paper, a characterization of additive mappings of unweighted directed graphs preserving a fixed value $k \geq 3$ of the cycle length is obtained.
arxiv:2611.00702.authors: Alexander Vlasov, Alexander Guterman, Svetlana Zhilina

arxiv:2611.00703.title: The e-Property for Quantum Markov Semigroups
arxiv:2611.00703.summary: Let $(\mathcal T_t)_{t\geqslant0}$ be a quantum Markov semigroup on a von Neumann algebra and let $\mathcal A$ be an invariant Feller $C^*$-algebra. We formulate the $e$-property on the full state space and show that its quantitative defect is equivalent, within an optimal factor two, to the Hausdorff measure of non-compactness of observable orbits. We develop Ces\`aro and Lip-norm criteria and a generalised Doeblin minorisation by a state-space contracting positive map, including finite-dimensional and measure-prepare factorisations.

arxiv:2611.00720.title: Sharp digirth bounds for C(k,k)-subdivisions in digraphs
arxiv:2611.00720.summary: For an integer $k\ge2$, let $C(k,k)$ denote the oriented cycle formed by two internally vertex-disjoint directed paths of length $k$ with the same initial and terminal vertices. We extend a problem of Picasarri-Arrieta and Rambaud [European J. Combin. 122 (2024)] on subdivisions of $C(k,k)$ to digraphs with several vertices of out-degree one.
arxiv:2611.00720.authors: Hao Zhang, Panpan Cheng, Jin Yan, Tong Zhou

arxiv:2611.00728.title: Partition statistics and universal mixed mock modular forms
arxiv:2611.00728.summary: In this note, we construct combinatorial statistics in terms of partitions, overpartitions, and two-color partitions and relate the corresponding generating functions to the universal mock theta functions. Our framework primarily builds on two $q$-series identities of Fine.

arxiv:2611.00742.title: Learning hidden-state dynamics from unpaired snapshots with lift-project SDEs
arxiv:2611.00742.summary: Many systems are observed only through unpaired snapshots, with population samples available at each time point but no correspondence between samples at different times. These snapshots determine the one-time distributions but leave the temporal coupling unspecified, requiring a modeling prior to connect successive times. We propose the lift-project stochastic differential equation (SDE), an autonomous SDE on the observed coordinate and a few hidden coordinates, trained only to match the snapshots.
arxiv:2611.00742.authors: Qi Wang, Uduak George, Gustaaf Jacobs

arxiv:2611.00772.title: A complete classification for n-species Lotka-Volterra stably dissipative systems based on a generalized AHU algorithm
arxiv:2611.00772.summary: This paper proposes a generalized AHU algorithm based on tree isomorphism theory and applies it to the complete classification of n-dimensional stably dissipative Lotka-Volterra systems.
arxiv:2611.00772.authors: Yajia Du, Zhengyi Lu, Jinya Xu, Ming Yang

arxiv:2611.00775.title: Fibre factorization and automorphisms of direct products of bipartite graphs
arxiv:2611.00775.summary: We determine the automorphism groups of direct products of finite connected twin-free bipartite graphs whose factors are different from $K_2$. The product is generally disconnected, so the problem requires both the automorphism groups of its components and a criterion for component isomorphism. We retain the order of the bipartition classes and use the fibre product over $K_2$.

arxiv:2611.00789.title: Congruent quotient matrix, nodal domain, and nodal count
arxiv:2611.00789.summary: We introduce the congruent quotient matrix along with its inequalities on inertia and demonstrate that these inequalities are the essence of the discrete nodal domain theorem, the bounds on nodal counts, and Fiedler's characterization on tree eigenvectors. Using these techniques, we also extend the existing bounds for the number of nodal domains and nodal counts.

arxiv:2611.00799.title: A result of continuous stability for generalized persistence diagrams
arxiv:2611.00799.summary: We study persistence modules obtained from the $A$-fundamental groupoids of finite graphs. Moreover, we verify the categorical properties needed to form generalized persistence diagrams, and describe a quotient that identifies equivalent groupoids. A normalized linear presheaf construction places these modules in an essentially small abelian category, where Patel's Continuity Theorem gives a $1$-Lipschitz estimate in erosion distance.
arxiv:2611.00799.authors: Yanga Bavuma, Martin Mijangos, Francesco G. Russo

arxiv:2611.00813.title: Stable compatibility for model categories
arxiv:2611.00813.summary: By introducing the notion of stable compatibility, we provide a framework in the model category theory which addresses the existence of a stable model structure on the category of modules over a monad. Exact version of such monads have been studied in the setting of triangulated categories, separately as separable monads a la Balmer in tensor triangular geometry and non-separable monads a la Dell'Ambrogio and Sanders in stable homotopy theory. By introducing stable compatibility, we explore their properties together and produce a non-separable monad in Algebraic geometry and more.

arxiv:2611.00816.title: SAWs, trails, kites, patterns
arxiv:2611.00816.summary: A self-avoiding walk (SAW) on a vertex-transitive graph $G$ is a path that visits no vertex more than once; a trail is a path that traverses no edge more than once. The number of $n$-step self-avoiding walks (respectively, trails) starting at a given vertex has order $\mu(G)^n$ (respectively, $\mu_{\text{T}}(G)^n$), where $\mu(G)$ is called the connective constant and $\mu_{\text{T}}(G)$ is the trail constant. It is immediate that $\mu=\mu_{\text{T}}$ if $G$ either has degree $3$ or less, or is a tree.

arxiv:2611.00817.title: Maxima of the Q-index: Forbidden an odd wheel
arxiv:2611.00817.summary: In 2013, Freitas, Nikiforov and Patuzzi (EJLA, 2013) proposed the problem of determining the maximum signless Laplacian spectral radius of an $n$-vertex $F$-free graph. Recently, Yuan, Zhai and Zhang (LAA, 2026) determined the maximum signless Laplacian spectral radius of graphs without wheels of sufficiently large order. In this paper, we consider the problem of forbidding a single wheel $W_{2k+1}=K_1\vee C_{2k}$.

arxiv:2611.00818.title: Well begun is half done: the computation of Eulerian paths
arxiv:2611.00818.summary: We characterize the uniform computational strength of finding one-way Eulerian paths in countable graphs. For both directed and undirected graphs, this problem is Weihrauch-equivalent to $\mathsf{lim}\times\mathsf{C}_{\mathbb{N}}'$, where $\mathsf{C}_{\mathbb{N}}'$ is the jump of closed choice on the natural numbers. This refines the proof-theoretical strength of the existence of an Eulerian path given by the reverse mathematics framework.

arxiv:2611.00825.title: Identities for generalized Bernoulli numbers from a Lie model of the 2-disk
arxiv:2611.00825.summary: We define generalized Bernoulli numbers as appropriate coefficients of the Baker--Campbell--Hausdorff (BCH) product formula, extending the classical sequence of rational numbers to a 2-dimensional setting. We give an identity involving these numbers and the classical Bernoulli numbers which is equivalent to the existence of a particular complete differential graded Lie algebra modelling a cell decomposition of the 2-disk and based on the Lawrence--Sullivan model of the interval. From this identity we derive explicit quadratic relations.
arxiv:2611.00825.authors: Urtzi Buijs, Jos\'e Manuel Moreno Fern\'andez

arxiv:2611.00830.title: On the nonvanishing of Floer lasagna modules
arxiv:2611.00830.summary: In this paper, we establish several nonvanishing results for Floer lasagna modules $\mathcal{FL}(W,K)$ for a smooth compact connected oriented $4$-manifold $W$ and a knot $K\subset \partial W$, via the evaluation maps to link Floer homology. We first establish a general criterion: if a certain Heegaard Floer cobordism map associated with a smooth $4$-manifold $W$ is nonzero, then $\mathcal{FL}(W,U)\neq 0$, where $U\subset \partial W$ is a local unknot. Applications include the nonvanishing of Floer lasagna modules for $\#^m\overline{\mathbb{C}P^2}$ and for knot traces $X_n(K)$ when $K$ is slice and $n$ is a non-positive integer.

arxiv:2611.00861.title: Regions of totally real arrangements of rational curves
arxiv:2611.00861.summary: We prove a plane-curve analogue of Zaslavsky's theorem for arrangements of real rational curves for which every complex singularity with more than one local branch is real and all of its branches are real. If at least one component has odd degree, the number of real regions equals the total rational Betti number of the complexified complement. We also give a formula for bounded affine regions which records the number of branches at infinity and the connected components of the real affine curve.

arxiv:2611.00864.title: From MHV Gravity Amplitudes and Hodges map to Pentad Varieties
arxiv:2611.00864.summary: We study some geometric aspects behind the Hodges matrix appearing in the context of scattering amplitudes for the $\mathcal N=8$ supergravity. Through a vector bundle construction, we show that the Hodges matrix gives rise to a canonical rational map from the two-step flag variety to symmetric matrices, called the $\textit{Hodges map}$. This construction allows to define the amplitude geometrically: its vanishing locus is a divisor - the $\textit{MHV gravity divisor}$.
arxiv:2611.00864.authors: Joris Koefler, Emanuele Ventura, Hongmiao Yu

arxiv:2611.00866.title: Laplacian Pair State Transfer on Edge Coronas
arxiv:2611.00866.summary: Let $G$ be a graph with edge set $E(G) = \{e_1, \ldots, e_m\}$, and let $\mathcal{H} = (H_1, \ldots, H_m)$ be an $m$-tuple of graphs. The edge corona $G\diamond\mathcal{H}$ is obtained from the disjoint union of $G,H_1,\ldots,H_m$ by joining both end vertices of each edge $e_j$ to every vertex of $H_j$ for $1\leq j\leq m$. In this paper, we investigate Laplacian perfect pair state transfer and Laplacian pretty good pair state transfer on edge coronas.

arxiv:2611.00872.title: Entry and position statistics in alternating permutations and Young tableaux
arxiv:2611.00872.summary: We study entry and position statistics in alternating permutations and standard Young tableaux using linear extensions and generating functions. For alternating permutations, we give explicit formulas for the mean and variance of the first entry and of the position of any fixed value. For standard Young tableaux, we express the sum of the lower-left entries as the number of tableaux of an associated skew shape.
arxiv:2611.00872.authors: Ran Pan, Dun Qiu, Weichen Wang, Xinhui Wang

arxiv:2611.00890.title: The covering radius of the first-order Reed-Muller code in nine variables is 242
arxiv:2611.00890.summary: We prove that the covering radius of the binary first-order Reed-Muller code RM(1,9) is exactly 242. Equivalently, the maximum nonlinearity of a Boolean function in nine variables is 242. Our proof combines a one-point rigidity theorem with a spectral and computational exclusion of the two larger candidate nonlinearities.

arxiv:2611.00893.title: On subgroup perfect codes and regular sets in generalized Cayley graphs
arxiv:2611.00893.summary: A subset $C$ of the vertex set of a graph $\Gamma$ is said to be an $(a,b)$-regular set if $C$ induces an $a$-regular subgraph and every vertex outside $C$ is adjacent to exactly $b$ vertices in $C$. A $(0,1)$-regular set is called a perfect code. Let $G$ be a finite group and let $\alpha\in\operatorname{Aut}(G)$ be such that $\alpha^2=\mathrm{id}$.

arxiv:2611.00912.title: Real zeros of $w$-polynomials: cycles and complete cutsets
arxiv:2611.00912.summary: For a simple graph $G$ with $n$ vertices, its $w$-polynomial is defined by \begin{align*} \sum_{q\geq0}P(G;q)x^q =\frac{w(G;x)}{(1-x)^{n+1}}, \end{align*} where $P(G;x)$ is the chromatic polynomial of $G$. This polynomial was introduced by Brenti in 1992. In this paper, we prove Conjecture~6.7 and the $w$-assertion of Conjecture~6.5 posed by Brenti, Royle and Wagner in 1994.

arxiv:2611.00916.title: Distances in the collinearity graphs of geometries related to simplex codes
arxiv:2611.00916.summary: Let $\cS(k,q)$ be the point-line geometry whose points and lines correspond to one-dimensional and two-dimensional subcodes of $q$-ary simplex codes of dimension $k$, respectively. We determine the complete distance relation and the diameter of its collinearity graph. For two points whose representing vectors have different sets of zero coordinates there is a common neighbour.

arxiv:2611.00925.title: A density theorem for non-standard irreducible cyclic codes
arxiv:2611.00925.summary: We prove a fixed-characteristic density form of the Berger-Charpin conjecture for non-degenerate irreducible cyclic codes: for each prime $p$, the lengths admitting such a non-standard code over some finite field of characteristic $p$ have natural density zero. Thus, for almost every length coprime to $p$, every such code over every finite field of characteristic $p$ has only the permutation automorphisms generated by the cyclic shift and the Frobenius map. The proof uses the Feng--Hollmann--Li--Xiang classification for non-standard irreducible cyclic codes, a normal form for the deriving constructions in that paper, and a theorem by Wiertelak on multiplicative orders, in the form recalled…
arxiv:2611.00925.authors: Tao Feng, Henk D. L. Hollmann, Weicong Li, Qing Xiang

arxiv:2611.00927.title: Latin cubes of order $4$ and $4320$-point quaternionic constructions in ${\mathbb R}^{16}$
arxiv:2611.00927.summary: Possibly the most enduring lower-bound record for kissing numbers in dimensions greater than $8$ (excluding $24$) is $$ \kappa_{16}\geq 4320. $$ This lower bound is attained by a shell of the famous Barnes--Wall lattice, which was discovered in 1959. Besides this configuration, at least one alternative $4320$-point kissing arrangement is currently known.

arxiv:2611.00950.title: The size and structure of graphs with a unique $k$-factor
arxiv:2611.00950.summary: For integers $n>k\ge1$ with $nk$ even, let $m(n,k)$ be the maximum size of a graph of order $n$ with a unique $k$-factor. In 1964, Hetyei and in 1984, Hendry [\emph{J. Combin.

arxiv:2611.00956.title: Strong complete immersions in graphs with independence number two
arxiv:2611.00956.summary: We prove that every graph $G$ with independence number at most two contains a strong immersion of $K_{\chi(G)}$. This strengthens Dahlke's theorem for weak immersions and establishes the Lescure--Meyniel conjecture for this class of graphs.

arxiv:2611.00961.title: Linear resolutions of powers of edge ideals of gap-free graphs with matching number four
arxiv:2611.00961.summary: For a finite simple gap-free graph $G$, let $B(G)$ denote the vertices $v$ for which $G-N_G[v]$ is not co-chordal, and put $C(G)=V(G)\setminus B(G)$. We prove a sufficient condition for all ordinary powers of its edge ideal to have linear resolutions from the second power onward: every induced anticycle of length at least five must contain an edge with both endpoints in $C(G)$. The argument uses variable generators of augmented colon ideals to eliminate anticycles that may persist in the ordinary quadratic colons.

arxiv:2611.00962.title: Markov-driven self-similar measures and non-homogeneous slicing
arxiv:2611.00962.summary: We introduce the concept of Markov-driven self-similar measures, a notion that simultaneously generalizes classical self-similar measures, self-conformal measures, dynamically driven self-similar measures and many random measures. This class is also closed under Cartesian products and linear projections. We initiate the study of this class of measures and investigate the $L^q$ dimension of Markov-driven self-similar measures under certain Diophantine conditions.

arxiv:2611.00966.title: Categorifications of noncrossing partitions of type B and affine type A
arxiv:2611.00966.summary: The lattice of wide subcategories of a tube is isomorphic to the lattice of noncrossing partitions of type B. We prove that through this categorification of noncrossing partitions, Kreweras complement is taking left perpendicular categories. With the help of this categorification and weighted projective lines, we obtain an inclusion from the lattice of noncrossing partitions of type B_n to a lattice of affine type A_n which preserves Kreweras complement.

arxiv:2611.00973.title: The Golden Quadruple: Four Reals Whose Differences Form a Geometric Progression, Rigidity of the Golden Ratio, and a Bohr Almost Periodic Cosine Sum
arxiv:2611.00973.summary: Let $\varphi=(1+\sqrt5)/2$. The four-point set $\{0,\varphi,\varphi^2,\varphi^3\}$ is classical: up to a dilation it consists of the two endpoints and the two crossing points on a side of the regular pentagram (Euclid, Elements XIII.8), and, by the identity $\varphi^2=\varphi+1$, its six pairwise differences are $1,\varphi,\varphi^2,\varphi^3$, with multiplicities $1,2,2,1$. We write this configuration as the golden quadruple $S=(F, F-a, F-b, F-a-b)$, where $u>0$, $a=\varphi u$, $b=\varphi^2u$ and $F>a+b$, and study its extremal and rigidity properties.

arxiv:2611.00977.title: There is only one transitive Anosov flow (in dimension 3, with orientable foliations, up to bicontact padding and Goodman surgeries)
arxiv:2611.00977.summary: We introduce a new surgical operation on Anosov flows, which we call bicontact padding surgery. The operation is defined using the machinery of strongly adapted bicontact structures, and involves inserting a 'padding' layer where one of the contact structures rotates many times around the Reeb flow of the other. We show that every skew Anosov flow with orientable stable and unstable foliations can be transformed into a finite cover of a geodesic flow using bicontact padding surgery and Goodman surgery.
arxiv:2611.00977.authors: Thomas Barthelm\'e, Federico Salmoiraghi, Chi Cheuk Tsang

arxiv:2611.00990.title: Galois Actions on Energy-Harmonic Functions
arxiv:2611.00990.summary: We study the action of $\text{Gal}(\overline{\mathbb{Q}}/\mathbb{Q})$ on the solutions to the discrete Dirichlet problem for a graph with fixed edge energies. We establish transitivity of the Galois action outside a thin set in the parameter space and demonstrate that the exceptional thin set may be Zariski dense, so the conclusion cannot in general be replaced by one that holds on a Zariski-open set. Identifying the parameter locus where the Galois action is transitive constrains the possibilities for linking combinatorial and arithmetic properties of the discrete energy-harmonic Laplace equations and other systems of the same form.

arxiv:2611.00993.title: A note on the product of holomorphic correspondences
arxiv:2611.00993.summary: In this article we study the concept of product of two holomorphic correspondences which was introduced in our previous work. Beginning with some basic results regarding the orbit space associated with the product correspondence, we then move on to a detailed analysis on the thermodynamic formalism of the same. Some of the results look at the behaviour of the product correspondence with respect to the individual correspondences.

arxiv:2611.00997.title: Canonical quantum curve I
arxiv:2611.00997.summary: We formulate a canonical quantum curve conjecture $\widehat H\Psi_*=0$ for spectral curves of positive genus. Here $\Psi_*$ is the non-perturbative wave function associated with Eynard--Orantin topological recursion, specialized at the \emph{canonical vanishing point}, a distinguished zero of the closed non-perturbative partition function. The operator $\widehat H$ is obtained by Weyl quantization of $H(x,y)$, with $\widehat x=x\cdot$ and $\widehat y=\hbar\partial_x$, together with quantum corrections to its coefficients.

arxiv:2611.01005.title: Positive expansiveness of operator semigroups: orbit growth and spectral criteria
arxiv:2611.01005.summary: This paper studies positive expansiveness and positive kinematic expansiveness for strongly continuous semigroups of bounded linear operators on complex Banach spaces. We prove that positive kinematic expansiveness is equivalent to the unboundedness of every nonzero orbit, while positive expansiveness additionally requires the generator to be bounded from below. We also show that continuous changes of time can be replaced by increasing homeomorphisms without changing positive expansiveness.

arxiv:2611.01008.title: On motivic multiplicativity of cyclic covers
arxiv:2611.01008.summary: Let $Y$ be a smooth projective complex variety of dimension $n$ with trivial Chow groups, and let $f: X\rightarrow Y$ be a cyclic cover of degree $d$ branched over a smooth ample divisor $D\in |dL|$. We show that a naturally constructed Chow--K\"unneth decomposition of $X$ is $m$-fold $mn$-multiplicative for each integer $m\geq2$ and that its stable motivic multiplicativity defect satisfies $\mathfrak{sd}(X)\leq 2dn$. If, in addition, each positive-codimension cycle class on $Y$ is supported on $D$, then a double cover admits motivic $0$-multiplicativity.

arxiv:2611.01012.title: Mutual-visibility colouring with two colours is NP-complete for every fixed diameter
arxiv:2611.01012.summary: A mutual-visibility set in a graph $G$ is a set $S$ of vertices such that any two vertices of $S$ are connected by a shortest path with no internal vertex in $S$, and the mutual-visibility chromatic number $\chi_\mu(G)$ is the minimum number of mutual-visibility sets needed to partition $V(G)$. Babu, Di Stefano and Lakshmanan showed that it is NP-complete to decide whether $\chi_\mu(G)\le 2$ for graphs of diameter four. We show that the problem remains NP-complete for graphs of diameter $d$, for every fixed $d\ge2$; diameter two is the smallest diameter for which the problem is non-trivial.

arxiv:2611.01014.title: On the Finite-Time Singularities of Point-Vortex Systems I: The Half-Plane
arxiv:2611.01014.summary: In this paper, the first in a series devoted to finite-time singularities of point-vortex systems in domains with boundaries, we establish the existence of finite-time interior collapse for three vortices in the upper half-plane $\mathbb{H}^+$. Our approach treats the boundary-induced interactions as a perturbation of the classical self-similar Gr\"{o}bli collapse in the full plane. Under suitable conditions on the vortex circulations and collapse profile, we prove the existence of a one-dimensional local strong stable manifold of the augmented rescaled system, which generates exact solutions in which three distinct vortices collapse simultaneously at any prescribed interior point…

arxiv:2611.01020.title: Spanning tree with bounded degree sum of two adjacent vertices
arxiv:2611.01020.summary: In this paper, we first give a sharp sufficient condition on degree sum for a connected graph to have a spanning tree whose maximum of degree sum of two adjacent vertices are bounded. These improve some previous results on the spanning tree with bounded maximum degree. Next, we also use our main result to study the generalized rainbow connection of graphs.

arxiv:2611.01032.title: Almost Gorenstein edge rings of bipartite graphs and their $h$-vectors
arxiv:2611.01032.summary: We characterize bipartite graphs whose edge rings are almost Gorenstein. Using this characterization, we recover known results for two families of graphs. In addition, we show that if the edge ring of a bipartite graph is almost Gorenstein and its $h$-polynomial has degree at least two, then the $h$-polynomial is palindromic except possibly for the linear and next-to-leading coefficients.

arxiv:2611.01060.title: A local limit theorem for singularity visits on translation surfaces
arxiv:2611.01060.summary: Let $(X,\omega)$ be a translation surface with at least one singularity. We investigate the distribution of the number of singularity encounters along prime closed geodesics on $X$. Writing $\ell(\gamma)$ for the geometric length of a closed geodesic and $m(\gamma)$ for the number of singularities it encounters, we establish a uniform counting local limit theorem for the values of $m(\gamma)$ sampled over $\ell(\gamma)<T$.

arxiv:2611.01064.title: Maximal input entropy for binary two-deletion and two-insertion channels
arxiv:2611.01064.summary: Under uniform transmission, we determine the received binary words that maximize input entropy for two-deletion and two-insertion channels. For two deletions the maximizers are exactly the two alternating words at every positive received length. For two insertions the same conclusion holds from received length five onward; we give all smaller cases and exact maximal values.
